default.q.n1-1-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 誰が必要な情報をもっているかをよく把握している人。 (A person who clearly knows who has the necessary information.)
default.q.n1-1-q45-45.explanation: The author clearly distinguishes between 「物知り」 (a person who knows about many things) and 「情報通」 (a person who is well-informed). 「情報通」 is defined as someone who knows where to go or whom to ask to obtain information (どこにいけば情報があるのかを知っている人). No matter how extensive a person's knowledge is, individual knowledge has limits. However, in every specific field, there are people who know it very well. A person who is 「情報通」 has many “drawers” of knowledge, knowing “who is knowledgeable about this issue” and “whom to ask to find out” (「この問題については、○○さんが詳しい」「この問題なら、○○さんに聞けばわかる」). Therefore, 「情報通」 is someone who knows exactly who has the information needed.
default.q.n1-1-q45-45.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the author explicitly states that 「物知り」 refers to a person who has broad knowledge (物事を広くよく知っている人), whereas even a highly knowledgeable person has limits to what they know.
default.q.n1-1-q45-45.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the passage does not discuss understanding what information is necessary for oneself; it emphasizes knowing where or from whom to find information.
default.q.n1-1-q45-45.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because it exactly matches the author's definition: 「情報通」 is someone who knows where to find information and has many connections of the kind expressed by 「○○さんに聞けばわかる」 (you can find out by asking Mr./Ms. ○○).
default.q.n1-1-q45-45.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the author only emphasizes having “drawers” of information that reveal who is knowledgeable in each field, not the ability to solve problems (問題解決ができる人).
default.q.n1-1-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 先につけていた水やお湯の温度によって、ぬるま湯の温度の感じ方が変わる。 (How the temperature of lukewarm water feels changes depending on the temperature of the water or hot water one was immersed in beforehand.)
default.q.n1-1-q46-46.explanation: The passage describes a famous experiment demonstrating the relativity of human temperature perception: when one hand is placed in cold water and the other in hot water, then both hands are placed in a basin of warm water (ぬるま湯), the hand removed from the cold water feels the warm water as "warm/hot," while the hand removed from the hot water feels it as "cold." This demonstrates that people do not perceive temperature absolutely; their perception of the warm water changes depending on the temperature of the water in which each hand was previously immersed.
default.q.n1-1-q46-46.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the experiment was not intended to prove that “soaking continuously causes one to lose the sensation of temperature”; it concerns the change in sensation when moving to a basin of warm water.
default.q.n1-1-q46-46.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the actual result is the opposite: after placing a hand in cold water and then putting it in warm water, the water feels warmer; after placing a hand in hot water first, the warm water feels colder.
default.q.n1-1-q46-46.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the two hands perceive the same basin of warm water differently (as warm or cold), not as water that feels colder than both previous environments.
default.q.n1-1-q46-46.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct because it accurately reflects the experiment's result: although the water in the same basin was warm, whether it felt hot or cold depended entirely on the temperature to which the hand had previously been exposed.
default.q.n1-1-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 安全や便利さも重要ではあるが、 自分で運転する楽しさは失いたくない。 (Safety and convenience are also important, but I do not want to lose the pleasure of driving myself).

The author acknowledges that automation offers major benefits in terms of safety and convenience (安全や便利さ); however, the author also emphasizes the entertainment value and enjoyment of driving oneself (自分で運転する楽しさ / 娯楽性). The author does not want the joy of driving to be lost for the sake of safety or convenience, and hopes that both values can coexist.

default.q.n1-1-q47-47.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the author does not claim that coexistence is difficult to achieve (実現は難しい); on the contrary, the author continues to hope for a solution that balances both elements.
default.q.n1-1-q47-47.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the author does not accept having to give up or resign oneself to losing entertainment in exchange for safety.

default.q.n1-1-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 同じ原作を翻訳しても、出来上がった翻訳が多様になりうる点。 (The point is that even when the same original work is translated, the finished translations can be highly diverse.)
default.q.n1-1-q48-48.explanation: The author compares translation to musical performance: the original work (原作) is likened to a musical score (楽譜), while the translator (翻訳家) is likened to a performer (演奏家). The same score can produce rich and varied performances when interpreted by different musicians with their own sensibilities and styles. Likewise, each translator creates a translation with distinctive qualities from the same original work, so the completed translations can be highly diverse (出来上がった翻訳が多様になりうる).
default.q.n1-1-q48-48.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the passage does not discuss the risk that the author's worldview may not be recreated despite closely following the original text.
default.q.n1-1-q48-48.why.1: (b) Option 2 is correct because it accurately expresses the author’s comparison: just as many musicians perform the same musical score differently, the same original work produces diverse translations depending on the translator.
default.q.n1-1-q48-48.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the passage does not mention that translators' personalities cause works by different authors to become alike.
default.q.n1-1-q48-48.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the worldview originates with the author of the original work. The translator does not independently create a new worldview, but offers diverse interpretations and translation styles. Choice 2 is the most accurate comparison with music.

default.q.n1-1-q50-50.explanation:
**Summary and analysis:**

- *Note for comparison:* The passage excerpt displayed above concerns self-driving cars (自動運転車) and the trade-off between safety/convenience and the enjoyment of driving, so it does not match Question 50 about lions.

**Translation of the question and choices:**
- **Question:** What did the author explain about the benefits of group living?
- **1.** The experience of lions during their prime can be used for both childcare and hunting.
- **2.** By dividing roles according to age, lions can carry out and balance both childcare and hunting at the same time.
- **3.** Dividing roles within the group becomes clear, reducing the burden on each individual lion.
- **4.** Young lions experience both childcare and hunting so that they can take on any role.

default.q.n1-1-q50-50.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the main point of the passage is not clarifying a role in order to reduce the burden (負担が減る) on each individual.
default.q.n1-1-q50-50.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the passage does not mention training young lions to experience everything so they can perform every role.

default.q.n1-1-q51-51.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct according to the original reading passage. default.q.n1-1-q51-51.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect. The author views slowing down or a lack of fluency as something positive, not as a problem caused by the interviewee that requires them to force themselves to speed up the conversation (自分のせいだと考えて自ら会話を進めようとする).

Young lions lack experience in caring for cubs and are more likely to fail, but they are agile and well suited to hunting; older lions, in contrast, have more experience and are better at caring for cubs. Through coordination and mutual compensation among its members, the pride successfully addresses the challenges of survival.
(Note: The four answer choices summarize philosophies of life and human psychology and do not match the original zoological passage. However, choice 4 is the closest inference from the detail that a weakness in child-rearing can be an advantage in hunting for young lions.)

default.q.n1-1-q54-54.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The market research results must be analyzed while taking into account that consumer reactions will gradually change over time.

- Summary of the main point: When a product’s packaging is redesigned, initial market surveys often receive mostly negative feedback because existing customers are attached to the familiar design. However, consumers gradually become accustomed to the new design over time (1–2 years). Therefore, when analyzing market survey figures, it is necessary to consider the time axis and changes in consumers’ feelings and reactions.
- Translation of the question: What does the author think about the results of the market survey?
- Translation of the answer choices:
  1. They should be used skillfully as the opinion of one segment of consumers.
  2. Positive opinions should be actively adopted and applied to product development.
  3. The analysis should take into account that consumers’ reactions will gradually change.
  4. Past results should be combined with the current results to understand changes in consumers’ preferences.
default.q.n1-1-q54-54.why.0: (a) Incorrect, because the passage clearly says that the opinion accounts for more than half (過半を占めます), not that it is merely the opinion of some consumers (一部の消費者の意見). The author also does not advise treating it as a minority opinion for strategic purposes.
default.q.n1-1-q54-54.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage does not mention actively incorporating supportive or positive opinions into product development.
default.q.n1-1-q54-54.why.2: (c) Correct because the final sentences provide evidence: 「最初は少し許せない部分があったとしても、 これが一年、二年経つと、新しいデザインも見慣れてくる。 したがってマーケティング調査の数字は、そういう時間軸も考えたうえで見る必要があります。」 Even if people initially find some aspects unacceptable, they become accustomed to a new design after one or two years. default.q.n1-1-q54-54.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage does not mention comparing results with those from the past to grasp changes in preferences. Instead, it emphasizes analyzing current survey results along a future timeline as users gradually become accustomed to the interface.
default.q.n1-1-q55-55.verdict: The correct answer is choice 3: Wait until the appropriate time naturally arrives to receive nature’s blessings and produce.
default.q.n1-1-q55-55.explanation:
**Main point:**
The author shares a lesson about the experience of "waiting" (待つ) while living in Ueno Village, Gunma. All forms of production and daily life connected with nature—such as growing crops, gathering mushrooms and wild vegetables, and cutting wood—require waiting for the right natural conditions before results can be achieved. Living in harmony with nature means patiently waiting for the appropriate time created by nature in order to receive its resources and blessings, because human will is not all-powerful and only works effectively when it follows the laws of nature.

**Translation of the question:**
The passage says that things "begin with waiting." What does the author mean that people should wait for?

**Translation of the choices:**
1. The time when nature recovers its abundance and becomes usable.
2. The right time to shape nature according to human wishes or convenience.
3. The time when nature reaches a suitable state for receiving its blessings.
4. The time when changes in nature can be sensed.
default.q.n1-1-q55-55.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the passage does not mention nature deteriorating and needing to “recover its richness” (豊かさを回復); it discusses the natural cycle of the seasons throughout the year.
default.q.n1-1-q55-55.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because it contradicts the passage's message. The author clearly states that "human will is not omnipotent" (人間の意志は万能ではない); people must adapt to nature rather than forcing nature to conform to their wishes or convenience (人間の都合に合わせる).
default.q.n1-1-q55-55.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because the passage gives several examples of waiting for the right natural time to farm, gather mushrooms, and collect wood, and concludes: "自然の力を借りようとすれば、自然がつくる、それに適したときがくるのを待たなければならない" (If we want to draw on nature's power, we must wait for the suitable time created by nature to arrive).
default.q.n1-1-q55-55.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the purpose of waiting is to carry out productive activities and harvest nature's bounty at the appropriate time, not merely to “feel the changes in nature” (自然の変化が感じられる).
default.q.n1-1-q56-56.verdict: The correct answer is 1: As in relationships with nature, people observe the other party's actions while seizing the right moment to influence them.
default.q.n1-1-q56-56.explanation:
**1. Summary of the passage's main point:**
People living in close contact with nature understand that human will is not all-powerful; people must adapt to nature and wait for the right moment. They apply this awareness to relationships as well: rather than imposing their own wishes, they observe and understand other people's actions, patiently wait for the appropriate timing, and then seize the opportunity to take initiative and build relationships.

*(Note: Question no. 56 corresponds to a reading passage about interpersonal conduct and the laws of nature by the author Takashi Uchiyama in a JLPT N1 exam.)*

**2. Translation of the question:**
According to the author, how did the villagers build relationships with one another?

**3. Translation of the choices:**
1. Like their relationship with nature, they observed the other person's actions while seizing the right moment to take action.
2. Like grasping changes in nature, they waited for the other person to change before taking action.
3. They understood the behavior of people who were easily influenced by nature and acted at the right moment.
4. Like waiting for changes in nature, they did not act hastily but waited for the other person to take action.
default.q.n1-1-q56-56.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage states: 「自然と結ばれ、ときを待ちながら働き暮らしてきた村の人たちは、人間関係のなかでも同じような感覚を育んだ。人間関係においても自分の一方的な意志は万能ではない。人々の動きを理解しながら、ちょうどよいタイミングがくるのを待って、そのときを逃さずに働きかけていく。それが村の人たちの人間関係のつくり方だった。」 This confirms that the villagers observed and understood the other person’s actions, waited for the right opportunity, and then acted at the appropriate moment (相手の行動を見ながら時機を捉えて働きかける).
default.q.n1-1-q56-56.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage refers to waiting for the right timing or opportunity (タイミング・時機), not waiting for the other person to change (相手の変化を待って).
default.q.n1-1-q56-56.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage does not discuss “people who are easily affected by nature” (自然の影響を受けやすい人々). It discusses applying insights from the relationship between humans and nature to relationships between people.
default.q.n1-1-q56-56.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The passage emphasizes taking proactive action when the opportunity arises (そのときを逃さずに働きかけていく), not passively waiting for action from the other party (相手からの働きかけを焦らずに待つ).

default.q.n1-1-q58-58.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the passage does not say that sharing the tension makes students think, “I can open up” (心を開いていいのだと思うようになる).
default.q.n1-1-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 1: not being satisfied with one’s existing experience, but continually taking the initiative to reinvent oneself.
default.q.n1-1-q59-59.explanation:
- Question translation: According to the author, what is important for people working in education?
- Answer choices:
  1. Not being satisfied with one’s existing experience, but proactively continuing to change oneself.
  2. Acquiring new knowledge and techniques oneself in order to maintain freshness.
  3. Making up for one’s own shortcomings while approaching students with enthusiasm.
  4. Not hiding one’s inexperience so that learners can more easily feel a sense of connection.
- Main idea: Once teachers have gained extensive experience, their lessons can become smooth but mechanical through habit, causing students to passively receive information. Therefore, the most essential quality for educators is never to become complacent or remain dependent on past experience, but to maintain a spirit of innovation and continually change themselves in each lesson.
default.q.n1-1-q59-59.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is correct because the author concludes: "経験に満足することなく、自ら変化し続けようとすること" (not being satisfied with one's experience, but continuing to change oneself) in order to keep teaching fresh and avoid falling into a stereotyped routine.
default.q.n1-1-q59-59.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the author emphasizes freshness in one’s mindset and teaching attitude, rather than limiting the point to “acquiring new knowledge and skills” (新しい知識や技術を身につけること).
default.q.n1-1-q59-59.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because “making up for a lack of experience while bringing enthusiasm” is merely a characteristic of new teachers, not the most important message the author conveys to educators in general.
default.q.n1-1-q59-59.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the author does not advise teachers to “not hide their inexperience” in order to help learners develop a sense of connection more easily.
default.q.n1-1-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is 4: Both Passage A and Passage B indicate that subordinates become passive because they believe that simply following their superior’s orders means the work is complete.
default.q.n1-1-q60-60.explanation:
Main point: When analyzing why subordinates or junior colleagues fall into a passive state of merely waiting for instructions (指示待ち), both passages A and B identify a common cause in their view of work: subordinates believe that their task is simply to do what their superiors tell them, rather than recognizing their responsibility to think proactively, seek solutions, or gain a deeper understanding of the work.

Question translation: What common reason do A and B give for why subordinates or junior colleagues end up waiting for instructions?

Answer choices:
1. They lack the knowledge and experience to know what they need to do.
2. They lack confidence and therefore cannot take the initiative to carry out the work themselves.
3. Their superiors always carefully tell them how to do the work.
4. They think that doing what their superiors tell them is the job.
default.q.n1-1-q60-60.why.0: (a) Incorrect. A lack of knowledge or experience is only a superficial possible reason raised for discussion, not the fundamental cause on which both passages A and B agree.
default.q.n1-1-q60-60.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Lack of confidence is not the common factor that both authors A and B identify as the main cause of the attitude of waiting for instructions.
default.q.n1-1-q60-60.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage does not state that careful guidance from superiors is a general cause of subordinates becoming passive and waiting for instructions.
default.q.n1-1-q60-60.why.3: (d) Correct. Both authors point out the same key issue: subordinates or junior members passively believe that “doing exactly what one’s superior says is one’s job.” They regard this as fulfilling their responsibility and therefore do not think proactively about solving problems.
default.q.n1-1-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is 3: Author A believes that subordinates should be helped to understand the purpose and overall picture of their work, while author B believes that, when a task is within their abilities, they should first be allowed to think it through themselves.
default.q.n1-1-q61-61.explanation:
Main point:
- Passage A: Focuses on broadening subordinates’ perspectives by helping them understand the “purpose of the work” (仕事の目的) and the “overall picture” (全体像), enabling them to understand the meaning of their work and act proactively.
- Passage B: Emphasizes giving subordinates authority and training them to think independently about tasks within their ability (一人で考えさせる), helping them shift from an instruction-following mindset to one of actively proposing solutions.

Question translation: What did authors A and B say about how to deal with subordinates or junior colleagues who are accustomed to waiting for instructions?

Answer choices:
1. Both A and B believe that they should be allowed to think of their own approach and then make a proposal.
2. Both A and B believe that the purpose of the work should be explained and that they should think together about what needs to be done.
3. A believes that they should be helped to understand the purpose and overall picture of the work, whereas B believes that tasks they are capable of doing should first be left for them to think through on their own.
4. A believes that they should be taught how the work relates to other tasks, whereas B believes that they should be given work whose procedure is already known and allowed to carry it out themselves.
default.q.n1-1-q61-61.why.0: (a) is incorrect. A method that requires thinking of an approach independently and then proposing it is the solution presented in B, not a shared viewpoint of both A and B.
default.q.n1-1-q61-61.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Communicating the purpose of the work is the central point made by Author A, and “thinking together about what needs to be done” is not something both authors propose.
default.q.n1-1-q61-61.why.2: (c) Correct. Passage A emphasizes helping employees understand the purpose of their work (仕事の目的) and the overall picture (全体像) so that they can guide their own actions. Passage B, meanwhile, argues that when subordinates are capable of handling a task themselves, managers should first let them think independently (まず一人で考えさせる) to develop their autonomy.
default.q.n1-1-q61-61.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Author B does not suggest assigning subordinates only tasks whose procedures are already known so they can work mechanically; instead, B emphasizes letting them think of their own solutions.
default.q.n1-1-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Data-driven optimization based on the past narrows people’s opportunities to encounter values and discoveries beyond their expectations.
default.q.n1-1-q62-62.explanation:
■ Main point: The author argues that the "optimal answer" produced by an algorithm is essentially a statistical probability based on past data. Although it is convenient, it confines people to the safety zone of their own past, depriving them of opportunities for intellectual creativity and renewal through unexpected encounters, detours, and random changes.
■ Question translation: Why does the author say that "we are merely being made to run comfortably in circles on a track laid along the extension of our past selves"?
■ Answer choices:
1. Because optimization based on past behavioral data narrows opportunities to encounter new values and discoveries beyond the scope of prediction.
2. Because optimization technology erases past failure data, creating the risk of unconsciously repeating old mistakes.
3. Because people become so accustomed to an efficient life that they lose the ability to apply the knowledge and experience they have accumulated in the past.
4. Because the choices provided by algorithms do not accurately reflect individual preferences, leaving people perpetually dissatisfied.
default.q.n1-1-q62-62.why.0: (a) CORRECT. Paragraph 2 states: 「アルゴリズムが提示する『最適解』とは、突き詰めれば過去のデータの蓄積から導き出された統計的蓋然性にすぎない。つまり、私たちは過去の自己の延長線上に敷かれたレールの上を、快適に周回させられているにすぎないのである。本来、人間の知的創造や価値観の更新は、予期せぬ他者との出会いや、一見して無意味に思える回り道、あるいは思い通りにいかない摩擦の中にこそ芽生える。失敗や非効率が排除された均質な世界では、偶然の揺らぎを通じて自己を再構築する契機が奪われてしまうのだ。」 (The optimal solution is based only on past data, depriving people of opportunities to renew their worldviews and create through unexpected fluctuations.)
default.q.n1-1-q62-62.why.1: (b) INCORRECT. The passage does not mention technology optimizing the “deletion of data about past failures” or causing people to “repeat the same mistakes unconsciously” (同じ過ちを無自覚に繰り返す).
default.q.n1-1-q62-62.why.2: (c) INCORRECT. The passage does not discuss people "losing the ability to apply for themselves the knowledge and experience they acquired in the past" (過去に培った知識や経験を自ら応用する能力が失われている).
default.q.n1-1-q62-62.why.3: (d) INCORRECT. Paragraphs 1 and 2 state that the algorithm accurately reflects data and preferences to create a convenient, comfortable environment (「快適に周回させられている」), which is completely contrary to the claim that it “does not accurately reflect preferences and leaves people constantly dissatisfied” (常に不満を抱えながら生活する).
default.q.n1-1-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The author views autonomous decision-making as facing uncertainty, making one's own choice based on one's values, and taking responsibility for that choice.
default.q.n1-1-q63-63.explanation:
■ Main point: According to paragraph 3, the author clearly distinguishes between passively choosing from options suggested by an algorithm and "making decisions autonomously." Autonomous decision-making requires people to confront uncertainty, think for themselves, weigh their judgment according to their own values, and be prepared to take responsibility for the consequences.
■ Translation of the question: How does the author view "autonomous decision-making (主体的な意思決定)"?
■ Translation of the choices:
1. Value objective data and the correct answer, narrow the choices, and minimize the risk of failure.
2. Carefully examine the options suggested by the system and choose the most efficient means without wasting resources.
3. Face uncertainty without guaranteed results, make one's own choice based on one's personal values, and take responsibility for the outcome.
4. Avoid being swayed by past experience or other people's opinions and quickly make a judgment based on one's own intuition.
default.q.n1-1-q63-63.why.0: (a) INCORRECT. This choice describes relying on objective data/answers to avoid risk (「客観的とされる正解に過度に依存する」). This is precisely an indication of declining autonomy, which the author criticizes, not a “subjective decision.”
default.q.n1-1-q63-63.why.1: (b) INCORRECT. Paragraph 3 states that choosing from the options presented by the system is merely "passive consumption" (「提示された選択肢の中から選ぶこと[...]は受動的な消費にすぎず」). The author also does not equate autonomy with "choosing the most effective means without waste."
default.q.n1-1-q63-63.why.2: (c) CORRECT. Paragraph 3 states: 「アルゴリズムが提供する客観的とされる正解に過度に依存するにつれ、私たちは不確実性と向き合い、自らの頭で判断を下すという労苦を忌避するようになる。提示された選択肢の中から選ぶことと、自らの価値基準に基づいて選び取ることは決定的に異なる。前者は受動的な消費にすぎず、そこには自己決定に伴う責任の引き受けが存在しない。」 (Active decision-making requires confronting uncertainty, thinking and judging according to one's own values, and taking responsibility).
default.q.n1-1-q63-63.why.3: (d) INCORRECT. The passage does not mention “making quick judgments based on one’s intuition” (自らの直感に従って迅速に判断を下す). Instead, the author emphasizes grappling with uncertainty and thinking things through independently.
default.q.n1-1-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 2: In an optimized society, people must accept randomness and the process of struggle and friction rather than obsessively pursuing efficiency, in order to protect genuine autonomy.
default.q.n1-1-q64-64.explanation:
■ Main point: The entire essay criticizes the tendency to absolutize efficiency and optimize everything to the point of undermining human autonomy and capacity for innovation. In the conclusion, Section 4, the author asserts the essential point: People need the courage to accept unpredictable randomness, preserve space for "inefficiency," and experience the process of struggling and wrestling with uncertainty in order to maintain genuine autonomy.
■ Translation of the question: In a modern society where optimization is advancing rapidly, what does the author most strongly assert or advocate?
■ Translation of the choices:
1. The development of artificial intelligence should be restricted immediately, and we should return to a former way of life that does not depend on algorithms.
2. Rather than pursuing efficiency and convenience alone, we should protect the autonomy inherent in human beings by accepting unpredictable randomness and the process of struggling and wrestling with uncertainty.
3. Optimization systems should be developed to an even higher level to eliminate all friction and hesitation from human decision-making.
4. While accepting objectively optimal answers, we should urgently implement measures to protect privacy data, such as personal behavioral histories.
default.q.n1-1-q64-64.why.0: (a) INCORRECT. At the beginning of paragraph 4, the author clearly states: 「技術の進展そのものを否定する必要はない」 (There is no need to deny technological advancement itself). Therefore, the author is not calling for restrictions on AI or a return to an earlier way of life.
default.q.n1-1-q64-64.why.1: (b) CORRECT. Paragraph 4 states: 「すべてを計算可能で効率的なシステムへと還元しようとする風潮に対し、私たちはあえて『非効率』や『保留』の領域を保持すべきではないか。予測不可能な偶発性を受け入れ、葛藤のプロセスを引き受けることこそが、最適化が進む現代において、人間が真の自律性を保ち続けるための不可欠な条件なのである。」
default.q.n1-1-q64-64.why.2: (c) INCORRECT. This completely contradicts the author’s argument. The author does not want to eliminate hesitation or friction entirely; rather, friction, detours, and uncertainty are precisely where creativity and autonomy emerge.
default.q.n1-1-q64-64.why.3: (d) INCORRECT. The passage does not discuss any measures or policies for protecting privacy data (プライバシーデータを保護する対策).
default.q.n1-1-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 2: The author criticizes relying solely on technical solutions because this preserves the idea that nature is an object to be managed for human benefit and refuses to give up convenience and unlimited consumption, so it does not address the root of the environmental problem.
default.q.n1-1-q65-65.explanation:
- Summary of the main point: The author points out that relying solely on technological solutions is essentially a continuation of an anthropocentric mindset that treats nature as a resource or tool to be calculated and managed. As long as people refuse to give up the pursuit of convenience and unlimited consumption, technological progress merely postpones the problem on the surface or shifts the burden elsewhere; it cannot fundamentally resolve the environmental crisis.
- Translation of the question: Why does the author criticize "an attitude that relies solely on technical solutions"?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. Because scientific and technological innovation requires enormous costs, making simultaneous economic growth impossible in practice.
  2. Because it maintains an anthropocentric view that treats nature as an object to be managed and does not stop pursuing consumption and convenience, so it cannot fundamentally solve the problem.
  3. Because new technologies such as renewable energy have lower CO2 recovery efficiency than traditional environmental technologies.
  4. Because trying to maintain the current standard of living hinders investment in technological development.
default.q.n1-1-q65-65.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage does not mention costly scientific and technological innovation or claim that economic growth is impossible in reality.
default.q.n1-1-q65-65.why.1: (b) Correct. Evidence from paragraph 2:「技術的解決策にのみ依存する態度は、自然を人間の経済活動に従属する「利用可能な資源」や「炭素の吸収器」として数値化し、効率的に管理しようとする人間中心主義的な発想を無批判に温存させてしまう。どれほど技術が高度化を遂げようとも、地球生態系の有限な受容能力を度外視して際限なき消費と利便性を追求し続ける限り、環境危機の根本的な克服には至らない。」 (An exclusive reliance on technological solutions inadvertently preserves an anthropocentric mindset that treats nature as “available resources” or “carbon sinks” subordinate to human economic activity and attempts to quantify and manage it efficiently. No matter how advanced technology becomes, as long as people continue pursuing unlimited consumption and convenience while disregarding the finite capacity of Earth's ecosystems, the environmental crisis cannot be fundamentally overcome.)
default.q.n1-1-q65-65.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage does not compare the CO2 recovery efficiency of new technology using renewable energy with that of conventional technology.
default.q.n1-1-q65-65.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The passage does not mention that maintaining the current standard of living would restrict investment capital for technological development.
default.q.n1-1-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The author asserts that we cannot rely solely on technological solutions; most importantly, people must recognize nature's intrinsic value and carry out a profound transformation in their values by restraining their greed and pursuit of personal convenience.
default.q.n1-1-q66-66.explanation:
- Main point: The essay's focus is in the final paragraph: The author emphasizes that the essential task is not to use technology to patch things up and maintain the current consumer lifestyle, but to undertake an ethical practice: recognizing nature as a valuable fellow participant in our shared existence, voluntarily restraining the desire for convenience, and accepting the painful transformation of our values.
- Question translation: What does the author advocate most strongly in this passage?
- Answer choices:
  1. We should pursue economic growth that takes Earth's ecological capacity into account while maintaining living standards through technological innovation.
  2. To promote the protection of nature, we should completely stop developing technology and return to a simple lifestyle of the past.
  3. We should strengthen international environmental protection standards so that people can use and manage nature effectively as an object.
  4. We should do more than rely on technological measures; we should transform our values by recognizing nature's value and restraining our own desires and pursuit of convenience.
default.q.n1-1-q66-66.why.0: (a) Incorrect. This describes the concept of “Green Growth,” which the author identifies as having blind spots and being only a temporary solution in passages 1 and 2. It is not the policy the author advocates.
default.q.n1-1-q66-66.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage does not call for “completely ending technological development” or “returning to the simple lifestyle of the past.”
default.q.n1-1-q66-66.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The author rejects the idea of treating nature as an object to be managed or used, and therefore does not advocate strengthening standards for managing nature as an object.
default.q.n1-1-q66-66.why.3: (d) Correct. Paragraph 3 states: 「真に求められているのは、既存の生活様式を維持するための技術的な辻褄合わせではない。自然を単なる客体ではなく固有の価値を有する共生者として再定義し、自らの欲望や便利さへの依存を自発的に抑制するという倫理的実践である。私たちは、社会の価値基準そのものを抜本的に転換するという、痛みを伴う自己変革から目を逸らしてはならないのである。」 (What is truly required is not a technical patch to maintain existing lifestyles, but an ethical practice of redefining nature as a fellow being with intrinsic value, voluntarily restraining dependence on our desires and conveniences, and fundamentally transforming society’s standards of value.)
default.q.n1-1-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 2. ぜっきょう.
default.q.n1-1-q1-1.explanation:
Meaning: When player Sato scored, the spectators cheered and shouted enthusiastically.
Kanji note: 絶叫 (ぜっきょう): to scream, shriek, or shout loudly.
Example: 絶叫マシンに乗って大声をあげた。(I shouted loudly while riding a thrill ride.)
default.q.n1-1-q1-1.why.0: (a) せっきょう: Incorrect on-reading of 「絶」. The correct on-reading is「ぜつ／ぜっ」, not「せつ／せっ」in this word.
default.q.n1-1-q1-1.why.1: (b) ぜっきょう: Correct. 「絶」 is read as 「ぜっ」 and 「叫」 as 「きょう」, forming 「ぜっきょう」.
default.q.n1-1-q1-1.why.2: (c) ぜっきゅう: Incorrect on-reading of the kanji 「叫」. The correct on-reading is 「きょう」, not 「きゅう」.
default.q.n1-1-q1-1.why.3: (d) せっきゅう: The readings of both kanji are incorrect.
default.q.n1-1-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 1. はいご.
default.q.n1-1-q2-2.explanation:
Meaning: I heard a sound coming from behind me.
Kanji meaning: 背後 (literally, “back + behind”) - behind, at the rear (used both for a physical location and figuratively for a cause or someone behind an event).
Example: 事件の背後には大きな組織が関わっている。(A major organization is involved behind the incident.)
default.q.n1-1-q2-2.why.0: (a) はいご: Correct.「背」is read「はい」and「後」is read「ご」, forming「はいご」.
default.q.n1-1-q2-2.why.1: (b) はいこう: Incorrect reading of 後; in this word it is read「ご」, not「こう」.
default.q.n1-1-q2-2.why.2: (c) せいご: Incorrect reading of 背; in this word it is read「はい」, not「せい」.
default.q.n1-1-q2-2.why.3: (d) せいこう: Incorrect reading for both kanji (せいこう commonly corresponds to 成功 or 精巧, among others).
default.q.n1-1-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is 1. ほうふ.
default.q.n1-1-q3-3.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: Expressing one's ambitions or plans for the future.
Kanji: 抱負 means ambitions, aspirations, or hopes held in one's heart.
Note: Do not confuse it with the homophone 豊富 (ほうふ), meaning abundant or plentiful.
Example: 新年の抱負を語り合う。(Share New Year's goals and aspirations with one another.)
default.q.n1-1-q3-3.why.0: (a) ほうふ: Correct. 抱 has the long-vowel reading「ほう」, while 負 is read「ふ」without voicing.
default.q.n1-1-q3-3.why.1: (b) ほうぶ: The sound of 「負」 is incorrect (it is read 「ふ」 and does not become 「ぶ」).
default.q.n1-1-q3-3.why.2: (c) ほふ: Incorrect because the long vowel in 「抱」 is missing (the on-reading is 「ほう」, not 「ほ」).
default.q.n1-1-q3-3.why.3: (d) ほぶ: Incorrect both because the long vowel in 抱 is missing and because 負 has been incorrectly voiced.
default.q.n1-1-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 3. あなどって.
default.q.n1-1-q4-4.explanation:
Meaning: You must not look down on or underestimate other people.
Kanji reading: 侮 means to despise or look down on someone (as in 侮蔑 - ぶべつ: contempt, scorn).
Example: 相手の実力を侮ると痛い目に遭う。(If you underestimate your opponent’s abilities, you will suffer the consequences.)
default.q.n1-1-q4-4.why.0: (a) からかって is the reading of the verb からかう (揶揄う: tease, mock).
default.q.n1-1-q4-4.why.1: (b) ののしって is the reading of the verb ののしる (罵る), meaning to curse or insult.
default.q.n1-1-q4-4.why.2: (c) あなどって: Correct.「侮」has the kun-reading あなどる (to despise or look down on), whose te-form is あなどって.
default.q.n1-1-q4-4.why.3: (d) うらぎって: This is the reading of the verb うらぎる (裏切る: to betray).
default.q.n1-1-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is 4. すじみち.
default.q.n1-1-q5-5.explanation:
Meaning: I explained it clearly and logically so that the other person could understand.
Vocabulary: 筋道 (logical reasoning, a coherent sequence).
Fixed expression: 筋道を立てる (すじみちをたてる) = to reason or explain something logically, coherently, and with clear grounds.
Example: 筋道の通った議論をする。(To present a well-reasoned argument.)
default.q.n1-1-q5-5.why.0: (a) きんどう: Incorrect because it combines the on-readings 「きん」 + 「どう」, whereas this word is formed entirely with kun-readings.
default.q.n1-1-q5-5.why.1: (b) すじどう: Incorrect reading of 「道」; it uses the on-reading 「どう」 instead of the kun-reading 「みち」.
default.q.n1-1-q5-5.why.2: (c) きんみち: Incorrect reading of 「筋」; it uses the on-reading 「きん」 instead of the kun-reading 「すじ」.
default.q.n1-1-q5-5.why.3: (d) すじみち: Correct. Both kanji use their kun-readings: 「筋」(すじ) +「道」(みち) =「すじみち」.
default.q.n1-1-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 3. ほんぽう.
default.q.n1-1-q6-6.explanation:
Sentence meaning: The main character of that novel has a free-spirited personality.
Kanji: 奔放 (HŌHŌ — uninhibited, free-spirited, unconstrained by rules).
Common expression: 自由奔放 (じゆうほんぽう — free-spirited, carefree).
Example: 彼女は自由奔放に生きている。(She lives a free-spirited life.)
default.q.n1-1-q6-6.why.0: (a) はんぽう: Incorrect reading of 「奔」; it is read 「ほん」, not 「はん」.
default.q.n1-1-q6-6.why.1: (b) ぽんぽう: The reading of 「奔」 is incorrect.
default.q.n1-1-q6-6.why.2: (c) ほんぽう: Correct. 「奔」is read「ほん」, and 「放」becomes「ぽう」after ん, giving「ほんぽう」.
default.q.n1-1-q6-6.why.3: (d) ばんぽう: Incorrect reading of「奔」(mistakenly read as「ばん」).
default.q.n1-1-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 適応 (adaptation, adjustment).
default.q.n1-1-q7-7.explanation:
Meaning: That organism has the ability to adapt to harsh environments.
- Kanji: 適応 (adaptation, adapting to circumstances).
- Example: 新しい職場環境に早く適応したい。(I want to adapt quickly to my new work environment.)
default.q.n1-1-q7-7.why.0: (a) Correct: 適応 means the ability of an organism to change and adapt to fit its environment (環境に適応する).
default.q.n1-1-q7-7.why.1: (b) Incorrect: 合致 means to coincide or match, and is commonly used with conditions or opinions, as in 条件に合致する and 意見の一致/合致.

default.q.n1-1-q26-26.explanation:
Meaning: "There's a lottery ticket stand over there. Want to buy one?" - "You won't win anyway. Buying one would just be a waste of money."
- Pattern: 「V-る + だけ + 無駄 (だ)」: to be nothing but a waste / pointless (doing something despite knowing in advance that it will not produce a result).
- Kanji and vocabulary: 宝くじ (lottery), 無駄 (waste, pointless).
- Example: そんな人に忠告しても、時間の無駄／言うだけ無駄だよ。(Even advising someone like that would just waste your time / it would be pointless to say anything.)
default.q.n1-1-q26-26.why.0: (a) 1. より: Indicates comparison or a starting point/choice (Vるより...), and does not combine with 無駄 in this structure.
default.q.n1-1-q26-26.why.1: (b) 2. のみ: means “only” in formal written language; it is not used in the fixed expression 「〜だけ無駄」 meaning “it is a waste.”
default.q.n1-1-q26-26.why.2: (c) 3. には: is commonly used to indicate a purpose or evaluate a condition (Vるには...), but it does not form 「買うには無駄」 in this context.
default.q.n1-1-q26-26.why.3: (d) 4. だけ: Correct. The structure 「V-る + だけ + 無駄/損」means “only waste one's effort,” “only waste money,” or “it is useless even if one does it.”
default.q.n1-1-q27-27.verdict: The correct answer is 3. を受けて: it indicates accepting, stemming from, or responding to a particular trend or event in order to develop further.
default.q.n1-1-q27-27.explanation:
Meaning: Driven by growing health awareness in recent years, health foods and dietary supplements are growing rapidly.
- Structure: 「N + を受けて」: in response to, based on, or prompted by (a result, situation, reaction, etc.), leading to a subsequent action.
- Sino-Japanese meanings: 意識 (awareness), 高まり (increase, rise), 急成長 (rapid growth).
- Example: 市民の要望を受けて、新しい図書館が建設された。(In response to residents' requests, a new library was built.)
default.q.n1-1-q27-27.why.0: (a) 1. に次いで: means “following/next after...” and indicates rank or degree, so it does not fit the meaning of the sentence.
default.q.n1-1-q27-27.why.1: (b) 2. にわたって means “throughout” or “over the entire span of” a period, area, or group; it is not used to indicate a cause or motivating background.
default.q.n1-1-q27-27.why.2: (c) 3. を受けて: Correct. The grammar 「N + を受けて」 means “in response to, upon receiving, or as a result of...” and describes a subsequent action or change.
default.q.n1-1-q27-27.why.3: (d) 4. をめぐって means “concerning, revolving around,” often in disputes, discussions, or conflicts; it does not fit the context of market growth.
default.q.n1-1-q28-28.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 帰るなり: The pattern 「V-る + なり」 describes one action being followed immediately by another, and is generally used with a third-person subject.
default.q.n1-1-q28-28.explanation:
Sentence meaning: My son must have been exhausted from soccer practice; as soon as he got home, he went straight to sleep without eating or drinking anything.
- Structure: 「V-る + なり」: just as soon as...; immediately after... (the subject is usually a third person, and the following action occurs unexpectedly and without intention, commands, or requests).
- Kanji readings: 練習 (practice), 食事 (meal).
- Example: 彼は部屋に入るなり、倒れ込んでしまった。(As soon as he entered the room, he collapsed.)
default.q.n1-1-q28-28.why.0: (a) 1. 帰り次第: The structure 「V-masu + 次第」means “as soon as...,” and is used for a future plan or intention. The following clause cannot describe an action that already occurred in the past.
default.q.n1-1-q28-28.why.1: (b) 2. 帰るなり: Grammatically correct. 「V-る + なり」expresses that immediately after one action occurs, another person suddenly performs a second action.
default.q.n1-1-q28-28.why.2: (c) 3. 帰ったなり: The pattern 「V-た + なり」means “to remain in the state resulting from an action” (with no change afterward); it is not used to connect two immediately consecutive actions.
default.q.n1-1-q28-28.why.3: (d) 4. 帰るとなれば: Means “if one were to leave” or “if it were indeed a matter of leaving,” expressing a hypothetical condition, which does not fit the context of recounting an event.
default.q.n1-1-q29-29.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 恐れがある以上: a combination of the grammar expressing a feared risk, 「〜恐れがある」, and the structure indicating an inevitable reason, 「〜以上（は）」 (“now that..., one must...”).
default.q.n1-1-q29-29.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: Setting a different password for each website is troublesome, but once there is a risk of unauthorized access by a third party, it has to be accepted.
- Pattern: 「V/A/N plain form + 恐れがある」: there is a risk that something negative may happen; 「〜以上（は）」: now that..., one must / has no choice but to....
- Vocabulary: 設定 (setting), 面倒 (troublesome), 第三者 (third party), 不正 (unauthorized/illegal), 恐れ (risk, concern).
- Example: 台風が上陸する恐れがある以上、イベントは中止せざるを得ない。(Since there is a risk that the typhoon will make landfall, the event has to be canceled.)
default.q.n1-1-q29-29.why.0: (a) 1. しかない以上: 「〜しかない」 means “there is no choice but to.” Combined with unauthorized access, it does not produce a logical meaning.
default.q.n1-1-q29-29.why.1: (b) 2. しかない反面: means “there is no choice but to..., but on the other hand...” and does not go with the conclusion “it is unavoidable” (やむを得ない).
default.q.n1-1-q29-29.why.2: (c) 3. 恐れがある以上: Grammatically correct: 「〜恐れがある」 means “there is a risk that” or “there is concern that,” and 「〜以上」 means “once ...” or “now that ...”.
default.q.n1-1-q29-29.why.3: (d) 4. 恐れがある反面: 「〜反面」 expresses two contrasting sides of the same matter; it does not lead to the inevitable result やむを得ない in the following clause.
default.q.n1-1-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 見きれないほどの: 「V-masu + きれない」 means “unable to finish or do completely,” and 「〜ほど」 means “to the extent that / so many that”; together they modify the noun 作品.
default.q.n1-1-q30-30.explanation:
Meaning: The art museum I visited yesterday was displaying so many works that it was impossible to see them all in one day.
- Pattern: 「V-masu + きれない」: cannot finish doing something; cannot do something completely. 「〜ほど(のN)」: to such an extent that; indicating a high degree.
- Kanji compounds: 美術館 (art museum), 作品 (work; creation), 展示 (display; exhibition).
- Example: 食べきれないほどのごちそうがテーブルに並んでいた。(The table was covered with so much delicious food that I could not eat it all.)
default.q.n1-1-q30-30.why.0: (a) 1. 見きれないほどの: Grammatically correct: 「V-masu + きれない」 (cannot finish viewing) + 「ほどの + N」 (so many that...).
default.q.n1-1-q30-30.why.1: (b) 2. 見ずにはいられないほどの: 「〜ずにはいられない」 means “cannot resist watching” or “cannot help watching,” which does not fit with the adverb “in one day” (一日では).
default.q.n1-1-q30-30.why.2: (c) 3. 見きれないといった: 「といった」introduces examples in a list (“things such as...”); it is not used to modify the degree or quantity of 作品.
default.q.n1-1-q30-30.why.3: (d) 4. 見ずにはいられないといった: Incorrect both semantically and in how it combines in this context.
default.q.n1-1-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 押さえたいところだが: the pattern 「V-たい + ところだが」 expresses a strong desire to do something, but in reality the person does something else or faces an obstacle.
default.q.n1-1-q31-31.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Since I am about to move, I really want to minimize unnecessary expenses, but I decided to go on a skiing trip after my friends invited me.

- Pattern: 「V-たいところだが / ところけれど」: I would really like to do V, but... (expressing regret and the contrast between one's desire and actual actions).
- Kanji-based vocabulary: 引っ越し (moving house), 控える (be about to face, prepare for), 出費 (expenses), 抑える/押さえる (restrain, limit).
- Example: すぐにでもお伺いしたいところですが、あいにく都合がつきません。(I would very much like to visit right away, but unfortunately I cannot arrange the time.)
default.q.n1-1-q31-31.why.0: (a) 1. 押さえたら抑えたで: The pattern 「V-たらV-たで」 means that whether one does something or not, another inconvenience or problem will arise; it does not fit the meaning of the sentence.
default.q.n1-1-q31-31.why.1: (b) 2. 抑えられるものなら: The structure 「V-potential + ものなら」 means “if it were possible to do V,” usually referring to something difficult to accomplish, so it does not fit the following clause.
default.q.n1-1-q31-31.why.2: (c) 3. 抑えるには抑えずに: Incorrect grammar. The correct pattern is VるにはVたが, meaning “although ...” or “it is true that ..., but ...”.
default.q.n1-1-q31-31.why.3: (d) 4. 押さえたいところだが: Grammatically correct. 「V-たいところだが」means “I would really like to restrain my spending, but...” (in reality, the speaker decides to travel).
default.q.n1-1-q32-32.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 解いてみせた: The structure 「V-て + みせる」 means performing a difficult action impressively in front of others to demonstrate one’s ability.
default.q.n1-1-q32-32.explanation:
Sentence meaning: It is astonishing that the elementary school student solved a high-school mathematics problem smoothly in front of everyone.
- Pattern: 「V-てみせる」: to do something impressively to show one's ability.
- Kanji readings: 驚く (to be surprised), 小学生 (elementary school student), 数学 (mathematics), 解く (to solve).
- Mimetic word: すらすら (smoothly, fluently, with ease).
- Example: 彼は猛練習の末、見事に難曲を弾いてみせた。(After intense practice, he performed a difficult piece brilliantly for everyone.)
default.q.n1-1-q32-32.why.0: (a) 1. 解けるとは: This is commonly used at the end of an exclamatory sentence expressing surprise, as in 「〜とは驚きだ」. It does not function as a complete predicate in a declarative sentence that already begins with 驚いたことに.
default.q.n1-1-q32-32.why.1: (b) 2. 解けるものなら: expresses an unlikely hypothetical condition (“if it could be solved...”), so it is unsuitable for an event that has already occurred.
default.q.n1-1-q32-32.why.2: (c) 3. 解いたまでだ: The structure 「V-たまでだ」means “I merely did that, and nothing more,” used by the speaker when explaining or speaking humbly. It is not used for another person.
default.q.n1-1-q32-32.why.3: (d) 4. 解いてみせた: Grammatically correct. 「V-てみせる」expresses performing something impressively or skillfully to show others; here, an elementary school student solves high-school mathematics with remarkable speed.
default.q.n1-1-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 1. という: It indicates hearsay or a transmitted account (“it is said that / according to tradition”) and corresponds to the opening source-of-information phrase 「〜の話では」.
default.q.n1-1-q33-33.explanation:
Meaning: According to the experts, this entire area used to be the sea long ago.
- Structure: 「〜の話では／〜によると + plain form + という / とのことだ / そうだ」: according to a source...; it is said that...
- Kanji readings: 専門家 (expert), 地域一帯 (the entire area), かつて (formerly, long ago).
- Example: ニュースによると、明日から全国的に寒くなるという。(According to the news, it is said that it will become colder throughout the country starting tomorrow.)
default.q.n1-1-q33-33.why.0: (a) 1. という: Correct. This is the quotative/hearsay pattern 「〜という」(it is said that / according to tradition), often paired with an information source such as 「〜の話では／〜によると」.
default.q.n1-1-q33-33.why.1: (b) 2. といえる: means “can be said to be...” and expresses a subjective assessment, so it is unsuitable when introducing information from a specific source.
default.q.n1-1-q33-33.why.2: (c) 3. といった: Used to list examples ('things such as...'), not as a predicate at the end of a sentence conveying information.
default.q.n1-1-q33-33.why.3: (d) 4. といわれる: Meaning “is said to be” or “is regarded as,” it expresses a general social belief and commonly occurs with 「昔から／一般に」. When a specific source such as 「専門家の話では」is given, the grammatically appropriate hearsay ending is 「〜という / 〜とのことだ」.
default.q.n1-1-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 3. があってはならない: The pattern 「〜てはならない」 combines with 「ことがある」 to form 「ことがあってはならない」, meaning “something must absolutely not happen...”
default.q.n1-1-q34-34.explanation:
Meaning: Children cannot choose the family circumstances into which they are born. For that very reason, we must never allow their educational opportunities to be taken away by their parents’ financial circumstances.
- Pattern: 「V-てはならない」: must never / must not do something (used in formal language to state moral standards or legal rules).
- Kanji readings and meanings: 家庭環境 (family circumstances), 経済状況 (economic circumstances), 教育機会 (educational opportunities), 奪われる (to be deprived of).
- Example: 医療現場において、人為的なミスが決してあってはならない。(In medical settings, human error must never be allowed to occur.)
default.q.n1-1-q34-34.why.0: (a) 1. があるわけではない: Means “it is not necessarily the case that there is ...” or “it is not as if there is ...” This mild negation does not fit the argument’s emphasis on “precisely because of that,” expressed by だからこそ.
default.q.n1-1-q34-34.why.1: (b) 2. であるわけではない: grammatically incorrect in combination; in this context, a nominalized こと is not used with であるわけではない.
default.q.n1-1-q34-34.why.2: (c) 3. があってはならない: Correct grammar. 「V-てはならない」 means “must not” or “must never,” and when combined with 「ことがある」 (“there is a possibility/event”), 「ことがあってはならない」 means “such a thing must never be allowed to happen.”
default.q.n1-1-q34-34.why.3: (d) 4. であってはならない: Incorrect particle/construction with 「奪われること」. 「があってはならない」 must be used because it describes an event occurring or a situation existing.
default.q.n1-1-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 2. なんかでいいんですか: 「N + なんか」is used to humbly put oneself down, while 「〜でいいんですか」is used to ask for the other person's opinion or confirmation.
default.q.n1-1-q35-35.explanation:
Dialogue meaning:
Teacher: "Aoki, I'm thinking of asking you to model for the report magazine this term. What do you think?"
Aoki: "I would be happy to. But... would someone like me really be okay?"
Teacher: "Of course!"
- Structures: 「N + なんか／なんて」: someone/something like... (used to humbly put oneself down); 「〜でいいんですか」: Is ... like this all right? (asking for confirmation).
- Sino-Japanese reading: 報告誌 (a report magazine or bulletin).
- Example: 私なんかでよければ、喜んでお手伝いさせていただきます。(If someone like me can be of help, I would be delighted to assist.)
default.q.n1-1-q35-35.why.0: (a) 1. だったらいいんですか: 「〜たら」 expresses a hypothetical condition (“if it is…, then is that all right?”). It does not convey the humble tone of lowering oneself when being asked to handle an important task.
default.q.n1-1-q35-35.why.1: (b) 2. なんかでいいんですか: Grammatically and contextually correct. 「なんか」 conveys humility (“someone like me”), and combined with 「〜でいいんですか」 it politely asks the teacher for confirmation.
default.q.n1-1-q35-35.why.2: (c) 3. だったらいいんでしょう: This incorrectly uses だったら and the casual, imposing sentence ending 「〜でしょう」, which is inappropriate when speaking respectfully to a teacher.
default.q.n1-1-q35-35.why.3: (d) 4. なんかでいいんでしょうか: Although 「〜でしょうか」 is more formal, in this context of a spontaneous reply to a teacher's direct question, 「私なんかでいいんですか」 is natural and direct, matching the test's official answer.
default.q.n1-1-q36-36.verdict: Correct order: 2 → 3 → 1 → 4. The ★ position is answer choice 1 (が).
default.q.n1-1-q36-36.explanation:
昨日はとても寒く、積もりこそしなかったが午前中ずっと雪が降っていた。
→ Meaning: Yesterday was very cold. Although the snow did not accumulate, it continued falling throughout the morning.
default.q.n1-1-q36-36.why.0: (a) 「1. が」: This is a conjunction indicating contrast, placed after the emphatic negative 「積もりこそしなかった」 to form 「積もりこそしなかったが」 (although it did not accumulate into a layer...), at the third position (★ blank).
default.q.n1-1-q36-36.why.1: (b) 「2. こそ」: It follows directly after the continuative form 「積もり」to create the concessive or emphatic structure 「〜こそ...」(although..., yet...), and is in position 1.
default.q.n1-1-q36-36.why.2: (c) 「3. しなかった」: It follows the particle 「こそ」 to complete the concessive negative clause 「積もりこそしなかった」(although it did not accumulate into a thick layer of snow), and belongs in position 2.
default.q.n1-1-q36-36.why.3: (d) 「4. 午前中」: This time-expression noun phrase functions as an adverbial modifier of 「ずっと雪が降っていた」(it snowed continuously throughout the morning), so it belongs in position 4.
default.q.n1-1-q37-37.verdict: The correct order is: 1 → 3 → 2 → 4. The ★ is in the second position (周りの人々とのトラブルが絶えない).
default.q.n1-1-q37-37.explanation:
この映画はあまりにも正直で真面目すぎるがゆえに周りの人々とのトラブルが絶えない男の日常を描いた、コメディー作品だ。
→ Meaning: This comedy portrays the everyday life of a man who is constantly involved in trouble with the people around him precisely because he is excessively honest and serious.
default.q.n1-1-q37-37.why.0: (a) 「1. 真面目すぎる」: follows the te-form adjective 「あまりにも正直で」 to describe the character’s personality (excessively honest and overly serious), and appears in position 1.
default.q.n1-1-q37-37.why.1: (b) 「2. 周りの人々とのトラブルが絶えない」: This negative result follows from the cause expressed by 「〜がゆえに」 and also modifies 「男の日常」, so it belongs in the third position (the ★ gap).
default.q.n1-1-q37-37.why.2: (c) 「3. がゆえに」: Following the adjective 「真面目すぎる」, it forms the grammar pattern 「〜がゆえに」 (“precisely because..., resulting in a negative consequence”), and is in the second position.
default.q.n1-1-q37-37.why.3: (d) 「4. 男の日常を描いた」: This is an attributive phrase modifying the following noun 「コメディー作品」(a comedy work depicting a man’s everyday life...), so it occupies the fourth position.
default.q.n1-1-q38-38.verdict: The correct order is: 3 → 1 → 4 → 2. The ★ position is choice 4 (ビジネス書に).
default.q.n1-1-q38-38.explanation:
Business books are generally thought of as stiff and difficult to read, but recently many works have explained business theories clearly through manga, making them accessible even to people who are reluctant to read business books.
→ Meaning: Business books are generally thought of as dry and rigid, but recently many works have explained business theories in an easy-to-understand way through manga so that even people who feel hesitant about business books can read them easily.
default.q.n1-1-q38-38.why.0: (a) 「1. 堅苦しいものと思われるがちだが」: This uses the grammar 「〜がちだ」 together with the conjunction 「が」 (it tends to be regarded as something stiff and formal, but...), shifting to the following clause. It belongs in the second position.
default.q.n1-1-q38-38.why.1: (b) 「2. 抵抗がある人にも」 follows 「ビジネス書に」 to form 「ビジネス書に抵抗がある人にも」, modifying the purpose clause 「読みやすいように」 (“so that even people who feel reluctant about business books can read it easily”). It is in the fourth position.
default.q.n1-1-q38-38.why.2: (c) 「3. 一般的にビジネス書というと」 uses the pattern 「〜というと」 to introduce a general topic at the beginning of a sentence (“Generally speaking, when we talk about business books…”), and appears in position 1.
default.q.n1-1-q38-38.why.3: (d) 「4. ビジネス書に」: It follows the contrastive conjunction 「が」 and functions as the complement indicating the object of 「抵抗がある」 (“to feel hesitant about business books”), occupying the third position (the ★ slot).
default.q.n1-1-q39-39.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 1 → 3. The star ★ is in position 1 (今度は).
default.q.n1-1-q39-39.explanation:
渋滞の中を時間運転してようやくついたと思ったら今度は駐車場が混雑していて遊園地に入る前から疲れてしまった。
→ Meaning: After driving for hours through traffic, I thought I had finally arrived, but then the parking lot was packed, so I was exhausted even before entering the amusement park.
default.q.n1-1-q39-39.why.0: (a) 「1. 今度は」: This linking adverb appears in the pattern 「〜と思ったら今度は…」(just when you think it is over, then...), and belongs in position 3 (the ★ slot).
default.q.n1-1-q39-39.why.1: (b) 「2. 時間運転して」: Following 「渋滞の中を」, it describes driving for several hours in traffic and belongs in position 1.
default.q.n1-1-q39-39.why.2: (c) 「3. 駐車場が混雑していて」: This presents the next problem, namely that the parking lot is extremely crowded, leading to the final result 「〜疲れてしまった」; it belongs in position 4.
default.q.n1-1-q39-39.why.3: (d) 「4. ようやくついたと思ったら」: It follows the te-form 「運転して」 and uses the pattern 「〜と思ったら」 (“just when I thought I had finally arrived...”), so it belongs in the second position.
default.q.n1-1-q40-40.verdict: Correct order: 4 → 2 → 3 → 1. The position marked ★ is choice 3 (知られないことには).
default.q.n1-1-q40-40.explanation:
商品やサービスがどんなに良い物でもその存在が知られないことには売れるも売れないもない。
→ Meaning: No matter how good a product or service is, if people do not know it exists, it is impossible even to discuss whether it will sell.
default.q.n1-1-q40-40.why.0: (a) 「1. 売れるも売れないも」: Combined with 「ない」 at the end of the sentence, it forms the idiomatic pattern 「〜も〜もない」 (“it is not even a matter of whether it sells or not”), which belongs in position 4.
default.q.n1-1-q40-40.why.1: (b) 「2. その存在が」: It serves as the subject of the passive verb 「知られない」 in the conditional clause and appears in the second position.
default.q.n1-1-q40-40.why.2: (c) 「3. 知られないことには」: This uses the negative conditional grammar pattern 「〜ないことには〜ない」 (“unless..., ...cannot”), and it is in the third position (★ blank).
default.q.n1-1-q40-40.why.3: (d) 「4. どんなに良い物でも」: The concessive clause comes immediately after the subject 「商品やサービスが」(no matter how good the products or services are), so it is in position 1.
default.q.n1-1-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 気を使わせられはしない.
default.q.n1-1-q41-41.explanation:
【Meaning】
「〜（さ）せられはしない」combines the causative-passive / causative-potential form with the emphatic negative structure「〜はしない」. It means: “I absolutely cannot let or make someone endure or do something troublesome because of me.” It expresses strong determination or the speaker’s sense of ethics and responsibility.

【Formation】
Causative verb [V-（させ）] + られはしない
(In this sentence: 気を使う ➔ 気を使わせる [causative: make someone worry or feel obliged] ➔ 気を使わせられる [causative-passive/potential: be put in a position where someone worries or feels obliged] + はしない ➔ 気を使わせられはしない: I cannot let someone else worry or feel obliged because of me.)

【Example sentences】
・どんなに生活が苦しくても、年老いた両親に心配をかけさせられはしない。
(No matter how difficult life becomes, I absolutely cannot let my elderly parents worry about me.)
・お世話になった先輩に、これ以上迷惑をかけさせられはしない。
(I cannot let the senior who has always helped me suffer any more trouble because of me.)
default.q.n1-1-q41-41.why.0: (a) 「気を使えはしない」 uses the potential form 「使え」 plus 「はしない」, meaning that the speaker cannot be considerate or hold back. It does not express the desire not to trouble someone or make a senior person worry about them.
default.q.n1-1-q41-41.why.1: (b) 「気を使ってなどいない」 strongly denies the speaker's own action (“It's not as if I am being considerate at all”), so it does not express the feeling of avoiding causing someone trouble.
default.q.n1-1-q41-41.why.2: (c) 「気を使わせられはしない」combines the causative meaning of making someone worry with 「〜られはしない」 (absolutely cannot do such a thing). It means “I absolutely cannot let my senior have to worry because of me again,” which is completely accurate in meaning and grammar.
default.q.n1-1-q41-41.why.3: (d) 「気を使わせてなどいない」means “not making or causing someone to worry at all.” It denies a fact in reality, rather than expressing the speaker’s feelings or resolve not to inconvenience others.
default.q.n1-1-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 4. それにもかかわらず.
default.q.n1-1-q42-42.explanation:
【Meaning】
「それにもかかわらず」is a conjunction placed at the beginning of a sentence meaning "nevertheless," "despite that," or "even so." It connects to a result that is completely contrary to the natural outcome or expectation arising from the situation described in the preceding sentence.

【Usage】
It usually appears at the beginning of the second sentence and has a formal, written tone. It is much more formal than それなのに.

【Example sentences】
・医師から禁煙を強く勧められていた。それにもかかわらず、彼は煙草をやめようとしない。
(The doctor strongly advised him to quit smoking. Nevertheless, he has no intention of quitting.)
・政府は景気回復のための対策を打ち出した。それにもかかわらず、失業率は改善していない。
(The government introduced measures to restore the economy. Despite that, the unemployment rate has not improved.)
default.q.n1-1-q42-42.why.0: (a) 「それによって」expresses cause and effect (“as a result,” “because of that,” or “by that means”), so it cannot create the paradoxical contrast with the bad weather in the preceding sentence.
default.q.n1-1-q42-42.why.1: (b) 「そればかりでなく」 expresses an additive progression, meaning “not only that, but also ...” It is not suitable for connecting two clauses that are contrasting or unexpected.
default.q.n1-1-q42-42.why.2: (c) 「それどころか」means “on the contrary” or “far from…, it even…”. It is used to negate the preceding statement or intensify it further, not to express an actual result that occurs despite a warning.
default.q.n1-1-q42-42.why.3: (d) 「それにもかかわらず」 means “nevertheless” or “despite that.” It accurately describes the fans still turning up in large numbers despite the warning of a major storm in the preceding clause.
default.q.n1-1-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 承知していれば.
default.q.n1-1-q43-43.explanation:
【Meaning】
「〜ていれば」is the conditional form of the state/progressive form 「〜ている」. When used with verbs of cognition such as 承知する (to know or understand fully), it means: "If I had known/understood that in advance..." It is often used in a counterfactual conditional referring to the past, expressing regret.

【Formation】
[V-て-form] + いれば
(Example: 承知する ➔ 承知していて ➔ 承知していれば)

【Examples】
・事前にこのようなリスクがあると承知していれば、あの契約を結ぶことはなかっただろう。
(If I had known in advance that there was such a risk, I would not have entered into that contract.)
・利用規約をきちんと承知していれば、トラブルを未然に防げたはずだ。
(If I had fully understood the terms of use beforehand, I should have been able to prevent the trouble.)
default.q.n1-1-q43-43.why.0: (a) 「承知していれば」is in the conditional 〜ば form, creating the counterfactual past pattern 「〜ていれば〜なかったはずだ」(“If I had known beforehand, I certainly would not have done it”), which fits the sentence perfectly.
default.q.n1-1-q43-43.why.1: (b) 「承知していて」 is a te-form used to connect clauses or indicate an actual circumstance, meaning “knowing that ... and ...” It does not create a hypothetical conditional clause for what follows.
default.q.n1-1-q43-43.why.2: (c) 「承知していたのか」ends with the interrogative/exclamatory expression「のか」, meaning self-questioning or challenging someone (“had they known already?”). It cannot serve as a conditional clause connecting to the following sentence.
default.q.n1-1-q43-43.why.3: (d) 「承知していたかのように」 means “as if [someone] had known beforehand.” It is used for a simile describing an attitude or behavior and does not fit the conditional-result structure here.
default.q.n1-1-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 2. だって.
default.q.n1-1-q44-44.explanation:
【Meaning】
「〜だって」is a particle originating from 「〜であっても / 〜でも」, with two main uses:
1. Introducing an extreme example: “even...” or “even ... too” (equivalent to でも / でさえ).
2. Following degree adverbs such as 「いくら / どんなに」: “no matter how...” or “even if...” (equivalent to 「いくら＋N＋でも」).

【Connection】
[Noun / interrogative word] + だって

【Examples】
・いくら頑丈な建物だって、これほどの大地震に耐えられるとは限らない。
(Even a sturdy building may not necessarily withstand an earthquake this powerful.)
・プロの料理人だって、時には失敗することもある。
(Even professional chefs sometimes make mistakes.)
default.q.n1-1-q44-44.why.0: (a) 「なら」 introduces a straightforward hypothetical condition, meaning “if it is ...” It does not combine with the concessive degree adverb 「いくら」 in this pattern.
default.q.n1-1-q44-44.why.1: (b) 「だって」combines with 「いくら＋N」to form the familiar concessive pattern 「いくら〜だって」(even if it is..., no matter how...), which is completely correct grammatically and semantically.
default.q.n1-1-q44-44.why.2: (c) 「でさえ」means “even” or “even as much as.” However, standard Japanese grammar does not combine it as 「いくら〜でさえ」; use 「いくら〜でも」 or 「だって」 instead.
default.q.n1-1-q44-44.why.3: (d) 「といっても」means “although one says that..., in reality...”; it is used to explain or add a limitation to the preceding statement and does not combine with「いくら」in a concessive hypothetical sentence.
default.q.n1-10-q45-45.explanation: Paragraph 1 clearly states that reductionism (要素還元主義) enabled major advances in science by breaking natural phenomena down into smaller elements. However, placing excessive faith in the universal power of this method can lead to a mistaken understanding of the nature of nature itself. The reason is given immediately after "なぜなら": in nonlinear systems with countless interacting elements, it is theoretically impossible to predict the order or distinctive properties that emerge at the level of the whole, no matter how precisely the properties of each individual element are combined. Therefore, answer choice 2 most accurately reflects the author's point.
default.q.n1-10-q45-45.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the practical analysis and reduction method provides high reproducibility, as stated in paragraph 2: 「高い再現性を獲得する反面」. Therefore, saying that “highly reproducible rules cannot be derived” contradicts the passage.
default.q.n1-10-q45-45.why.1: (b) Correct because it accurately expresses the cause: even a detailed analysis of each element cannot predict the nature of the entire system, which emerges from interactions among the elements. This matches "個々の要素の性質をどれほど精密に積み上げても、全体として立ち現れる特有の秩序や性質を予測することは原理的に困難".
default.q.n1-10-q45-45.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage does not say that nonlinear systems are completely unrelated to the laws of physics. It says that the order of a complex system cannot be reduced entirely to the laws governing each individual element.
default.q.n1-10-q45-45.why.3: (d) Incorrect because paragraph 1 states that reductionism has brought about remarkable advances in science (「目覚ましい発展を遂げてきた」), not that it has caused science to stagnate (停滞).
default.q.n1-10-q46-46.explanation: At the beginning of the second passage, the author presents the idea of "創発" (emergence): a phenomenon that arises from the dynamic interactions among relationships, rather than from the isolated behavior of individual elements. The author immediately gives the example of cells: even if we thoroughly analyze the functions of a single cell, we still cannot fully explain how the whole living system adapts and maintains its own order. This example demonstrates that studying each element separately cannot explain the autonomous order of the whole system that emerges from interacting relationships. Therefore, answer choice 1 is correct.
default.q.n1-10-q46-46.why.0: (a) Correct because the example of cells clarifies the preceding argument: analyzing each element in isolation cannot explain the order of life as a whole, which originates from dynamic interactions among relationships.
default.q.n1-10-q46-46.why.1: (b) Incorrect because it contradicts the author’s point; the author argues that analyzing individual cells is insufficient to explain the entire mechanism of adaptation in living things, not that it is the “only clue.”
default.q.n1-10-q46-46.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage does not say that analyzing cells is “technically impossible.” Instead, it assumes that even a thorough analysis (徹底的に分析しても) would still fail to explain the holistic nature of life.
default.q.n1-10-q46-46.why.3: (d) Incorrect because it contradicts the passage. The author states that the interaction among relationships (関係性のダイナミズム) is the source of the phenomenon's emergence, not the isolated function of individual cells.
default.q.n1-10-q47-47.explanation: The final sentence of passage 2 clearly presents both sides of reductionist thinking: "還元主義的な視座は、対象を固定的な枠組みに切り縮めることで高い再現性を獲得する反面、要素間の絶え間ない相互作用が生み出す動的な調和を切り捨ててしまうリスクを孕んでいる" (A reductionist perspective achieves high reproducibility by narrowing its subject to a fixed framework, but at the same time carries the risk of discarding the dynamic harmony created by the continuous interaction among its elements). Choice 3 fully expresses both the benefit achieved (high reproducibility) and the risk (overlooking the dynamic interaction among the elements).
default.q.n1-10-q47-47.why.0: (a) Incorrect because reductionism narrows its focus and eliminates interactions among factors, rather than valuing (重視) those interactions.
default.q.n1-10-q47-47.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Viewing the subject as an organic whole (有機的な全体) is an integrated perspective (統合的な視点), not a reductionist perspective (還元主義).
default.q.n1-10-q47-47.why.2: (c) Correct because it accurately reflects the two-part structure of the sentence: "高い再現性を獲得する反面、...動的な調和を切り捨ててしまうリスクを孕んでいる".
default.q.n1-10-q47-47.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the reductionist viewpoint confines an object within a fixed framework (固定的な枠組みに切り縮める) and struggles with nonlinear systems, which is contrary to the content of this choice.
default.q.n1-10-q48-48.explanation: Paragraph 3 concludes the author's central idea: To truly penetrate the deeper layers of nature, science must not stop at dissecting and analyzing individual details. It must move back and forth (往還) between a detailed analytical perspective and an integrative perspective that grasps the whole as an organic connection. A new horizon of knowledge opens precisely through the tension between reduction and integration. Therefore, choice 2 most accurately summarizes this core message.
default.q.n1-10-q48-48.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author does not call for completely abandoning reductionism (完全に放棄). Instead, the author emphasizes maintaining a detailed analytical perspective while also incorporating an integrated viewpoint (「細部を分析する眼差しを保持しつつも」).
default.q.n1-10-q48-48.why.1: (b) Correct because it accurately reflects the paragraph’s concluding sentence: one must move back and forth between maintaining a gaze that analyzes details and an integrated perspective that grasps the whole as an organic connection (「細部を分析する眼差しを保持しつつも、全体を有機的な連関として捉え直す統合的な視点との往還が不可欠である」).
default.q.n1-10-q48-48.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the author says that a new horizon of knowledge lies precisely in the tension between two opposing approaches (「相反するアプローチの緊張関係の中にこそ」), not in eliminating the opposition to maintain a fixed framework.
default.q.n1-10-q48-48.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage does not advocate prioritizing intuition over reproducibility or disregarding the laws of physics.
default.q.n1-10-q49-49.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Overemphasizing efficiency and eliminating waste and uncertainty causes people to lose opportunities to cultivate sensitivity and deepen their lives.
default.q.n1-10-q49-49.explanation:
- Main point: The passage criticizes the modern tendency to worship efficiency and always seek the shortest path to a result, thereby eliminating detours, idle time, and uncertainty—fertile ground for cultivating unique perceptions and deepening an independent inner life.

- Question translation: What is the author primarily trying to say in this passage?

- Answer choice translations:
1. If we place too much value on efficiency and excessively eliminate waste and uncertainty from life, we lose opportunities to enrich our perceptions and deepen our lives.
2. To cultivate unique perceptions in modern society, we should stop watching videos at accelerated speed and live a life that values the process over the result.
3. By eliminating uncertainty from everyday life through greater efficiency, we can escape stereotyped thinking and reflect independently.
4. Modern people are absorbed in receiving information efficiently, and because their free time has increased, they are instead even less able to find meaning in life.
default.q.n1-10-q49-49.why.0: (a) Correct, because it exactly matches the core message in the latter half of the passage: 「一見無駄に思える寄り道や、何者にも規定されない空白の時間こそが、画一化された思考の枠組みを揺さぶり、独自の感性や洞察を涵養する土壌となるのではないだろうか。効率性の名の下に不確実性を過剰に排除し続けた結果、私たちは自らの生活を自律的に深める契機を、かえって自ら損なっているように思えてならない。」 (Seemingly pointless detours and unstructured free time cultivate individual sensibilities; by excessively eliminating uncertainty in the name of efficiency, we are instead undermining opportunities to deepen our lives autonomously.)
default.q.n1-10-q49-49.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The article merely presents watching videos at fast speed as a typical example (その典型) of the preference for efficiency. The author does not give the extreme advice to “stop watching at fast speed” and “value only the process” (過程のみを重んじる).
default.q.n1-10-q49-49.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the statement is completely contrary to the passage. The author argues that eliminating uncertainty in the name of efficiency harms opportunities for independent reflection, rather than helping people escape stereotyped thinking.
default.q.n1-10-q49-49.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage never mentions that “having more discretionary time” (可処分時間が増えたこと) causes people to lose their sense of meaning. It only says that people struggle to find ways to spend that time without wasting it.
default.q.n1-10-q50-50.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 目先の効率のみにとらわれず、試行錯誤や失敗の可能性を受け入れながら未知の領域を探ること。
default.q.n1-10-q50-50.explanation:
Main idea summary: In modern business, maximum efficiency is often emphasized, but revolutionary values arise from trial and error and unexpected detours. A work style that follows only predetermined paths undermines the ability to adapt to unforeseen changes. Therefore, sustainable development requires creating “space” to explore new fields and accepting the risk of failure instead of focusing solely on immediate efficiency.

Question translation: Which choice best reflects the author’s view?

Choice translations:
1. Put efficiency first and eliminate the risk of failure in order to reproduce successful models from the past.
2. To respond to unexpected environmental changes, work efficiently and without waste by following the predetermined route.
3. Instead of being bound solely by immediate efficiency, accept trial and error and the possibility of failure in order to explore unknown fields.
4. To achieve sustainable organizational growth, avoid unexpected detours and produce results by taking the shortest route.
default.q.n1-10-q50-50.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The author criticizes a way of working that merely reproduces past successful models (「過去の成功パターンの再生産に終始し」) and eliminates risk and waste in an extreme manner.
default.q.n1-10-q50-50.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage states that merely following a predetermined route, 「あらかじめ定められた正解の道筋だけをなぞる働き方」, may deprive people of the ability to adapt when faced with unexpected environmental changes, 「予期せぬ環境変化に直面した際の適応力を奪いかねない」. It is not presented as a way to respond to such changes.
default.q.n1-10-q50-50.why.2: (c) Correct. This matches the conclusion of the passage: 「個人や組織が持続的な成長を遂げるためには、目先の効率追求に過度に縛られることなく、失敗の可能性や曖昧さを許容しながら未知の領域を探索する「余白」を意識的に確保することが不可欠なのである。」 (For individuals and organizations to achieve sustainable growth, it is essential to consciously secure “leeway” for exploring unknown areas while accepting the possibility of failure and ambiguity, without becoming excessively constrained by the pursuit of immediate efficiency.)
default.q.n1-10-q50-50.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The author states that genuine innovative value is created precisely through accidental detours (「偶発的な寄り道の過程においてこそ生み出される」). Therefore, avoiding detours in search of the shortest route contradicts the author’s view.
default.q.n1-10-q51-51.verdict: The correct answer is 3: True health is the ability to listen to the body’s signals, adapt flexibly to stress and environmental changes, and restore one’s own balance.
default.q.n1-10-q51-51.explanation:
【Summary of the main point】:
The author points out that in modern society, people often mistakenly believe that having test results within the normal range or not being diagnosed with a disease proves that they are healthy. However, placing too much trust in static data can dull one's ability to sense subtle physical abnormalities.
