default.q.n1-10-q33-33.why.3: (d) 「〜を経た」means “having gone through” or “having passed through” a period or stage; it is semantically inappropriate when modifying an information leak.
default.q.n1-10-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 3. を禁じ得なかった because the pattern 「N (a noun expressing emotion) + を禁じ得ない (past: を禁じ得なかった)」means “be unable to suppress one’s feelings / be unable not to feel.”
default.q.n1-10-q34-34.explanation:
Meaning: Seeing firsthand a historically rich street that had once proudly flourished but had now become completely dilapidated, I could not help feeling deep sorrow.
- Kanji note: 栄華を誇る (to have once enjoyed glorious prosperity), 荒廃 (devastation, decay), 目の当たりにする (to witness firsthand), 悲哀 (sorrow, grief).
- Example: その悲惨な事故のニュースを聞いて、強い憤りを禁じ得なかった。(After hearing the news of that tragic accident, I could not suppress my intense anger.)
default.q.n1-10-q34-34.why.0: (a) 「〜を余儀なくされた」means 'was forced to do something' or 'had no choice but to do something due to objective circumstances'; it is not used to express surging emotions.
default.q.n1-10-q34-34.why.1: (b) 「〜に堪えなかった」: The pattern 「〜に堪えない」 takes the particle に and usually means “extremely [grateful, regretful, etc.]” or “unable to bear / unable to resist.” It does not combine with 「念を...」 as in the question.
default.q.n1-10-q34-34.why.2: (c) 「〜を禁じ得なかった」 means “could not suppress” feelings such as emotion, sorrow, or sadness, and combines naturally and accurately with 「深い悲哀の念を」.
default.q.n1-10-q34-34.why.3: (d) 「〜をもってした」 means “by means of” or “with” an attitude or means, so it does not fit this context.
default.q.n1-10-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 4. きらいがある because the pattern 「V-る / Nの + きらいがある」 means “tend to...” or “have the bad habit of...” with a generally negative tendency.
default.q.n1-10-q35-35.explanation:
Meaning: He is an excellent employee in charge of planning, but he has a tendency to decide everything on his own without listening to the opinions of those around him.
- Vocabulary: 企画 (きかく: plan, project), 独断 (どくだん: making decisions unilaterally, dogmatism), 嫌いがある (きらいがある: to have a tendency or bad habit).
- Example: 彼は他人の意見を軽視するきらいがある。(He has a tendency to disregard other people’s opinions.)
default.q.n1-10-q35-35.why.0: (a) 「〜にかたくない」means “not difficult to do something” (often used in 想像にかたくない - easy to imagine and 察するにかたくない - easy to understand empathically); it does not modify this sentence.
default.q.n1-10-q35-35.why.1: (b) 「〜極まりない」 means “extremely / utterly...”; it follows directly after na-adjectives (with な removed) or i-adjectives (e.g., 失礼極まりない), and does not follow a verb predicate clause.
default.q.n1-10-q35-35.why.2: (c) 「〜にあたらない」 means “not worth doing” or “there is no need to...,” as in 驚くにあたらない, “there is nothing surprising about it,” so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n1-10-q35-35.why.3: (d) 「〜きらいがある」means “tend to / have the bad habit of,” accurately describing his flaw of acting on his own and refusing to listen to others.
default.q.n1-10-q36-36.verdict: The correct order is 2 → 1 → 4 → 3; the starred ★ position is choice 4 (適任者は).
default.q.n1-10-q36-36.explanation:
Complete sentence: 次のプロジェクトのリーダーには、長年の経験と実績を持つ彼をおいてほかに適任者はいないだろう。
Meaning: For the next project leader position, there is probably no one more suitable than him, given his many years of experience and achievements.
default.q.n1-10-q36-36.why.0: (a) 「ほかに」 occupies the second position and combines with 「～をおいて」 to form 「～をおいてほかに…ない」, meaning “there is no one or nothing else besides...”.
default.q.n1-10-q36-36.why.1: (b) 「をおいて」: It occupies position 1 and follows the noun 「彼」 to form the grammar pattern N1 「N + をおいて（～ない）」, meaning “there is no one other than N who is equally suitable or comparable.”
default.q.n1-10-q36-36.why.2: (c) 「い」: It stands in the fourth position and is the continuative form of 「いる」, combining with the existing ending 「ないだろう」 to form the predicate 「いないだろう」.
default.q.n1-10-q36-36.why.3: (d)「適任者は」: It occupies the third position (the ★ position); the particle「は」marks「適任者」as the topic of the predicate「いないだろう」.
default.q.n1-10-q37-37.verdict: The correct order is: 3 → 1 → 4 → 2; the choice in the ★ position is 4 (揺さぶらずには).
default.q.n1-10-q37-37.explanation:
Complete sentence: 彼女の情熱的な歌声は、聴く者の心を揺さぶらずにはおかないだろう。
Meaning: Her passionate singing will surely move the hearts of those who listen.
default.q.n1-10-q37-37.why.0: (a) 「心を」: In position 2, it is the object of the verb 「揺さぶる」(to move deeply), forming 「聴く者の心を」(the hearts of those who listen) with the preceding modifier.
default.q.n1-10-q37-37.why.1: (b) 「おかない」: In the fourth position, it follows 「～ずには」to complete the N1 grammar pattern 「V-ずにはおかない」(will certainly cause; cannot help but...), and comes before the sentence ending 「だろう」.
default.q.n1-10-q37-37.why.2: (c) 「聴く者の」: It appears in first position and is a modifying phrase for the noun 「心」that follows.
default.q.n1-10-q37-37.why.3: (d) 「揺さぶらずには」: This occupies the third position, marked by the star ★. It is the 「ずには」 negative form of the verb 「揺さぶる」 (“to shake” or “to stir”), and combines with 「おかない」 to create a structure emphasizing a powerful emotional impact.
default.q.n1-10-q38-38.verdict: The correct order is: 4 → 3 → 2 → 1; the star ★ is in position 2 (聞くに).
default.q.n1-10-q38-38.explanation:
Complete sentence: 彼のあの不誠実な発言は、同じチームの仲間として聞くに堪えないものだった。
Meaning: As a fellow member of the same team, I found his insincere remark impossible to listen to.
default.q.n1-10-q38-38.why.0: (a) 「堪えないもの」: It occupies the fourth position and combines with 「聞くに」 to form the N1 grammar pattern 「聞くに堪えない」(too offensive to listen to / unbearable to hear), with the nominalizer 「もの」 connecting it to the predicate 「だった」.
default.q.n1-10-q38-38.why.1: (b) 「聞くに」: At the third position (the ★ position), the verb 「聞く」combines with the particle 「に」and 「堪えない」to form the pattern N1 「V-る + に堪えない」(“cannot bear to V / cannot stand V”).
default.q.n1-10-q38-38.why.2: (c) 「仲間として」: Occupies the second position and uses the pattern 「N + として」 (in the capacity of...). Together with the preceding modifier 「同じチームの」, it forms the adverbial phrase 「同じチームの仲間として」.
default.q.n1-10-q38-38.why.3: (d) 「同じチームの」: It appears in position 1 and is an attributive phrase modifying the following noun 「仲間」.
default.q.n1-10-q39-39.verdict: The correct order is: 3 → 1 → 4 → 2; the choice in the ★ position is 4 (全国10か所を).
default.q.n1-10-q39-39.explanation:
Complete sentence: その人気ロックバンドは、東京ドームでの公演を皮切りに全国10か所を巡るツアーを行った。
Meaning: That popular rock band began with a performance at Tokyo Dome and went on a tour of 10 locations nationwide.
default.q.n1-10-q39-39.why.0: (a) 「皮切りに」 is in the second position and combines with the preceding noun to form the grammar pattern N1 「N + を皮切りに（して）」, meaning “starting with N, followed by a succession of similar events.”
default.q.n1-10-q39-39.why.1: (b) 「巡るツアーを」: it occupies the fourth position. The verb 「巡る」 modifies the noun 「ツアーを」, which serves as the direct object of the predicate verb 「行った」 at the end of the sentence.
default.q.n1-10-q39-39.why.2: (c) 「公演を」: appears in the first position, immediately after 「東京ドームでの」, and combines with 「皮切りに」 to form 「東京ドームでの公演を皮切りに」.
default.q.n1-10-q39-39.why.3: (d) 「全国10か所を」 appears in position 3 (the ★ position) and functions as the object indicating the scope of the route for the verb 「巡る」 (travel around or tour).
default.q.n1-10-q40-40.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 1 → 3; the choice in the ★ position is 1 (山奥ならではの).
default.q.n1-10-q40-40.explanation:
Complete sentence: この旅館の露天風呂では、豊かな大自然に囲まれた山奥ならではの風情を存分に味わえる。
Meaning: At this inn's open-air bath, guests can fully enjoy the unique atmosphere of a remote mountain area surrounded by abundant natural beauty.
default.q.n1-10-q40-40.why.0: (a) 「山奥ならではの」: It occupies the third position (the ★ position) and uses the N1 grammar pattern 「N + ならではの」(unique to / characteristic of N) to modify the noun 「風情」.
default.q.n1-10-q40-40.why.1: (b) 「豊かな大自然に」: It occupies position 1 and combines with the passive verb 「囲まれた」 to form an attributive phrase modifying the noun 「山奥」.
default.q.n1-10-q40-40.why.2: (c) 「風情を存分に」is in the fourth position. It is the object of the adverb 「存分に」(to one's heart's content), which directly modifies the verb 「味わえる」.
default.q.n1-10-q40-40.why.3: (d) 「囲まれた」 occupies the second position and is a passive verb in an attributive clause modifying 「山奥」 in 「豊かな大自然に囲まれた山奥」 (“a remote mountain area surrounded by abundant nature”).
default.q.n1-10-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 1. を皮切りに.
default.q.n1-10-q41-41.explanation:
Meaning: Starting with this performance in Tokyo, the large-scale concert tour visiting 10 cities nationwide will officially begin.
- Kanji-based vocabulary: 皮切り (starting point; opening), 公演 (performance), 巡る (to go around; to tour).
- Example: この映画は東京を皮切りに、全国各地で上映される予定だ。(This film is scheduled to be shown throughout the country, starting in Tokyo.)
default.q.n1-10-q41-41.why.0: (a) 「〜を皮切りに」 means “starting with” or “beginning from,” describing an opening event followed by a series of related developments or expansions. Here, the tour begins in Tokyo and continues to ten cities, so it fits the context perfectly.
default.q.n1-10-q41-41.why.1: (b) 「〜を限りに」means “as of the end of... / using this point as the cutoff” (or “to the utmost”), indicating an ending rather than the beginning of development.
default.q.n1-10-q41-41.why.2: (c) 「〜をおいて（〜ない）」means “apart from ..., there is no one or nothing else,” and must be followed by a negative clause.
default.q.n1-10-q41-41.why.3: (d) 「〜にかこつけて」means “using ... as an excuse” and is used when someone uses one reason to do something else, often with a negative nuance; it does not fit the context.
default.q.n1-10-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 2. と相まって.
default.q.n1-10-q42-42.explanation:
Meaning: Exceptional talent is one thing, but this achievement became possible only through combining it with one's own unceasing efforts.
- Kanji and vocabulary: 類まれなる (rare, extraordinary), たゆまぬ努力 (unceasing effort), 快挙 (remarkable achievement, feat), 成し遂げる (accomplish, achieve).
- Example: 厳しい自然環境と人手不足とが相まって、復旧作業は難航している。(The harsh natural environment, combined with a labor shortage, is making the restoration work difficult.)
default.q.n1-10-q42-42.why.0: (a) 「〜にかこつけて」means “using ... as an excuse to do something else” and carries a negative implication, so it does not fit a context praising an achievement.
default.q.n1-10-q42-42.why.1: (b) 「〜と相まって」means “combined with” or “working together with...”; it follows a noun to express multiple factors combining to produce a notable result, and forms a natural pair with 「〜もさることながら」.
default.q.n1-10-q42-42.why.2: (c) 「〜にかまけて」means “to be so absorbed or occupied with something that one neglects something else,” and has a negative nuance, so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n1-10-q42-42.why.3: (d) 「〜をよそに」 means “despite” or “ignoring” someone’s opinions or concerns, so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n1-10-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 2. たるもの.
default.q.n1-10-q43-43.explanation:
Sentence meaning: As the leader of a country, one must always listen to the voice of the people and make fair decisions.
- Sino-Japanese roots & vocabulary: 耳を傾ける (to listen attentively), 公平 (fairness), 判断を下す (to make a judgment/decision).
- Example: 医者たるもの、患者の命を最優先に考えるべきだ。(A doctor should put the patient's life first.)
default.q.n1-10-q43-43.why.0: (a) 「〜にあって」 means “in a particular circumstance or situation”; it is not used to state the status or corresponding duty associated with a position.
default.q.n1-10-q43-43.why.1: (b) 「〜たるもの」means “once one is...” or “as someone who holds a position or bears serious responsibility.” The following clause typically expresses a proper attitude or duty (〜べきだ, 〜なければならない), so this is completely correct.
default.q.n1-10-q43-43.why.2: (c) 「〜とあれば」 means “if it is for...” (then one is willing to do anything), expressing a special condition, so it does not fit the context.
default.q.n1-10-q43-43.why.3: (d) 「〜なしに（は）」 means “without ...” or “unless there is ...”; the following clause requires a negative or impossible meaning.
default.q.n1-10-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 1. おかなかった.
default.q.n1-10-q44-44.explanation:
Meaning: His passionate, soulful speech moved the entire audience in the hall and made it impossible for them not to be touched.
- Structural distinction: 「〜ずにはいられない」describes the subject's inability to suppress their own feelings, whereas 「〜（さ）せずにはおかない」describes a powerful impact that inevitably makes someone else do or feel something.
- Vocabulary and Sino-Japanese character notes: 魂 (soul, spirit), 聴衆 (audience, spectators).
- Example: 彼女の迫真の演技は、観客を魅了せずにはおかなかった。(Her realistic performance inevitably captivated the entire audience.)
default.q.n1-10-q44-44.why.0: (a) 「〜ずにはおかない」 (past form: 「〜ずにはおかなかった」) combines with the causative 「〜させずにはおかない」 to mean “will definitely make someone do something.” The speech causes the listeners to be moved, so this is completely accurate.
default.q.n1-10-q44-44.why.1: (b) 「〜ずにはいられない」 expresses that the subject cannot restrain their own feelings or actions. It is not used when another person is caused to do something, as in 「〜を感動させずには...」.
default.q.n1-10-q44-44.why.2: (c) 「〜ずにはすまない」 means that something cannot be left unresolved or accepted without taking action, particularly from an ethical or social-responsibility standpoint; it does not fit this context.
default.q.n1-10-q44-44.why.3: (d) 「〜やまない」 is used with the te-form as 「〜てやまない」, meaning to sincerely continue wishing or hoping; it does not combine with 「〜ずには」.
default.q.n1-11-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 経験からつくられた枠を取り除けることが大切だ (It is important to be able to remove the framework formed by experience when necessary).
default.q.n1-11-q46-46.explanation: The author explains that everyone has their own “frameworks”—mental patterns formed unconsciously from past experiences and thoughts. These frameworks shape each person’s personality, character, and individual standards, so having them is natural and acceptable (“枠はあってもいい”). However, if someone becomes too bound by such a framework (“枠にとらわれていると”), their imagination cannot develop. Therefore, a key to training the imagination is being able to consciously remove or set aside the mental framework when necessary (“その枠を取り除くことが、想像力を鍛えるひとつのポイントになる” / “必要なときには意識してそれをはずせることが大切だ”). Choice 3 expresses this idea most accurately.
default.q.n1-11-q46-46.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The author states that 「枠はあってもいい」(it is acceptable for frameworks to exist because they create individuality and standards), so the point is not that they must be completely discarded ("捨てなければいけない").
default.q.n1-11-q46-46.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage says "意識してそれをはずせる" (one must consciously remove it when necessary), so the choice "not being conscious of it" ("意識しない") contradicts the author's point.
default.q.n1-11-q46-46.why.2: (c) Correct. The passage clearly states, 「その枠を取り除くことが、想像力を鍛えるひとつのポイントになる」and「必要なときには意識してそれをはずせることが大切だ」, which directly corresponds to being able to remove the framework formed by experience.
default.q.n1-11-q46-46.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The author never says that the framework must be made stronger (“より強いものにしなければいけない”); this contradicts the view of expanding one’s thinking to develop the imagination.
default.q.n1-11-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 「苦しさを受け止めつつ、喜びが感じられるような働き方を目指すべきだ」 (We should aim for a way of working that allows us to accept the hardships while also experiencing joy).
default.q.n1-11-q47-47.explanation: The author points out the dual nature of labor: on the one hand, it involves the physical hardship of producing goods (“体に労苦を強いる”), but on the other hand, it can be transformed into joy when one feels connected to society (“社会とのつながりを感じることができれば喜びにも転化します”). The major problem in today's society is that the joyful aspect has been taken away, leaving only hardship (“苦役だけが残る”). Therefore, the right attitude is neither avoidance nor extremism, but to accept the inherent difficulty of work while also finding joy in one's connection with society. Choice 4 fully captures the author's idea.
default.q.n1-11-q47-47.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The article emphasizes that the joy of work arises precisely from sensing one's connection with society. It does not propose the idea of “feeling happy without feeling connected to society.”
default.q.n1-11-q47-47.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The author discusses balancing and restoring enjoyment in work, not advising workers to “confront or fight hardship” (「苦しさに立ち向かう」).
default.q.n1-11-q47-47.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Work itself is inherently linked to physical exertion (“体に労苦を強いる”), so the goal is not “to avoid feeling any hardship at all” (“苦しさを感じないで済む”) but to regain joy in one's work.
default.q.n1-11-q47-47.why.3: (d) Correct. It accurately expresses the article’s argument: while acknowledging the hardship inherent in work (“苦しさを受け止めつつ”), we should aim for a way of working that brings the joy of social connection (“喜びが感じられるような働き方を目指すべきだ”).
default.q.n1-11-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 買い手が商品を選択する際の判断材料になっている (It serves as a basis for buyers' decisions when selecting products).
default.q.n1-11-q48-48.explanation: In an information-saturated society, the overwhelming amount of information leaves consumers in a dilemma when choosing products because they cannot fully understand the true nature of each one. In such circumstances, highly representative and broadly informative elements, such as names, symbols, and slogans—in other words, brands—become the main basis for judgment, helping consumers evaluate products and reduce the risk of making a purchase decision. Therefore, choice 3 is the most accurate answer.
default.q.n1-11-q48-48.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage focuses on how brands support decision-making in an information-saturated environment, not on stimulating the desire to purchase (「購買意欲を高める」).
default.q.n1-11-q48-48.why.1: (b) Incorrect. A brand or symbol helps buyers feel less uncertain when making a choice; it does not increase their dilemma ("ジレンマを増大させている").
default.q.n1-11-q48-48.why.2: (c) Correct. The article states that symbols and brands serve as key criteria and tools for judgment (「判断材料」), helping consumers choose products more easily and reduce risk.
default.q.n1-11-q48-48.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The article discusses reducing the risk involved in buyers' choices (「選択のリスクを軽減」), not reducing the risk of companies conveying inaccurate information.
default.q.n1-11-q49-49.verdict: The correct answer according to the original test is 3 (クマの餌になる種子の凶作はこれまでもあったから).
default.q.n1-11-q49-49.explanation:
NOTE: The passage pasted into the question is passage (2), about “indigenous housing” (土着の住まい), whereas Question 49 belongs to passage (1) of the July 2019 JLPT N1 exam, which discusses bears (クマ) appearing in residential areas.

• Main point of the original passage (about bears): The author argues that attributing the increased appearance of bears in villages to a “lack of food deep in the forests” is unconvincing/forced (無理がある), because good and bad harvests (豊凶) of forest seeds and nuts are natural cycles that have existed from long ago, not a recently emerging phenomenon.

無理があるように思うのはなぜか。

By contrast, rural culture is not simply characterized by confinement; it is a storehouse of accumulated “life skills” formed through the rhythms of nature, daily work, and unavoidable relationships with other people.

- Translation of the answer choices:
1. Urban freedom establishes true autonomy by freeing people from community constraints, while rural culture has declined into isolation because it has lost its connection with nature.
2. Urban freedom tends to depend on consumer behavior and lead to isolation, whereas rural culture possesses practical wisdom rooted in work and unavoidable relationships with others.
3. Urban freedom creates abundant creativity by enabling people to avoid conflict with others, whereas rural culture deprives individuals of their foundation in life through excessive pressure to conform.
4. Urban freedom helps people connect organically with others through the market economy, whereas rural culture has value only as an increasingly vanishing, idealized pristine landscape.
default.q.n1-11-q61-61.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because paragraph 2 states that freedom in the city is not about “establishing genuine autonomy”; it can easily degenerate into passive consumption (自律的な創造性というよりも...受動的に消費する自由に変質しやすい). It also says that rural culture consists of accumulating practical life skills, not becoming disconnected from nature and falling into closed-off decline.
default.q.n1-11-q61-61.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because paragraph 2 states: "都市における「自由」とは、実のところ自律的な創造性というよりも、市場経済が供給する記号やサービスを受動的に消費する自由に変質しやすい。他者との摩擦を避けるための過剰な配慮や匿名性は、逆説的に希薄な孤立感をもたらし、生活の根拠を奪ってしまう。" (Urban freedom tends to become freedom to passively consume symbols and services supplied by the market, producing isolation) and "農村に息づく文化の本質は、単なる閉鎖性にあるのではなく、自然のリズムや日々の労働、他者との不可避な関わりの中で培われる「生きる技法」の蓄積であったはずだ。" (The essence of rural culture lies in accumulated ways of living cultivated through nature's rhythms, daily work, and unavoidable relationships with others.)
default.q.n1-11-q61-61.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the author says that avoiding conflict and maintaining anonymity in cities creates “a sense of isolation,” not “rich creativity.” The view that rural areas are “places where pressure to conform robs people of the foundation of life” is an extreme perspective that the author criticizes, not the author's own position.
default.q.n1-11-q61-61.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the urban market economy leads to passive consumption and isolation, not an “organic connection.” The idea that the countryside is merely a poetically idealized landscape is a one-sided view mentioned in the first paragraph for the author to challenge; it is not the author's assessment of the value of rural areas.
default.q.n1-11-q62-62.verdict: The correct answer is 3: We need to overcome the isolation of the city’s anonymous environment and connect deeply with others, while rebuilding the reality of life to create a new culture of living.
default.q.n1-11-q62-62.explanation:
- Summary of the main points: As the expansion of the information space blurs the physical boundary between urban and rural areas, the author argues that what we should aim for is neither nostalgia for the past nor one-sided enjoyment of convenience. The true goal is to create a new culture of everyday life: one that connects organically with others within the anonymity of the city while also recreating the physical awareness and authenticity of life rooted in rural areas.

- Translation of the question: In today’s era, considering the relationship between urban and rural areas, what should we aim for according to the author?
- Translation of the answer choices:
1. Because the development of the information space has erased the difference between urban and rural areas, we should maximize urban convenience and pursue individual freedom to the extreme.
2. To overcome the drawbacks of urban life caused by weak interpersonal relationships, we should abandon modern life and return to traditional rural communities.
3. While preserving the anonymity provided by the city, we should overcome isolation and build a new culture of everyday life that makes use of the realities of life and deep connections with others.
4. We should eliminate the remaining pressure to conform in rural areas through urban mobility and homogenize the cultures of both areas through the power of the market economy.
default.q.n1-11-q62-62.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the author only says that the physical boundary is becoming blurred (物理的境界が曖昧になりつつある), not that the difference has completely disappeared (差異は消滅した). Paragraph 3 also states that the important point is not merely to enjoy urban convenience (都市の利便性を享受しつつ...ではない).
default.q.n1-11-q62-62.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because in paragraph 3, the author clearly states: "重要なのは、都市の利便性を享受しつつ農村の共同体性を懐古することではない" (What matters is not nostalgically longing for rural community while enjoying urban convenience); the author does not advocate abandoning modern life and returning to traditional villages.
default.q.n1-11-q62-62.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because it is quoted directly from the end of paragraph 3: "私たちが問うべきは、いかにして都市的な匿名性の中で他者と有機的につながり、農村的な身体感覚や生のリアリティを再構築するかという、新たな生活文化の創造なのである。" (We need to find ways to connect organically with others within urban anonymity and reconstruct a rural sense of the body and the reality of life in order to create a new culture of living.)
default.q.n1-11-q62-62.why.3: (d) Option 4 is incorrect because the author does not propose using the power of the market economy to homogenize the two cultures (市場経済の力で均質化させていく). On the contrary, paragraph 2 criticizes the way the market economy distorts freedom.
default.q.n1-11-q63-63.verdict: The correct answer is 2: Deliberately forgetting helps eliminate minor differences between details and extract common points from individual experiences, thereby forming concepts and applying them flexibly to new situations.
default.q.n1-11-q63-63.explanation:
- Main idea: The author explains that an organism's memory system is not intended to reproduce every detail of the outside world exactly as it is, but to achieve "abstraction." "Active forgetting" functions as a filter, removing minor differences between individual experiences and extracting what they have in common (forming concepts and categories). This enables organisms to reason flexibly and adapt to unfamiliar objects and environments.
- Question translation: According to the author, why is "active forgetting" important for organisms?
- Answer choices:
  1. By erasing unpleasant or traumatic memories from the past, organisms can reduce their mental burden when facing an unfamiliar environment.
  2. By discarding trivial differences among individual experiences and extracting what they have in common, organisms can form concepts and apply them to situations they have never encountered before.
  3. Because the brain has limited storage capacity, old information must be deleted sequentially to ensure that new information can be stored accurately.
  4. Because retaining detailed memories for a long time may accelerate the aging of nerve cells and lead to impaired cognitive function.
default.q.n1-11-q63-63.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is inappropriate because the passage does not mention erasing unpleasant memories or psychological trauma to reduce emotional burdens; this is an inference beyond the text.
default.q.n1-11-q63-63.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because paragraph 2 states: 「瑣末な差異をそぎ落とす「能動的な忘却」というフィルターが介在して初めて、生物は過去の限られた経験から共通項を抽出し、初めて遭遇する未知の対象に対して柔軟に類推を働かせることが可能になるのである。」 Only through the filter of 「能動的な忘却」, which removes trivial differences, can living creatures extract common features from their limited past experiences and make flexible analogies when encountering unfamiliar objects for the first time.
default.q.n1-11-q63-63.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is not appropriate because the reading does not mention that limited brain capacity requires old data to be deleted in order to store new data; instead, it states that the purpose of biological memory is not to store perfectly accurate copies.
default.q.n1-11-q63-63.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is inappropriate because the passage gives no information suggesting that retaining detailed memories for a long time causes neurons to age faster or leads to cognitive decline.
default.q.n1-11-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 4: Noise in the brain prevents thinking from being trapped by preconceptions, provides flexible adaptability to environmental changes, and motivates unique innovations.
default.q.n1-11-q64-64.explanation:
- Main point: In contrast to the engineering view that treats “noise” as an error to be eliminated in order to achieve accurate reproducibility, biological neural networks make use of random noise in synaptic transmission to prevent thought from falling into fixed biases or local optimization. Accepting this fluctuation provides behavioral flexibility and sparks unique innovations when facing a changing environment.
- Question translation: Which statement about the role of “noise (fluctuation)” in the brain is consistent with the explanation in the passage?
- Answer choice translations:
  1. Like a precision-engineered device, it improves the reproducibility of thought and prevents errors from occurring.
  2. It compensates for delays in synaptic transmission, enabling perfectly accurate behavior without the slightest error in response to external stimuli.
  3. It increases as the brain ages and causes damage to rational and logical judgment.
  4. It prevents thought from being trapped by particular fixed biases, creating flexible adaptation to environmental changes and unique innovations.
default.q.n1-11-q64-64.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is inappropriate because engineering thinking treats noise as an error-causing factor that obstructs reproducibility, whereas the biological brain makes use of randomness in noise, not to improve reproducibility or prevent errors.
default.q.n1-11-q64-64.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is unsuitable because the passage states that the neural network uses noise to avoid strict optimization, not to compensate for synaptic delays and produce perfectly accurate behavior.
default.q.n1-11-q64-64.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is inappropriate because the author presents noise as an ingenious adaptation mechanism of neural networks, not as a defect that increases when an aging brain damages judgment.
default.q.n1-11-q64-64.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is correct, as shown directly in paragraph 3: 「生体の神経ネットワークは、シナプス伝達などに伴う確率的なノイズを巧みに利用することで、思考が特定の固定観念や「局所的な最適解」に囚われて膠着状態に陥るのを防いでいる。不確実で変動の激しい自然界を生き抜く上で、あえて厳密な最適化を行わず、ある程度のランダムなゆらぎを許容することこそが、予期せぬ環境変化に対する行動の可塑性や、独創的な発想をもたらす推進力となっているのである。」
default.q.n1-11-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is 1: Unlike the strict precision of digital computers, the human brain excels in resilience and adaptive flexibility because it accommodates ambiguity and redundancy.
default.q.n1-11-q65-65.explanation:
- **Main point:** The author points out that the true strength of human intelligence does not lie in achieving absolute accuracy in every detail, as digital systems do, but in "structural flexibility"—the ability to accommodate ambiguity and redundancy in order to adapt flexibly to circumstances.
- **Question translation:** How does the author view digital computer intelligence and the human brain?
- **Answer choices:**
  1. Unlike the strict accuracy and optimization pursued by digital computers, the human brain is strong in its ability to adapt flexibly by incorporating ambiguity and redundancy.
  2. Because the human brain is inferior to computers in accuracy and memory retention, it is desirable to compensate for these shortcomings with artificial intelligence technology.
  3. Digital computers are good at abstracting information and forming concepts, whereas the human brain is good at perfectly storing past experiences as objective copies.
  4. Only by completely eliminating noise from calculations and increasing infallibility can artificial intelligence imitate the human brain's unique creative ability.
default.q.n1-11-q65-65.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is correct because the passage states: 「人間の知性の本質的な強みは、デジタルシステムのような寸分違わぬ精密さではなく、むしろ曖昧さや冗長性を内包した「構造的なしなやかさ」にあることが明白となる。」 (The essential strength of human intelligence lies not in the flawless precision of digital systems, but rather in “structural flexibility,” which includes ambiguity and redundancy.)
default.q.n1-11-q65-65.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is unsuitable because the author rejects the reductionist view that forgetfulness or vagueness is a “shortcoming that should be corrected with computer technology.”
default.q.n1-11-q65-65.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is inappropriate because the content is reversed. It is the human brain that moves toward abstraction and concept formation, and the author states that the human brain does not store a perfect objective copy.
default.q.n1-11-q65-65.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is inappropriate because the article says that human beings’ unique inventions arise from accepting and making use of noise or fluctuations, not from completely eliminating noise.
default.q.n1-11-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is 3. Intelligence should not be measured solely by accuracy or perfect memory; instead, we need to reassess the value of the original, flexible nature of human cognition, which includes both forgetting and fluctuation.
default.q.n1-11-q66-66.explanation:
- Main point: Throughout the passage, the author explains that imperfect memory (forgetting) and instability in neural networks (noise) are evolutionary adaptive strategies that enable humans to abstract concepts and think creatively. Therefore, in an age of AI striving for perfection, we need to properly reassess the value and richness of human cognition, which contains flexibility, forgetting, and fluctuation.
- Translation of the question: What does the author most want to assert throughout the passage?
- Translation of the answer choices:
  1. To compete with the development of artificial intelligence, humans should also train themselves to possess the enormous information-processing capacity and accuracy of digital computers.
  2. Since forgetting and neural noise are unavoidable defects in the evolutionary process, the task for the future is to overcome them through the power of science and technology.
  3. Perfect memory and accuracy should not be the only measures of intelligence; instead, we need to reassess the value of humans' flexible cognition, which includes forgetting and fluctuation.
  4. As the history of biological evolution indicates, all phenomena of life aim to completely eliminate ambiguity and always reach one optimal solution.
default.q.n1-11-q66-66.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is inappropriate because the author never recommends training people to achieve the precision or ability to process vast amounts of data that computers possess.
default.q.n1-11-q66-66.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is inappropriate because the author argues that forgetting and distraction are not defects that technology should remedy, but sophisticated evolutionary achievements of living organisms.
default.q.n1-11-q66-66.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is correct because it directly matches the final sentence of paragraph 4: 「無謬性を求める人工知能の発展が著しい現代だからこそ、私たちは、余分な情報を削ぎ落とし、ゆらぎを受け入れることで真理の輪郭を捉えようとする、人間本来の認知の豊かさを再評価する必要があるのだ。」 (Precisely because artificial intelligence, which seeks infallibility, is advancing rapidly today, we need to reevaluate the richness of human cognition—the ability to strip away excess information and embrace fluctuation in an attempt to grasp the contours of truth.)
default.q.n1-11-q66-66.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is inappropriate because the passage emphasizes that living organisms do not try to eliminate ambiguity in order to reach one optimal solution; they accept fluctuations and adapt flexibly to nature.
default.q.n1-11-q67-67.explanation:
- Main point: The passage indicates that the echo chamber phenomenon on social media cannot be blamed solely on technical flaws or on platforms and their algorithms. The core problem lies in the cognitive laziness of information consumers, who unconsciously seek only the comfort of agreement, accept information without sufficient consideration, and easily reject opposing views.
- Translation of the question: What does the author identify as the primary cause of information bias on social media, such as the echo chamber phenomenon?
- Translation of the answer choices:
  1. It is caused not only by information-filtering systems but also by the psychology of users who uncritically seek opinions that are pleasant to hear.
  2. It is caused by platforms intentionally creating social division and therefore using algorithms that distribute only biased information.
  3. It is caused by users making excessive efforts to completely refute differing opinions and reach agreement through sheer willpower.
  4. It is caused by a shortage of information in modern society, leaving users without enough material to make appropriate judgments.
default.q.n1-11-q67-67.why.0: (a) Correct. The author points out that the underlying cause is not merely the system, but people's cognitive laziness and desire to accept comforting affirmations: 「それを無批判に受容し、異質な意見を安易に排斥する態度の根底にあるのは、人間の持つ認知の怠惰さにほかならない。私たちは…精神的な安定をもたらす心地よい肯定のみを無意識に欲しているのである。」
default.q.n1-11-q67-67.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Paragraph 1 states that algorithms optimize according to user preferences, and the author says it is premature to place all responsibility on the platform side (「プラットフォーム側の責任として片付けてしまうのは早計」); the text does not say that platforms “intentionally cause social division.”
default.q.n1-11-q67-67.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Paragraph 2 points out that users tend to “easily reject opinions that differ from their own” (「異質な意見を安易に排斥する」) in search of reassurance, rather than trying to debate in order to reach agreement.
default.q.n1-11-q67-67.why.3: (d) Incorrect. Paragraph 3 states that today’s society is an age in which information is excessively abundant (「情報が過剰に氾濫する現代」), not an age suffering from a lack of information.
default.q.n1-11-q68-68.explanation:
- Main point: The author emphasizes that in an age of information explosion, the most important solution is not simply to rely on system-side controls or technical improvements. Rather, each recipient must develop "intellectual load-bearing capacity": the ability to question one's own beliefs and proactively and persistently face opinions that conflict with or disadvantage oneself.
- Question translation: What does the author advocate as most important in modern information society?
- Answer choices:
  1. Quickly promote legal regulations and technical improvements to prevent algorithmic manipulation of information.
  2. Efficiently select only information that reinforces one's own views in order to maintain emotional stability.
  3. Prioritize reaching agreement with others and avoid disagreement and friction of opinion as much as possible.
  4. Question one's own beliefs and develop intellectual perseverance so as to face even opinions that are unfavorable to oneself.
default.q.n1-11-q68-68.why.0: (a) Incorrect. In the final part, the author rejects relying solely on regulations or technology: 「単なるシステム側の規制や技術的改善に頼ることではない。」
default.q.n1-11-q68-68.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Selecting only information that reinforces one’s beliefs in order to maintain emotional stability is precisely an example of the “cognitive laziness” (「認知の怠惰」) criticized by the author.
default.q.n1-11-q68-68.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The author emphasizes that the true value of receiving information lies in experiencing the “friction” that shakes one’s preconceptions (「自己の前提や信念を揺さぶる『摩擦』を経験すること」), not in reaching easy agreement or avoiding friction.
default.q.n1-11-q68-68.why.3: (d) Correct. It precisely matches the core message in the final sentence of the passage: 「自己の確信を疑い、時には不都合な言説にすら進んで向き合おうとする、受け手側の主体的な知的負荷への耐性を養うことなのではないだろうか。」
default.q.n1-11-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 4. もうれつ (猛烈: intense, fierce, violent).
default.q.n1-11-q1-1.explanation: Meaning: I was extremely angry at that attitude. Sino-Japanese roots: 猛 (fierce) + 烈 (violent) = 猛烈 (intense, fierce). Another example: 猛烈な勢いで台風が接近している。(The typhoon is approaching with great intensity.)
default.q.n1-11-q1-1.why.0: (a) 「もれつ」: Incorrect kanji reading. 猛 has the on-readings 「もう」 or 「みょう」, not the short sound 「も」 in this word.
default.q.n1-11-q1-1.why.1: (b) 「きょうれつ」: Incorrect kanji. This reading belongs to 「強烈」, meaning “intense, powerful.”
default.q.n1-11-q1-1.why.2: (c) 「きょれつ」: Incorrect kanji reading. 猛烈 does not have this reading.
default.q.n1-11-q1-1.why.3: (d) 「もうれつ」: Correct. 猛 (もう) + 烈 (れつ) = 猛烈 (もうれつ), meaning fierce, intense, or vehement.
default.q.n1-11-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 4. こくふく (克服: to overcome, conquer, or prevail over difficulties or illness).
default.q.n1-11-q2-2.explanation: Sentence meaning: She overcame her illness and returned to work. Kanji note: 克服 means to overcome difficulties. Another example: 困難を克服して成功を収めた。(He overcame difficulties and achieved success.)
default.q.n1-11-q2-2.why.0: (a) 「こうふく」: Incorrect kanji. This is the reading of 「降伏」 (surrender) or 「幸福」 (happiness).
default.q.n1-11-q2-2.why.1: (b) 「かくふく」: Incorrect kanji reading. 克 (KHẮC) does not have the on-reading 「かく」.
default.q.n1-11-q2-2.why.2: (c) 「かいふく」: Incorrect kanji. This reading belongs to 「回復」, meaning recovery of health or the economy.
default.q.n1-11-q2-2.why.3: (d) 「こくふく」: Correct. 克 (こく) + 服 (ふく) = 克服 (こくふく: to overcome, conquer).
default.q.n1-11-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is 2. くずれやすい (崩れる: to collapse, fall apart, or lose its original shape).
default.q.n1-11-q3-3.explanation: Meaning: This item is very fragile and easily loses its shape, so please be careful when transporting it. Sino-Japanese roots: 崩 (to collapse, crumble, become deformed). Another example: 大雨で山が崩れた。(The mountain collapsed because of heavy rain.)
default.q.n1-11-q3-3.why.0: (a) 「つぶれやすい」: Incorrect kanji. This reading belongs to 「潰れやすい」, meaning easy to be crushed, flattened, or driven out of business.
default.q.n1-11-q3-3.why.1: (b) 「くずれやすい」: correct. 崩れる (くずれる: to collapse, crumble, or lose its shape) combines with やすい to form 崩れやすい (easy to collapse, break apart, or become deformed).
default.q.n1-11-q3-3.why.2: (c) 「はがれやすい」: Incorrect kanji. This reading corresponds to 「剥がれやすい」(easy to peel or come off).
default.q.n1-11-q3-3.why.3: (d) 「こぼれやすい」: Incorrect kanji. This is the reading of 「零れやすい / 溢れやすい」(likely to spill or fall out).
default.q.n1-11-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 1. はんしょく (繁殖: reproduction, breeding, propagation).
default.q.n1-11-q4-4.explanation: Meaning of the sentence: This medicine inhibits the reproduction of viruses. Kanji components: 繁 (HAN, abundance) + 殖 (SHOKU, reproduction) = 繁殖 (はんしょく, reproduction, proliferation). Another example: 春になると動物たちが繁殖期を迎える。(When spring arrives, animals enter their breeding season.)
default.q.n1-11-q4-4.why.0: (a) 「はんしょく」: Correct. 繁 (はん) + 殖 (しょく) = 繁殖 (はんしょく: reproduction, multiplication).
default.q.n1-11-q4-4.why.1: (b) 「はんちょく」: Incorrect reading of the kanji. 殖 (SHOKU) is read as 「しょく」, not 「ちょく」.
default.q.n1-11-q4-4.why.2: (c) 「ばんしょく」: Incorrect kanji reading. 繁 (PHỒN) is read 「はん」, not 「ばん」 through sound change.
default.q.n1-11-q4-4.why.3: (d) 「ばんちょく」: Both kanji are read incorrectly. 繁 is 「はん」and 殖 is 「しょく」.
default.q.n1-11-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is 3. りれき (履歴: history, personal record, traces left behind).
default.q.n1-11-q5-5.explanation: Meaning: The website browsing history was no longer being saved. Kanji components: 履 (to go through/wear shoes) + 歴 (passage through) = 履歴 (a record, history). Another example: アルバイトの応募のために履歴書を書いた。(I wrote a résumé to apply for a part-time job.)
default.q.n1-11-q5-5.why.0: (a) 「ふくれき」: Incorrect kanji reading. 履 (LÍ) does not have the reading 「ふく」.
default.q.n1-11-q5-5.why.1: (b) 「られき」: Incorrect kanji reading. 履 does not have the reading 「ら」.
default.q.n1-11-q5-5.why.2: (c) 「りれき」: Correct. 履 (LÍ - り) + 歴 (LỊCH - れき) = 履歴 (りれき: history, personal record).
default.q.n1-11-q5-5.why.3: (d) 「ふうれき」: Incorrect kanji reading. 履 (LÍ) does not have the reading 「ふう」.
default.q.n1-11-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 2. はえる (映える: to shine brilliantly, stand out, enhance the beauty).
default.q.n1-11-q6-6.explanation: Meaning: I took a photograph of the mountain glowing a brilliant red in the sunset. The Sino-Japanese reading of 映 is Ánh (to reflect or stand out beautifully). Another example: 青空に白い雲が美しく映える。(The white clouds stand out beautifully against the blue sky.)
default.q.n1-11-q6-6.why.0: (a) 「そびえる」: Incorrect kanji. This is the reading of 「聳える」(to tower, rise high).
default.q.n1-11-q6-6.why.1: (b) 「はえる」: Correct. 映える (はえる) means to shine brilliantly or stand out attractively.
default.q.n1-11-q6-6.why.2: (c) 「もえる」: Incorrect kanji. This is the reading of 「燃える」 (to burn, burst into flames) or 「萌える」 (to sprout).
default.q.n1-11-q6-6.why.3: (d) 「さえる」: Incorrect kanji. This is the reading of 「冴える」 (clear, alert, sharp-minded).
default.q.n1-11-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 3. センサー.
default.q.n1-11-q7-7.explanation:
Sentence meaning: “When gas leaks, the sensor detects it and the alarm sounds.”
・Related vocabulary: 感知（かんち）: to sense or detect; 警報（けいほう）: warning alarm; 漏れる（もれる）: to leak.
・Additional example: 火災センサーが煙を感知してスプリンクラーが作動した。(The fire sensor detected smoke, and the sprinklers were activated.)
default.q.n1-11-q7-7.why.0: (a) 1. レーダー (radar): A device that locates objects using radio waves, commonly used to detect ships, aircraft, or weather—not gas leaks inside a house.
default.q.n1-11-q7-7.why.1: (b) 2. モーター (motor): An electric motor used to create mechanical movement; it does not sense or detect gas.
default.q.n1-11-q7-7.why.2: (c) 3. センサー (sensor): a sensing device capable of detecting changes in the environment (temperature, smoke, gas, etc.). It is highly appropriate in the context of “a sensor detecting a gas leak.”
default.q.n1-11-q7-7.why.3: (d) 4. レバー (lever): a manually operated lever or handle for mechanical control, not an automatic sensor device that activates an alarm bell.
default.q.n1-11-q8-8.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 壮大な (grand, magnificent, large-scale—often used for dreams or plans).

- Distinction from 「様子」(the concrete appearance or condition of a person or thing in everyday situations) and 「気配・兆し」(a sign or indication).
- Example: 激しい選挙戦は、混戦の様相を呈している。(The fierce election campaign is taking on the appearance of a complicated, closely contested race.)
default.q.n1-11-q24-24.why.0: Incorrect usage: To indicate that there is no sign of the abdominal pain easing, use 「気配」 (けはい) or 「兆し」 (きざし), as in 腹痛が治まる気配がない, not 「様相」.
default.q.n1-11-q24-24.why.1: This is incorrect: To record a child’s appearance and development as they grow day by day, use 「成長の様子」, 「成長の過程」, or 「成長の姿」, not 「様相」.
default.q.n1-11-q24-24.why.2: 「社会の様相」 (“the appearance, overall picture, or state of society”) is a formal and accurate collocation for referring to the social conditions of an era.
default.q.n1-11-q24-24.why.3: Incorrect usage: To investigate the atmosphere or actual conditions at a workplace, use 「職場の雰囲気」, 「職場の実態」, or 「職場の様子」, not 「様相」.
default.q.n1-11-q25-25.explanation:
「交える」（まじえる - Giao）: a transitive verb meaning to mix in or incorporate something, such as emotions, jokes, or gestures, while speaking or carrying out an action; it can also mean to cross or interweave, as in crossing swords or exchanging glances.
- Common collocations: 「冗談・ユーモアを交える」(to add jokes or humor), 「私情を交えずに判断する」(to make a judgment without allowing personal feelings to interfere), 「身振り手振りを交えて説明する」(to explain while using gestures), 「視線を交える」(to exchange glances).
- Example: 専門用語ばかりでなく、具体例を交えて説明すると分かりやすい。(It is easier to understand if you explain things with specific examples rather than using only technical terms.)
default.q.n1-11-q25-25.why.0: Incorrect usage: When including the period of part-time work in the total, use 「含めると」 or 「合わせると」, not 「交えると」.
default.q.n1-11-q25-25.why.1: Correct usage: 「冗談を交える」 (to mix in jokes or humorous remarks) is a highly appropriate collocation for describing the inclusion of something in a conversation or meeting atmosphere.
default.q.n1-11-q25-25.why.2: Incorrect usage: When putting one's wholehearted effort and feelings into knitting a sweater, use 「心を込めて」(こころをこめて), not 「心を交えて」.
default.q.n1-11-q25-25.why.3: Incorrect usage: When presenting a bouquet with a congratulatory card or message attached, use「メッセージを添えて」(そえて) or「メッセージを添えた」, not「交えて」.
default.q.n1-11-q26-26.verdict: The correct answer is 2. こそ (the structure 「〜こそ…が／けれど」 expresses concession: “although..., ...”).
default.q.n1-11-q26-26.explanation:
- Sentence translation: Although he missed out on the championship, Ishikawa achieved an excellent result in this tournament by setting a new personal best.
- Grammar pattern: `N / V-stem + こそ + [verb] + が／けれど` (Although... / Even though...). It acknowledges an incomplete or unfavorable fact in the first clause in order to highlight a positive point in the second clause.
- Vocabulary and kanji:
  - 優勝 (ゆうしょう): championship, victory.
  - 逃す (のがす): to miss, let slip away.
  - 自己ベスト (じこベスト): personal best.
  - 更新 (こうしん): update, break a record.
  - 成績を収める (せいせきをおさめる): achieve a result.
- Example: 苦戦こそしたが、最終的には試合に勝つことができた。(Although we struggled, we were ultimately able to win the match.)
default.q.n1-11-q26-26.why.0: (a) 「〜さえ」means “even,” introducing an extreme example. In this context, it does not create the contrastive structure 「〜さえ〜が」.
default.q.n1-11-q26-26.why.1: (b) 「〜こそ」combines with 「〜が／けれど」in the structure 「〜こそ…が」, meaning “although...,” acknowledging the first clause in order to emphasize the positive point that follows.
default.q.n1-11-q26-26.why.2: (c) 「〜ほど」 means “to the extent of,” “approximately,” or “about”; it is not used to connect contrastive, concessive clauses.
default.q.n1-11-q26-26.why.3: (d) 「〜ばかり」 means “only” or “just recently,” so it does not fit the meaning or structure of this sentence.
default.q.n1-11-q27-27.verdict: The correct answer is 3. ことだから (used to state a reason or circumstance supporting the plan in the following clause: “Because..., therefore...” ).
default.q.n1-11-q27-27.explanation:
- **Translation of the sentence:** Since my son, who is studying abroad, will also be coming home during this New Year’s holiday, I am thinking that perhaps the whole family should take a trip together after being apart for such a long time.
- **Grammar pattern:** `V in the plain form + ことだから`: Here, it gives an objective reason or background serving as the basis for a suggestion or plan (= 〜ことだし / 〜のだから).
- **Vocabulary and kanji readings:**
  - 正月休み (しょうがつやすみ): New Year’s holiday.
  - 留学 (りゅうがく): studying abroad.
  - 久しぶり (ひさしぶり): after a long time.
  - 家族旅行 (かぞくりょこう): family trip.
- **Example:** 来週は連休でもあることだから、どこか遠くへ出かけよう。(Since next week is also a long holiday, let’s go somewhere far away.)
default.q.n1-11-q27-27.why.0: (a) 「〜ことだが」 means “it is a matter of..., but...” and is used to make a transition or express contrast. It is unsuitable for stating the reason for the plan in the following clause.
default.q.n1-11-q27-27.why.1: (b) 「〜ことでも」 means “even if it is ...” or “even something like ...”; it is not used to express a cause or reason.
default.q.n1-11-q27-27.why.2: (c) 「〜ことだから」: Used to give a reason or factual circumstance as the basis for explaining the plan for the whole family to travel together.
default.q.n1-11-q27-27.why.3: (d) 「〜こととはいえ」 means “although it is...” and is used for concession. It does not fit the cause-and-intention logic here.
default.q.n1-11-q28-28.verdict: The correct answer is 4. どうやら (This adverb combines with 「〜ようだ」to express an inference based on observed evidence: “it seems” or “apparently.”)
default.q.n1-11-q28-28.explanation:
- Sentence translation: My older brother has just returned from a job interview. Judging from his radiant expression, it seems that everything went smoothly.
- Grammar pattern: The adverb `どうやら〜ようだ／らしい` means “apparently” or “it seems that.” It is used to make an inference based on observable signs or clues.
- Vocabulary and kanji:
  - 採用 (さいよう): recruitment, hiring.
  - 面接試験 (めんせつしけん): interview examination, job interview.
  - 表情 (ひょうじょう): facial expression.
  - 〜ところを見ると: judging from the sign that...
- Example: 外が騒がしいところを見ると、どうやら事故が起きたようだ。(Judging from the noise outside, it seems that an accident has occurred.)
default.q.n1-11-q28-28.why.0: (a) 「仮に（かりに）」 means “assuming” or “supposing” and commonly pairs with hypothetical conditional structures such as 「〜たら」「〜ても」 and 「〜ば」. It does not go with 「〜ようだ」.
default.q.n1-11-q28-28.why.1: (b) 「まさか」 means “surely not” or “it can’t be,” and is commonly used with a negative ending or negative conjecture such as 「〜ないだろう」 or 「〜わけがない」.
default.q.n1-11-q28-28.why.2: (c) 「必ずしも（かならずしも）」 means “not necessarily” or “not always” and is always used with a negative ending such as 「〜とは限らない」「〜ない」.
default.q.n1-11-q28-28.why.3: (d) 「どうやら」 means “apparently” or “it seems that” and combines with 「〜ようだ」 to make an inference based on observable signs, such as a bright facial expression.
default.q.n1-11-q29-29.verdict: The correct answer is 1. ものか (the pattern 「〜ないものか」 expresses a strong wish, desire, or a suggestion tinged with complaint: “Is there no way to...?”).
default.q.n1-11-q29-29.explanation:
- **Sentence translation**: The food at this restaurant really is delicious, but the dishes look cheap. I keep wondering whether they could use somewhat better tableware.
- **Grammar pattern**: `V-ない + もの（だろう）か` (Could they possibly...? / If only they could...?). It is often used with the negative potential form to express a strong wish, earnest hope, or complaint that one wants the situation to improve.
- **Vocabulary and kanji notes**:
  - 皿 (MÃNH - さら): dish, plate, tableware.
  - 安っぽい (AN - やすっぽい): cheap-looking, tacky.
- **Example**: この難病を治療する良い薬は開発できないものだろうか。(Could they possibly develop a good medicine to treat this serious disease?)
default.q.n1-11-q29-29.why.0: (a) 「〜ないものか」 expresses a strong wish or an earnest question about whether something can be improved (“Is there no way to …?”). Combining it with the negative potential form 「使えない」 is completely correct.
default.q.n1-11-q29-29.why.1: (b) 「〜ものの」: Means “although...,” connecting two contrasting clauses; in this sense, it does not come before 「と思う」.
default.q.n1-11-q29-29.why.2: (c) 「〜ものだ」 is used for truths, natural laws, moral advice, or recollections of the past; it does not express a desire for change here.
default.q.n1-11-q29-29.why.3: (d) 「〜ものを」 means “if only...” or “even though...,” expressing regret or reproach about something that has already happened. It does not combine with 「と思う」 in this context.
default.q.n1-11-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 書けてるじゃない (the colloquial form 「〜じゃない」is used to make an observation or compliment: “You can write it, can’t you?” / “You write really well.”).
default.q.n1-11-q30-30.explanation:
- Sentence translation:
  Teacher: "Kimura, I've read this report. You said you weren't good at summarizing, but you've written it quite well, haven't you?"
  Kimura: "Thank you, teacher."
- Grammar pattern: `V-ている + じゃない（か）`: Used in everyday spoken language to affirm an unexpected fact and express pleasantly surprised praise or admiration ("isn't it...!" / "you actually...!").
- Vocabulary:
  - レポート: report, term paper.
  - まとめる: to summarize, to compile.
  - けっこう: fairly, quite.
- Example: 初めて作った料理にしては、けっこうおいしくできてるじゃない。(For a dish you made for the first time, it turned out quite delicious!)
default.q.n1-11-q30-30.why.0: (a) 「書けてなきゃ」is a shortened form of 「書けていなければ（困る／いけない）」(if it cannot be written, that would be a problem / unacceptable). It expresses a required condition and is not used to praise a completed piece of writing.
default.q.n1-11-q30-30.why.1: (b) 「書けてたらいいね」: Means “It would be nice if you could write it,” expressing uncertainty about the result or a future wish. It does not fit a situation in which the teacher has already read and commented on it.
default.q.n1-11-q30-30.why.2: (c) 「書けてるじゃない」: This is an informal affirmative expression meaning “You write really well, don't you?” It conveys surprise and praise, so it fits the reply “Thank you, teacher” perfectly.
default.q.n1-11-q30-30.why.3: (d) 「書けてるかどうかだね」 means “what matters is whether it can be written, I suppose,” expressing uncertainty rather than praise.
default.q.n1-11-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is 1. とかで (a pattern expressing a reason based on information heard from others: “apparently because...” or “I hear it is due to...” ).
default.q.n1-11-q31-31.explanation:
- **Sentence translation**: The "Yamamura" udon shop in front of the station was apparently featured on television recently, so there is a long line in front of the shop every day.
- **Grammar pattern**: `[Plain-form clause] + とかで`: indicates a reason based on hearsay or unverified information (“apparently because... / I heard that it was because...").
- **Vocabulary and kanji**:
  - 駅前 (えきまえ): in front of the station.
  - 紹介 (しょうかい): introduction; being featured.
  - 行列ができる (ぎょうれつができる): to form a long line.
- **Example**: 田中さんは風邪を引いたとかで、今日の会議を欠席した。(Tanaka was absent from today’s meeting, apparently because he had caught a cold.)
default.q.n1-11-q31-31.why.0: (a) 「〜とかで」 follows a clause to give a cause based on indirectly heard information (“apparently because…”), which suitably explains the long line mentioned in the following clause.
default.q.n1-11-q31-31.why.1: (b) 「〜とかなら」is a hypothetical form meaning “if I hear that...”; it is not used to explain the cause of an actual event currently taking place.
default.q.n1-11-q31-31.why.2: (c) 「〜というのが」functions as the subject of the following clause (“the fact that it is called ...”); it is not used to indicate a cause.
default.q.n1-11-q31-31.why.3: (d) 「〜というのも」 usually begins a following sentence to explain the reason for the preceding sentence, often with 「〜からだ」. It cannot directly connect the sentences in this context.
default.q.n1-11-q32-32.verdict: The correct answer is 2. にもなっておらず (a pattern emphasizing complete negation, 「何のNにもならない／なっていない」: “it has not amounted to any explanation whatsoever”).
default.q.n1-11-q32-32.explanation:
- Sentence translation: The president held a press conference about this accident, but it did not explain anything at all; it only damaged our company's reputation.
- Grammar pattern: `何の + noun + にもならない／になっていない` means “to be of no use whatsoever” or “not to amount to anything.” `〜ておらず` is the formal connective negative form of `〜ていなくて`.
- Vocabulary and kanji:
  - 会見を行う (かいけんをおこなう): to hold a press conference.
  - 信用が失われる (しんようがうしなわれる): to lose credibility.
- Example: そんな言い訳は何の解決にもならず、かえって事態を悪化させるだけだ。(Such an excuse solves nothing; on the contrary, it only makes the situation worse.)
default.q.n1-11-q32-32.why.0: (a) 「になっておらず」: The particle 「も」must accompany 「何の〜」; the fixed pattern emphasizing complete negation is 「何の〜にもならない／なっていない」.
default.q.n1-11-q32-32.why.1: (b) 「にもなっておらず」: Correct. The structure 「何の〜にもならない／なっていない」means “does not become anything at all,” and 「〜ず」connects clauses in a formal style.
default.q.n1-11-q32-32.why.2: (c) 「になっているのではなく」means “it is not becoming...” It does not combine with the interrogative expression 「何の〜」, which conveys total negation, and does not fit the flow of the sentence.
default.q.n1-11-q32-32.why.3: (d) 「にもなっているのではなく」 is awkward grammar and does not successfully express a complete negation of the idea that the press conference provided a satisfactory explanation.
default.q.n1-11-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 来たり来なかったり (The structure 「〜たり〜たりだ」expresses irregular or alternating actions and states: “sometimes... and sometimes....”)
default.q.n1-11-q33-33.explanation:
- Sentence translation:
  Kobayashi: "Hey, Yamaguchi-san is coming to today's dance practice too, right?"
  Mori: "Who knows? Even if they say they will come, sometimes they show up and sometimes they don't, so..."
- Grammar pattern: `V1-たり + V2-たり + だ／です`: Describes actions that alternate repeatedly or an inconsistent state that changes from one way to another.
- Vocabulary:
  - ダンスの練習 (れんしゅう): dance practice.
  - どうだろう: I wonder / hard to say.
- Example: 最近の天気は雨が降ったり止んだりだから、傘を持って行ったほうがいい。(The weather has been alternating between rain and sunshine lately, so you should take an umbrella.)
default.q.n1-11-q33-33.why.0: (a) 「来ても来なくても」 means “whether someone comes or not” and introduces a concessive clause. It does not combine with the reason marker 「だから」 at the end of the sentence.
default.q.n1-11-q33-33.why.1: (b) 「来るか来ないか」means “whether someone will come or not.” It commonly occurs with 「わからない」 or 「決まっていない」, and is not used before 「だから」 to describe an unpredictable personality.
default.q.n1-11-q33-33.why.2: (c) 「来たり来なかったり」: the pattern 「〜たり〜たり（だ）」 expresses irregular alternation, “sometimes coming and sometimes not,” and combines perfectly with 「だから」 to give a reason.
default.q.n1-11-q33-33.why.3: (d) 「来るのも来ないのも」 means “both coming and not coming.” As a nominalized subject or predicate, it does not fit the meaning of explaining inconsistency.
default.q.n1-11-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 1. させられるところだった (the adverb 「危うく〜ところだった」 combines with the causative-passive form to mean “I almost ended up being forced to participate”).
default.q.n1-11-q34-34.explanation:
- Sentence translation: Yesterday, I was put under great pressure to join a university club. They kept forcefully pushing the conversation along, and I nearly ended up being pressured into signing up.
- Grammar:
  - Adverb `危うく（あやうく） + V-る + ところだった`: I almost... (indicates that a dangerous or unwanted event came very close to happening).
  - `V-（さ）せられる`: Causative-passive form (being forced or made to do something against one's will).
- Vocabulary and kanji readings:
  - 勧誘 (かんゆう): invitation, solicitation, recruitment.
  - 強引に (ごういんに): forcefully, coercively.
  - 入会 (にゅうかい): joining a club or organization.
- Example: スリップして危うく前の車に追突するところだった。 (I skidded and nearly rear-ended the car in front.)
default.q.n1-11-q34-34.why.0: (a) 「させられるところだった」: Combined with the adverb 「危うく」, it forms 「危うく〜ところだった」(I almost…). The passive causative 「入会させられる」(be forced to join) fits the context of being pressured into joining.
default.q.n1-11-q34-34.why.1: (b) 「されようがなかった」 means “there was no way for it to be done,” so it does not go with 「危うく」 and does not fit the logic of the sentence.
default.q.n1-11-q34-34.why.2: (c) 「させなかったのかと思った」: Means “I thought they had not let [someone] participate,” which does not fit the structure or the situation of being forced into the club.
default.q.n1-11-q34-34.why.3: (d) 「しなかったことにした」means “treated it as though one had not participated,” so it does not go with the adverb 「危うく」.
default.q.n1-11-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 入らなきゃいけないってわけじゃない (the pattern 「〜からって…わけじゃない」means “just because …, it does not mean that one must …”).
default.q.n1-11-q35-35.explanation:
- **Sentence translation**:
  Takahashi: “Hayashi, I heard you’re looking for a guitar class. Have you found one yet?”
  Hayashi: “No, I still haven’t found one.”
  Takahashi: “If you’d like, would you like to sit in on the guitar class I’m taking and see what it’s like? Even if you come to observe it, it doesn’t mean you have to sign up, so what do you think?”
- **Grammar pattern**: `〜からって + 〜わけじゃない／わけではない`: Even if..., that does not necessarily mean that... / it does not mean that one must... Used to deny an imposed or unwarranted conclusion.
- **Vocabulary and Sino-Vietnamese readings**:
  - 教室 (GIÁO THẤT - きょうしつ): classroom, class.
  - 見学 (KIẾN HỌC - けんがく): observation for learning, sitting in to see what a class is like.
  - 〜なきゃ（いけない）: colloquial shortened form of 「〜なければ（ならない／いけない）」 (must do something).
- **Example**: 失敗したからって、全てが終わったわけじゃない。(Just because you failed does not mean everything is over.)
default.q.n1-11-q35-35.why.0: (a) 「入りたがるだけじゃない」: means “not only want to enter” and does not combine with the partial negation structure following 「〜からって」.
default.q.n1-11-q35-35.why.1: (b) 「入らせないわけにはいかない」means “cannot refuse to let someone enter,” a compulsory double negative that contradicts the suggestion to feel free to go and take a look.
default.q.n1-11-q35-35.why.2: (c) 「入りたくないだけかもしれない」means “perhaps they simply do not want to go inside,” which does not fit the conversational role of Takahashi encouraging Hayashi to go and take a look.
default.q.n1-11-q35-35.why.3: (d) 「入らなきゃいけないってわけじゃない」 combines with 「〜からって」 to form 「〜からって…わけじゃない」 (“just because… does not mean that one must…”). It reassures the other person by relieving the pressure to enter.
default.q.n1-11-q36-36.verdict: The correct order is 1 → 4 → 2 → 3. The ★ position is the third slot, corresponding to answer choice 2 (診察できる).
default.q.n1-11-q36-36.explanation:
・ Complete sentence: X医院は、患者を待たせることなく診察できるように近々予約制を導入するらしい。
・ Meaning: Apparently, Clinic X will soon introduce an appointment system so that it can see patients without making them wait.
default.q.n1-11-q36-36.why.0: (a) 「待たせる」 follows the object 「患者を」 and combines with the grammar pattern 「～ことなく」 in (d) to form 「患者を待たせることなく」 (“without making the patients wait”), so it belongs in position 1.
default.q.n1-11-q36-36.why.1: (b) 「診察できる」 is the potential form of the verb and comes directly before the purpose pattern 「ように」 in (c), forming 「診察できるように」(so that one can examine patients). It belongs in position 3 (the ★ slot).
default.q.n1-11-q36-36.why.2: (c) 「ように」follows the potential verb 「診察できる」in (b) to indicate the purpose toward which the subsequent action (導入する) is directed, so it belongs in position 4.
default.q.n1-11-q36-36.why.3: (d) 「ことなく」 is a grammar pattern that follows the V-ru form (待たせる) and means “without doing V.” It modifies the following clause about receiving medical treatment and belongs in position 2.
default.q.n1-11-q37-37.verdict: The correct order is 4 → 2 → 3 → 1. The ★ position is the third position, corresponding to choice 3 (がちな).
default.q.n1-11-q37-37.explanation:
・ Complete sentence: 昨日、友人から野菜ジュースをたくさんもらった。一人暮らしだとインスタント食品ばかり食べてしまって野菜不足になりがちなだけにありがたい。
・ Meaning: Yesterday, I received a lot of vegetable juice from a friend. When you live alone, you tend to eat nothing but instant food and become deficient in vegetables, so this gift is especially appreciated.
default.q.n1-11-q37-37.why.0: (a) 「だけに」 is a grammar pattern meaning “precisely because…, all the more…” or “for that very reason,” connecting the noun/adjective phrase before it to the predicate 「ありがたい」; it belongs in the fourth position.
default.q.n1-11-q37-37.why.1: (b) 「になり」 is the continuative form of 「になる」. It follows 「野菜不足」 in (d) and modifies 「がちな」 in (c), forming 「野菜不足になりがちな」, so it belongs in the second position.
default.q.n1-11-q37-37.why.2: (c) 「がちな」is a grammar pattern that follows the continuative form of a verb (になり) and means “tend to” or “be prone to.” It modifies 「だけに」in (a) and belongs in the third position (the ★ blank).
default.q.n1-11-q37-37.why.3: (d) 「野菜不足」 is a compound noun placed before 「になり」 in (b), forming 「野菜不足になり」 (become deficient in vegetables). It follows 「インスタント食品ばかり食べてしまって」 and appears in position 1.
default.q.n1-11-q38-38.verdict: The correct order is 3 → 1 → 4 → 2. The ★ position is the third slot, corresponding to answer choice 4 (そうではなく).
default.q.n1-11-q38-38.explanation:
・ Complete sentence:
Q：洗剤をたくさん使ったほうが、洗濯物がきれいになりますか。
A：洗濯物をきれいに洗うには洗剤をたくさん入れればいいかといえばそうではなく、逆にすすぎ切れなかったりして悪臭の原因にもなります。適量を守りましょう。
・ Meaning:

Passage 3 clearly states the benefits of a side job (副業) for employees: 「社員にとっても本業を持ちながら第2のキャリアを築いたり、ローリスクで起業したり、メリットがある。」 (Employees can benefit by building a second career while keeping their main job, or by starting a business with low risk.) In other words, employees can try a new job or field with peace of mind while keeping their main job as a safety net.

**Question translation:**
According to the author, what is the benefit of a side job for employees?

**Answer choices:**
1. They can gain a wide range of experience while increasing their income.
2. By experiencing another career, they can rediscover the good points of their main job.
3. They have more opportunities to find work that suits them better than their main job.
4. With their main job as a foundation, they can try a new job with peace of mind.

default.q.n1-12-q54-54.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage only discusses building a second career or starting a business; it does not mention finding work “better suited to oneself than one’s main job” (本業よりも自分に向いている仕事).
default.q.n1-12-q54-54.why.3: (d) Correct because Passage 3 states: 「社員にとっても本業を持ちながら第2のキャリアを築いたり、ローリスクで起業したり、メリットがある。」 (For employees, it is also beneficial to build a second career while maintaining their primary job or to start a business with low risk.) 「本業を持ちながら」corresponds to “while using one's primary job as a foundation,” and 「ローリスクで起業したり」(starting a business with low risk) corresponds to “being able to try new work with confidence.”

(According to the author, what is required of employees who have a side job?)
- **Choices:**

Because elderly people have a wealth of life experience, they can take in large amounts of information, and their minds are filled with memories, while real life brings peace of mind (平安). In contrast, young people often feel empty (空虚), unstable, and bewildered because their dreams have not yet taken shape.
- **Note on the mismatch:** The excerpt contains no content or keywords related to "side jobs" (副業) or "employees" (社員). Question 55 was paired with the wrong passage, so the analysis and review retain the provided answer (3).

default.q.n1-12-q55-55.why.1: (b) 2. 本業に対しても常に意欲を失わないこと: Does not match. The passage does not mention one's attitude toward or motivation for one's main job while working a side job.
default.q.n1-12-q55-55.why.2: (c) 3. 何のために副業をするのかを明確に自覚すること: According to the provided answer key, the answer is 3. However, the quoted passage contains no discussion of side jobs (副業) or company employees, indicating a mismatch between the passage and the question provided.
