default.q.n1-17-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 飛び出してきたのだろう.
default.q.n1-17-q41-41.explanation:
【Meaning】「〜のだろう」(or 〜のだろうか / のだろうと思う) is used to make a judgment or supposition based on a specific situation or sign ("must be..." or "perhaps..."). With the past form 「〜たのだろう」, the pattern is used to speculate about the cause or reason for something that has happened.
【Structure】Plain form (普通形) + のだろう / んだろう (For na-adjectives and nouns: である / だ + のだろう, or な + のだろう).
【More examples】
・昨夜雨が降ったのだろう、道がまだ濡れている。(It must have rained last night; the road is still wet.)
・疲れていたのだろう、彼は電車に乗るなりぐっすり眠ってしまった。(He must have been exhausted, because he fell fast asleep as soon as he got on the train.)
default.q.n1-17-q41-41.why.0: (a) 「飛び出してくることもあった」 describes a habit or an event that occasionally occurred in the past (“there were also times when ...”), so it is unsuitable for inferring the reason for a specific situation being observed.
default.q.n1-17-q41-41.why.1: (b) 「飛び出してくるかもしれなかった」: Expresses a possibility that may have occurred in the past but is uncertain ("might have..."); it is unnatural when explaining an obvious actual state directly visible before one's eyes.
default.q.n1-17-q41-41.why.2: (c) 「飛び出してきたほどだ」indicates the degree of an event (“to the extent that...”); it is not appropriate at the end of a sentence to present a judgment or inference about a reason.
default.q.n1-17-q41-41.why.3: (d) 「飛び出してきたのだろう」uses the pattern 「〜たのだろう」to make a well-founded conjecture explaining the cause of a past event (“he must have rushed out of the house...”); it is highly accurate and natural.
default.q.n1-17-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 2. いたらなあ.
default.q.n1-17-q42-42.explanation:
【Meaning】「〜たらなあ」(similar to 〜たらいいなあ / 〜といいなあ / 〜ばいいなあ) is an emotive expression that reveals the speaker's wish or desire for something contrary to the present reality or difficult to achieve ("If only..." or "It would be wonderful if...").
【Structure】Conditional form (〜たら / 〜ば) + なあ / いいなあ.
【Another example】
・もっと若かったらなあ、いろんな国へ留学してみたかった。(If only I were younger, I would have liked to study abroad in various countries.)
・明日、大事な試合があるから晴れてくれたらなあ。(I have an important match tomorrow, so I hope the weather will be clear.)
default.q.n1-17-q42-42.why.0: (a) 「いたとしてもね」 expresses a concessive supposition ("even if it were there"). It cannot occur at the end of a sentence to express a desire.
default.q.n1-17-q42-42.why.1: (b) 「いたらなあ」combines the conditional form 「〜たら」with the exclamatory particle 「なあ」to express a heartfelt wish for something contrary to reality (“If only there were someone by my side; that would be wonderful”), so it is completely accurate.
default.q.n1-17-q42-42.why.2: (c) 「いたとはなあ」: Expresses surprise and exclamation at a fact that has already happened (“I can't believe it was there/that it existed”), not a wish.
default.q.n1-17-q42-42.why.3: (d) 「いたんだけどね」is used to narrate a situation with a nuance of regret or an unfinished implication (“I was there, you know, but…”). It does not express the wish “if only there were someone.”
default.q.n1-17-q43-43.explanation:
【Meaning】「私」(わたし/わたくし) is the standard first-person pronoun in Japanese. It is used when the speaker or writer describes their own experiences, feelings, or actions.
【Usage in N1 questions】In narrative reading-comprehension and grammar passages, correctly identifying the viewpoint as the first-person narrator 「私」 helps the reader follow the author’s ongoing emotions and sequence of actions.
【Additional examples】
・その知らせを聞いたとき、私は自分の耳を疑った。(When I heard the news, I could hardly believe my ears.)
・私自身もその意見には強く賛同している。(I myself strongly agree with that opinion.)

default.q.n1-17-q43-43.why.1: (b) 「部下」is a noun meaning “subordinate.” It is not the appropriate subject for expressing the narrator’s direct experience and psychological reaction in this context.
default.q.n1-17-q43-43.why.2: (c) 「私」 is a first-person pronoun (“I”), appropriate for referring to oneself and accurately narrating the writer’s own actions and genuine feelings in a narrative.
default.q.n1-17-q43-43.why.3: (d) 「あの子」 refers to a third person, such as “that child” or “that person,” from an outside observer’s perspective, so it does not fit the sentence’s direct emotional flow.
default.q.n1-17-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 2. なのに.
default.q.n1-17-q44-44.explanation:
【Meaning】「なのに」is a contrastive conjunction meaning “and yet,” “even so,” or “despite that.” It is placed at the beginning of a sentence to connect two sentences when the second event is contrary to the expectation or natural consequence of the first, conveying disappointment, surprise, or reproach.
【Structure】[Sentence 1]. なのに、[Sentence 2].
【Another example】
・約束の時間はもう過ぎている。なのに、彼はまだ姿を見せない。(The appointed time has already passed. And yet, he still has not shown up.)
・あれほど注意しておいた。なのに、彼女はまた同じミスをしてしまった。(I warned her so carefully. Even so, she made the same mistake again.)
default.q.n1-17-q44-44.why.0: (a) 「すると」 is a conjunction indicating a natural consequence or temporal sequence (“then,” “and immediately...”); it is used when the second clause occurs naturally after the first and does not express contrast.
default.q.n1-17-q44-44.why.1: (b) 「なのに」 is a contrastive conjunction expressing a result that is completely contrary to the effort or expectations in the preceding sentence. It conveys regret and dissatisfaction ("and yet" / "even so") and is entirely appropriate.
default.q.n1-17-q44-44.why.2: (c) 「こうして、」is a conjunction indicating manner or continuation (“in this way / by doing this...”). It is used to conclude or smoothly continue a sentence, not to express contrast.
default.q.n1-17-q44-44.why.3: (d) 「それどころか」 means “on the contrary, even more so” or “far from that—in fact, it is worse,” emphasizing that a situation goes beyond ordinary expectations. It does not fit a regular contrast between sentences.
default.q.n1-17-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 1. あの若者だ.

【Meaning】The noun-predicate structure 「〜だ」, especially in the emphatic pattern 「〜のは、…だ」, clearly identifies and asserts the identity of the subject or the nature of an event ("The person who... is...").
【Use in the N1 test】It is often used at the end of a narrative passage or paragraph to highlight the central person or thing after a notable series of actions has been described.
【Additional examples】
・暗闇の中で私に手を差し伸べてくれたのは、あの若者だ。(The person who reached out to help me in the darkness was that young man.)
・この困難なプロジェクトを成功に導いたのは、他でもないあの若者だ。(The person who led this difficult project to success was none other than that young man.)

default.q.n1-17-q45-45.why.1: (b) 「あの若者だからか」: This expresses speculation or uncertainty about the reason (“Could it be because he is that young man?”), leaving the sentence hanging rather than forming a complete affirmative conclusion.

default.q.n1-18-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 効率的に働くことばかりを考えていると、自分にできる仕事しかしなくなる (If one thinks only about working efficiently, one ends up doing only the work one is capable of.)
default.q.n1-18-q46-46.explanation: The passage begins by presenting a common view among many senior colleagues: recognizing waste early, prioritizing tasks, and completing work quickly are intelligent and highly efficient ways of working. However (でも), the author immediately points out the underlying problem: 「仕事の判断軸が自分になる」 (one's own perspective becomes the standard for evaluating one's work). People become concerned only with “whether they themselves are working efficiently” and “whether they themselves can complete the assigned amount of work within the allotted time.” As a result (すると), 「できる範囲のこと、無理のないことに収まっていってしまう」 (they end up limiting themselves to what they can do and what does not overburden them). The author's main warning is therefore this: If we focus only on working efficiently, we will end up doing only tasks that are within our own capabilities, without taking on or challenging ourselves with more difficult responsibilities.
default.q.n1-18-q46-46.why.0: (a) Not appropriate. The passage does not say that a person cannot complete an assigned task if they fail to recognize waste. Instead, it criticizes the tendency to focus excessively on optimizing individual efficiency.
default.q.n1-18-q46-46.why.1: (b) Not appropriate. The passage uses 「仕事の判断軸が自分になる」to mean that work is evaluated according to one's own convenience or efficiency, not that one forces one's standards onto other people.
default.q.n1-18-q46-46.why.2: (c) Unsuitable. The passage does not say that the person does not understand what their assigned work is. Rather, the person chooses to do only what lies within their comfort zone and does not dare to go beyond their limits.
default.q.n1-18-q46-46.why.3: (d) Fully appropriate. The author points out that when work is measured only by whether one can do it in time or handle it physically, the inevitable result is 「できる範囲のこと、無理のないことに収まっていってしまう」(one ends up limiting oneself to what one can do without overexertion), which is equivalent to 「自分にできる仕事しかしなくなる」.

default.q.n1-18-q48-48.why.3: (d) Not suitable. This is a common assumption or belief presented in the passage for the author to challenge, and it is completely contrary to the author’s view.
default.q.n1-18-q49-49.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 感情と深くかかわりながらも、感情に縛られないようにする (To remain deeply connected to one’s emotions without being bound by them).

Paragraph 2 clearly states that, thanks to technological innovation—specifically, the author’s example of using a personal computer to write a thesis—the time and effort required to complete a task have been significantly reduced. default.q.n1-18-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 4. The common point between the study of history and the natural sciences is that both must provide evidence that other scholars can verify.
default.q.n1-18-q59-59.explanation:
**Main point of the passage and supporting basis:**
The author points out that in historiography, when presenting a new perspective or historical interpretation, one must provide solid historical evidence so that other historians can compare it with the evidence and critique it. The author emphasizes that this is exactly the same as in the natural sciences (such as physics and chemistry): when developing a new theory, a researcher must present the reasoning and logic in a form that other scholars can verify.

**Question and answer choices:**
- **Question:** According to the author, what do historiography and the natural sciences have in common?
- **Answer choices:**
1. The value of research is recognized through the presentation of a new theory.
2. Mutual criticism among scholars is essential for developing a new theory.
3. It is not easy to present evidence for a new theory in a verifiable form.
4. Evidence for a new theory must be presented so that other scholars can verify it.
default.q.n1-18-q59-59.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage does not mention that the value of research is recognized only when a new theory is presented (新説を示すことで認められること).
default.q.n1-18-q59-59.why.1: (b) Inaccurate. The passage only states that historians can criticize one another on the basis of historical evidence; it does not claim that mutual criticism is indispensable to developing new theories.
default.q.n1-18-q59-59.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage does not say that presenting verifiable evidence is “not easy” (容易ではない).
default.q.n1-18-q59-59.why.3: (d) Correct. The first paragraph states: 「歴史学では、史実の究明にはもちろんのこと、新しい歴史像を提示する時にも史料的根拠が必要です。そして、この史料的根拠を基盤とするがゆえに、歴史学者の歴史観は、相互に批判可能なものです。これは、物理や化学といった自然科学の世界で新理論を展開する場合に、その論拠、論理を他の学者にも検証可能な形で提示しなければならないことと同様です。」 When presenting a new historical perspective, historians need documentary evidence so that others can criticize it, just as natural scientists must present their grounds and logic in a form that other scholars can verify.

default.q.n1-18-q63-63.explanation:
- Main point and textual basis:
The author points out that works presented in incomplete forms or containing gaps require an internal act of supplementation by the viewer ("未完の形式や余白を孕む作品は、鑑賞者の内的な補完行為を不可欠とする"). This is not a passive reception of the author's one-way message; the work is completed only when viewers project their own experiences and sensibilities onto it ("観る者が自らの経験や感性を投影することで初めて作品が完成する"), creating a "creative complicity" ("創造的な共犯関係").

- Question translation:
According to the author, what kind of relationship arises between the viewer and a work "that contains an incomplete form or gaps"?

- Answer choice translations:
1. A relationship in which the viewer accurately understands the author's intentions conveyed through the work and faithfully receives the intended message.
2. A relationship in which the viewer participates in completing the work by filling its deficiencies with their own experiences and sensibilities.
3. A relationship in which the author and viewer use digital technology to create a perfect work together.
4. A relationship in which distortions and ambiguities in the work are eliminated and objective, uniform standards of beauty are shared.
default.q.n1-18-q63-63.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage rejects passively accepting a one-sided message from the author: 「作者の一方的な主張の受容ではなく」.
default.q.n1-18-q63-63.why.1: (b) Correct. The supporting passage states: 「これに対し、未完の形式や余白を孕む作品は、鑑賞者の内的な補完行為を不可欠とする。そこに生じるのは、作者の一方的な主張の受容ではなく、観る者が自らの経験や感性を投影することで初めて作品が完成するという、創造的な共犯関係である。」
default.q.n1-18-q63-63.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the article does not mention using digital technology to collaborate on creating a perfect work. Instead, the author criticizes digital perfection for eliminating space for dialogue.
default.q.n1-18-q63-63.why.3: (d) Incorrect because eliminating ambiguity and distortion to create uniform, flawless beauty, 「均質で非の打ち所のない美」, is a characteristic of digitized products, which the author contrasts with the beauty of imperfection and empty space.
default.q.n1-18-q64-64.verdict: The correct answer is 3: Beauty is not fixed in the object itself; it arises through interaction when the viewer uses their imagination to engage in dialogue with gaps and imperfections.
default.q.n1-18-q64-64.explanation:
- Main theme and textual basis:
The central theme of the article appears in the final paragraph: Beauty is not a fixed entity existing statically within a work; it is a dynamic event that emerges in the moment of interaction between the work and the subject facing it (“美とは、対象の中に静止した実体として存在するのではなく、作品とそれに対峙する主体の相互作用の瞬間に立ち現れる動的な出来事である”). Precisely in an age overflowing with information, we need to use our imagination to supplement what is missing from a work and regain the opportunity to engage in dialogue with ourselves.

- Translation of the question:
What does the author most strongly advocate in this passage?

- Translation of the answer choices:
1. The beauty of a work of art lies in standing before a work containing perfect information and objectively evaluating the author’s advanced expressive technique.
2. Modern digital technology improves the perfection of works, but on the other hand completely destroys the value of traditional East Asian aesthetics, such as the tea ceremony and ink wash painting.
3. Beauty is not fixed within the object itself; it emerges through interaction when the viewer uses imagination to engage in dialogue with gaps and imperfections.
4. In a modern society overflowing with information, viewers should eliminate subjective interpretation and passively accept only the facts fully stated in the work.
default.q.n1-18-q64-64.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author says that a perfect work containing complete information merely forces viewers into passive appreciation (「ただ受動的な鑑賞を強いるにすぎない」), not that artistic beauty consists of objectively evaluating technique.
default.q.n1-18-q64-64.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the author does not say that digital technology has completely eliminated the value of the tea ceremony or ink-wash painting, but uses them only as examples of traditional aesthetics that value imperfection and empty space.
default.q.n1-18-q64-64.why.2: (c) Correct. The supporting quotations from the passage are: 「美とは、対象の中に静止した実体として存在するのではなく、作品とそれに対峙する主体の相互作用の瞬間に立ち現れる動的な出来事である。」and「過剰な情報が溢れる現代だからこそ、私たちは自らの想像力を用いて作品の欠落を埋め、自己と対峙する契機を取り戻す必要がある。」
default.q.n1-18-q64-64.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the author opposes passive reception and emphasizes that viewers need to use their own imagination to fill in the gaps in the work (「私たちは自らの想像力を用いて作品の欠落を埋め…」).
default.q.n1-18-q65-65.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: Health management, originally a means of achieving a better life, has become an ultimate goal and an obligation that must be fulfilled.
default.q.n1-18-q65-65.explanation:
• Summary of paragraph 1: Paragraph 1 explains that modern public health has expanded its scope of management to include individual lifestyles, such as digitized records of diet, exercise, and sleep. A profound paradox arises when maintaining one's health, originally a "means of living," is transformed into an "ultimate goal" and a "social obligation."

• Translation of the question: What does the "profound paradox" in paragraph 1 mean?
• Translation of the answer choices:
1. As improvements in living conditions extend average life expectancy, the number of patients with lifestyle-related diseases, which are more difficult to treat than acute infectious diseases, is increasing.
2. Health management, originally a means of helping individuals live better lives, has become an absolute goal and an obligation that must be fulfilled.
3. Although people try to digitize and manage their daily habits to prevent illness, prioritizing individual freedom of choice makes these efforts ineffective.
4. As public systems such as the Health Promotion Act have been developed, individuals have lost the desire to take the initiative in maintaining their own physical health.
default.q.n1-18-q65-65.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is inaccurate because paragraph 1 only describes the historical shift in the structure of disease; the author does not call the increase in chronic diseases a “profound paradox.”
default.q.n1-18-q65-65.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because it matches the final sentence of paragraph 1 exactly: 「自らの健康を主体的に維持・管理することは、一見すると自己実現のための望ましい営みのように映るが、ここには『健康』そのものが生きるための手段から至上の目的に転化し、さらには個人の果たすべき社会的責務へと変貌していくという深刻なパラドックスが潜んでいる」 (Actively maintaining and managing one’s health may at first appear to be a desirable activity for self-actualization, but it conceals a serious paradox: “health” itself changes from a means of living into an ultimate goal and, moreover, transforms into a social responsibility that individuals are expected to fulfill).
default.q.n1-18-q65-65.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the passage does not mention the digitization of management being ineffective due to prioritizing individuals’ freedom to make decisions.
default.q.n1-18-q65-65.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the passage does not say that public systems cause individuals to lose the will or motivation to maintain their own health.
default.q.n1-18-q66-66.verdict: The correct answer is choice 1: Focusing only on an individual’s lack of effort causes the structural social problems underlying poor health to be overlooked, and society is no longer held accountable.
default.q.n1-18-q66-66.explanation:
• Summary of the main point of paragraph 2: The author criticizes the trend of "health supremacism," which treats illness as a moral failing caused by insufficient effort or self-management. When intervention focuses exclusively on individual habits, structural social factors such as poverty, overwork, and isolation are obscured, and society evades its responsibility to provide protection and support.

• Translation of the question: What problem arises when "the focus of intervention is narrowed entirely to an individual’s way of life"?
• Translation of the answer choices:
1. By focusing only on an individual’s lack of effort, the structural social problems underlying poor health are overlooked, and society’s responsibility is not called into question.
2. Because solving social problems such as poverty and long working hours is given too much priority, individuals are deprived of the opportunity to reconsider their own lifestyle habits.
3. For people who do not follow scientifically based numerical standards, social support and medical care are completely cut off institutionally.
4. Because information about health risks is left to individuals’ free will, society’s concern for preventing lifestyle-related diseases declines.
default.q.n1-18-q66-66.why.0: (a) Answer choice 1 is correct because the latter half of passage 2 states directly: 「こうした個人の責任を強調する言説が、疾病の背景にある貧困や長時間労働、社会的孤立といった構造的要因を不可視化してしまう点である。健康格差の本質は社会構造の歪みにあるにもかかわらず、介入の矛先がもっぱら個人の生活態度へと矮小化されることで、社会が果たすべき包摂の責任が免責されてしまうのだ」 (The more serious problem is that discourse emphasizing individual responsibility renders invisible structural factors behind illness, such as poverty, long working hours, and social isolation. Although the essence of health disparities lies in distortions in the social structure, narrowing intervention down to individuals' lifestyles allows society to evade its responsibility for inclusion.)
default.q.n1-18-q66-66.why.1: (b) Option 2 is inaccurate because the passage says that social issues such as poverty and excessive working hours are concealed, not that social issues are prioritized to the point of taking away opportunities to reconsider one’s lifestyle.
default.q.n1-18-q66-66.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is inaccurate because the text does not mention that people who fail to meet numerical standards are completely cut off from social assistance or medical treatment.
default.q.n1-18-q66-66.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the passage does not say that society's concern about disease prevention has faded; it criticizes society for avoiding responsibility by placing the entire burden on individuals.
default.q.n1-18-q67-67.verdict: The correct answer is choice 3: Health does not mean being completely free of illness or discomfort; it is a flexible foundation that supports a way of life imbued with personal values even when physical limitations exist.
default.q.n1-18-q67-67.explanation:
• Main point of paragraph 3: The author asserts that human beings are naturally fragile and vulnerable. Health is not a perfect numerical target or the complete absence of illness; rather, it is a flexible foundation that enables people to live according to their own values and connect with others despite physical limitations.

• Translation of the question: How does the author view "health" in paragraph 3?
• Translation of the answer choices:
1. Eliminating every risk through strict self-restraint and always maintaining bodily indicators at optimal standard levels.
2. Fully following medical techniques and public-health guidance to prevent the weakening and aging of the body at an early stage.
3. It is not the complete absence of illness or instability, but a flexible foundation that supports one's own way of life despite physical limitations.
4. A sense of psychological security gained by managing oneself to avoid criticism from others and fulfill one's social responsibilities.
default.q.n1-18-q67-67.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because it presents a one-sided way of measuring data that the author questions and refutes at the beginning of paragraph 3: 「病気や老いを完全に排除し、常に最適な数値を保ち続けることだけが人間の豊かさであろうか」 (Is maintaining optimal numerical values at all times while completely eliminating illness and aging the only form of human well-being?).
default.q.n1-18-q67-67.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is inaccurate because the author states that human beings are inherently vulnerable, and no matter how much restraint they exercise, they cannot completely avoid illness or physical decline (「どれほど節制を尽くしたところで、不条理な発病や身体の衰弱を完全に免れることはできない」).
default.q.n1-18-q67-67.why.2: (c) Answer choice 3 is correct because the author states directly in passage 3: 「健康とは、絶対的な無病状態を指すのではなく、時に不調や制約を抱えながらも、他者と関わり、自らの価値観に基づいて生きることを可能にする柔軟な状態を意味するはずである」「健康は生を支えるための土台であって、生そのものを従属させる支配者であってはならないのである」 (Health does not mean an absolute state of being free from illness. Rather, it should mean a flexible state that allows people to interact with others and live according to their own values, even while sometimes experiencing poor health or limitations... Health is a foundation that supports life, not a ruler to which life itself must be subordinated.)
default.q.n1-18-q67-67.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because managing oneself to avoid judgmental looks or to fulfill social obligations is a negative expression of the extreme-health trend criticized earlier in the passage, not the author's true definition of health.
default.q.n1-18-q68-68.verdict: The correct answer is choice 2: Public health should stop intervening mechanically in individual lifestyles and instead work to build a social foundation that enables everyone to live with dignity and address structural injustices.
default.q.n1-18-q68-68.explanation:
• Summary of the main point of the entire passage: The author criticizes health supremacism for turning health into an obligation and blaming individuals while concealing structural social injustice. The author calls on public health to abandon rigid, standardized surveillance and instead respect self-determination, build social foundations that protect human dignity, and rectify structural injustices.

• Translation of the question: What does the author most want to assert throughout the entire passage?
• Translation of the choices:
1. To prevent the increase in chronic diseases, the government should impose stricter lifestyle metrics on individuals and manage them thoroughly.
2. Rigid intervention in individuals' lifestyles should be ended, while efforts should be made to improve social foundations so that everyone can live with dignity and to remedy injustice.
3. The role of public health should be limited to preventing acute infectious diseases, while the prevention and management of lifestyle-related diseases should be left entirely to individual self-responsibility.
4. To eliminate health disparities, individuals should stop avoiding risks excessively and rely solely on their own efforts to overcome social prejudice.
default.q.n1-18-q68-68.why.0: (a) Answer choice 1 is incorrect because the author opposes the state imposing rigid, uniform standards and monitoring or correcting deviations in individual lifestyles (「画一的な規範を個人に押しつけ、逸脱を監視・矯正するようなパターナリズムではない」).
default.q.n1-18-q68-68.why.1: (b) Answer choice 2 is correct because the concluding message in the final paragraph provides the evidence: 「これからの公衆衛生に求められるのは、画一的な規範を個人に押しつけ、逸脱を監視・矯正するようなパターナリズムではない。真に目指すべきは、どのような健康状態にある個人であってもその尊厳が守られ、安心して生きられるような社会的基盤の整備である。個人の自己決定を尊重しつつ、健康を損なう構造的不公正の是正に注力することこそが、公衆衛生の本来の使命であると言えよう」(What public health will require in the future is not paternalism that imposes uniform norms on individuals and monitors and corrects deviations. What it should truly aim for is to build a social foundation in which every individual, regardless of their health condition, has their dignity protected and can live with peace of mind. Focusing on correcting structural injustices that harm health while respecting individual self-determination is precisely the true mission of public health.)
default.q.n1-18-q68-68.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because the author does not say that public health should be limited to acute infectious diseases or that chronic diseases should be left entirely to individual responsibility. Instead, the author calls on society to take structural responsibility.
default.q.n1-18-q68-68.why.3: (d) Answer choice 4 is inaccurate because the author emphasizes the responsibility to build social foundations and correct structural injustice, rather than requiring individuals to “overcome social prejudice through their own strength alone.”
default.q.n1-18-q69-69.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 「曖昧さ」 and 「冗長性」serve as motivation and opportunities for listeners to use their imagination to infer the other person’s inner world.
default.q.n1-18-q69-69.explanation:
- Main point: The author points out that in genuine human communication, ambiguity (multiple possible meanings) and redundancy (hesitation and silence) are not simply transmission errors. They encourage the listener to use their imagination fully in order to empathize with the speaker and grasp their inner intentions.
- Translation of the question: According to the author, what role do "ambiguity" and "redundancy" in language play?
- Translation of the choices:
  1. They accurately encode the speaker's intentions, enabling information to be shared without misunderstanding.
  2. They give the listener an opportunity to use their imagination to infer the other person's inner feelings.
  3. They ease friction and imperfect communication in dialogue, deepening the logical thinking of both sides.
  4. They slow the transmission of information, thereby preventing the recipient from consuming meaning unilaterally.
default.q.n1-18-q69-69.why.0: (a) Incorrect because this is the ideal of communication through digital tools presented in paragraph 1: eliminating ambiguity and communicating clearly without causing misunderstandings. It is completely contrary to the role of ambiguity and redundancy.
default.q.n1-18-q69-69.why.1: (b) Correct. Paragraph 2 states: 「言葉が持つ多義性や、発話に伴う逡巡や沈黙といった冗長性こそが、他者の内面に思いを馳せる契機を生み出しているのではないか」 (It may be precisely the polysemy of words and the redundancy of hesitation and silence accompanying speech that create opportunities to reflect on the inner lives of others) and 「解釈の揺らぎを含む言葉を前にしたとき、受け手は相手の意図を汲み取ろうと自らの想像力を総動員することになる」 (When faced with words open to varying interpretations, the recipient mobilizes all of their imagination in an attempt to understand the other person’s intention).
default.q.n1-18-q69-69.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the author regards ambiguity itself as “friction” (摩擦) and never mentions that it helps “relieve friction or deepen the two sides' logical thinking.”
default.q.n1-18-q69-69.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage does not discuss “slowing the speed of communication to prevent recipients from unilaterally consuming meaning”; “unilateral consumption of meaning” is the result of exchanging symbols that have been completely rationalized.
default.q.n1-18-q70-70.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The author argues that if we pursue efficiency single-mindedly and eliminate the uncertainty of language, we lose the opportunity to empathize deeply with others.
default.q.n1-18-q70-70.explanation:
- Main idea: The author asserts that genuine understanding is not merely the sharing of accurate information; it lies in a dialogic process through which both sides strive to narrow the gap in their understanding. If we pursue efficiency single-mindedly and eliminate the uncertainty of language, we will lose the opportunity to engage in dialogue and empathize deeply with others.
- Question translation: What does the author think about dialogue through language?
- Answer choices:
  1. We should eliminate all discrepancies in understanding by exchanging rational information thoroughly.
  2. We should overcome the uncertainty of language caused by advances in digital tools and aim for clearer communication.
  3. If we pursue efficiency alone and eliminate uncertainty, we will lose the opportunity to empathize deeply with others.
  4. To eliminate the gap between ourselves and others, we should prioritize conveying objective facts over emotional resonance.
default.q.n1-18-q70-70.why.0: (a) Incorrect, because the author argues that genuine understanding must be based on accepting an unbridgeable distance (「埋められない隔たりを前提としながらも…」), not on completely eliminating differences through rational information exchange.
default.q.n1-18-q70-70.why.1: (b) Incorrect because digital tools are making language less ambiguous, not creating ambiguity. The author opposes eliminating this ambiguity merely in exchange for straightforward communication.
default.q.n1-18-q70-70.why.2: (c) Correct. The final sentence of paragraph 3 states: 「効率の追求によって言葉からこの不確実性を奪い去ることは、一見すると合理的でありながら、実のところ他者と深く共鳴し合う対話の契機を自ら放棄することに他ならないのである」 (Removing this uncertainty from language in pursuit of efficiency may appear rational at first glance, but in fact it amounts to voluntarily giving up the opportunity for dialogue that resonates deeply with others).
default.q.n1-18-q70-70.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the author does not propose prioritizing the communication of objective truth over emotional resonance; instead, the author emphasizes deep empathy and resonance (深く共鳴し合う) in the process of dialogue.
default.q.n1-18-q1-1.verdict: The correct answer is 1. こうふん.
default.q.n1-18-q1-1.explanation:
- Translation: The audience was extremely excited by the wonderful final-round match.
- Kanji components: 興 (excitement) + 奮 (rousing) → 興奮 (こうふん): excitement, intense enthusiasm.
- Example: 試合の結果を知って、興奮のあまり夜も眠れなかった。(I was so excited when I learned the result of the match that I could not sleep at night.)
default.q.n1-18-q1-1.why.0: (a) 「こうふん」: Correct. 「興奮」 is correctly read as 「こうふん」 (the on-reading of 興 is こう, and that of 奮 is ふん).
default.q.n1-18-q1-1.why.1: (b) 「きょうふん」: Incorrect. 「興」 has the on-reading 「きょう」, as in 「興味」きょうみ, but in 「興奮」 it is read 「こう」.
default.q.n1-18-q1-1.why.2: (c) 「きょうぶん」: Incorrect. The reading of 「興」 is wrong, and the rendaku change of 「奮」 is also incorrect (ふん → ぶん).
default.q.n1-18-q1-1.why.3: (d) 「こうぶん」: Incorrect. 「奮」 is read 「ふん」 and does not undergo voicing to become 「ぶん」. It is easily confused with 「構文」 or 「公文」, both read こうぶん.
default.q.n1-18-q2-2.verdict: The correct answer is 2. となえた.
default.q.n1-18-q2-2.explanation:
- Meaning: This theory was first proposed by Mr. Suzuki 30 years ago.
- Kanji component: 唱 (SHOU) -> 唱える (となえる): to propose or advocate a theory or policy; to chant a prayer; to call out a slogan.
- Example: 彼は会議で思い切って異論を唱えた。(He boldly raised an opposing view at the meeting.)
default.q.n1-18-q2-2.why.0: (a) 「たたえた」: incorrect. This is the reading of 「称える／讃える」(to praise) or 「湛える」(to be filled with or brim with smiles or tears).
default.q.n1-18-q2-2.why.1: (b) 「となえた」: Correct. 「唱えた」is the past form of 「唱える」(となえる), meaning to advocate or propose a doctrine, or to chant.
default.q.n1-18-q2-2.why.2: (c) 「かなえた」: Incorrect. This is the reading of the verb 「叶えた」, meaning to fulfill a dream or wish.
default.q.n1-18-q2-2.why.3: (d) 「うったえた」: Incorrect. This is the reading of the verb 「訴えた」 (complained, sued, appealed, or appealed to someone’s emotions).
default.q.n1-18-q3-3.verdict: The correct answer is 3. へんせん.
default.q.n1-18-q3-3.explanation:
- Meaning: I researched the changes over time in the key industries of this region.
- 変遷: 変 means change and 遷 means transition; together, 変遷 means the changes and shifts that occur over time as eras and circumstances change.
- Example: 時代の変遷とともに、人々の価値観も変わってきた。(As the times have changed, people's values have gradually changed as well.)
default.q.n1-18-q3-3.why.0: (a) 「へんさん」: Incorrect. 「さん」 is the on-reading of 纂, as in 「編纂」へんさん (to compile), or of 産; it is not the reading of 遷.
default.q.n1-18-q3-3.why.1: (b) 「へんさい」: incorrect. 「さい」is the on-reading of 「済」, as in 「返済」へんさい (repayment), not the reading of 「遷」.
default.q.n1-18-q3-3.why.2: (c) 「へんせん」: Correct. The standard reading of 「変遷」 is 「へんせん」: 変 is read へん and 遷 is read せん.
default.q.n1-18-q3-3.why.3: (d) 「へんせい」: Incorrect. 「せい」 is the on-reading of 「成」, as in 「編成」へんせい (organization, structure), not the reading of 「遷」.
default.q.n1-18-q4-4.verdict: The correct answer is 4. あたいする.
default.q.n1-18-q4-4.explanation:
- Meaning: Sato's daily efforts deserve respect.
- Kanji note: 値 → 値する (あたいする): to be worth or deserve N, commonly used in 「〜に値する」.
- Example: この作品は一度じっくり鑑賞するに値する。(This work is worth taking the time to appreciate carefully at least once.)
default.q.n1-18-q4-4.why.0: (a) 「ちする」 is incorrect. The kanji 「値」 has the on-reading 「ち」, as in 「価値」(かち) and 「数値」(すうち), but the verb 「〜に値する」 is read 「あたいする」 using the kun-reading.
default.q.n1-18-q4-4.why.1: (b) 「ねする」: Incorrect. 「値」 has the kun-reading 「ね」 (as in 「値段」ねだん and 「値上げ」ねあげ), but the verb 「ねする」 does not exist.
default.q.n1-18-q4-4.why.2: (c) 「ちょくする」: Incorrect. 「ちょく」is the on-reading of 「直」(as in 「直する」); 「値」does not have this reading.
default.q.n1-18-q4-4.why.3: (d) 「あたいする」: Correct. The compound expression 「〜に値する」 is read 「あたいする」 and means “to deserve” or “to be worth.”
default.q.n1-18-q5-5.verdict: The correct answer is 2. ずいじ.
default.q.n1-18-q5-5.explanation:
- Meaning: Applications are accepted at any time on an ongoing basis, with no fixed application period.
- Kanji meaning: 随 (随: according to) + 時 (time) → 随時 (ずいじ): at any time, whenever necessary, as needed.
- Example: 最新情報はホームページで随時更新しています。(The latest information is updated regularly on the website.)
default.q.n1-18-q5-5.why.0: (a) 「じゅうじ」: Incorrect. 「随」 has been confused with 「従」, as in 「従事」じゅうじ: to engage in, work in.
default.q.n1-18-q5-5.why.1: (b) 「ずいじ」: Correct. 「随時」 is correctly read 「ずいじ」 (随: ずい, 時: じ).
default.q.n1-18-q5-5.why.2: (c) 「すいじ」: Incorrect. 「随」is read with the voiced sound「ずい」, not the unvoiced「すい」, which is easily confused with「炊事」すいじ (cooking).

default.q.n1-18-q21-21.why.1: Correct because 「現実味を帯びる」is a standard idiom meaning that an idea or plan becomes realistic and highly feasible.
default.q.n1-18-q21-21.why.2: Incorrect because possessing a qualification or certificate is expressed with 「資格を持っている / 有している / 取得している」, not 「資格を帯びる」.

default.q.n1-18-q22-22.explanation:
「軌道（きどう）」: orbit; figuratively, a course, track, or process of development. Common fixed expressions: 「軌道に乗る」 (get on track, settle into a stable course), 「軌道を修正する / 軌道修正」 (correct the course or plan).

default.q.n1-18-q22-22.why.1: This is incorrect: For an action that deviates from a work plan or schedule, or an action taken without permission, use 「予定から外れた行動」 or 「勝手な行動」, not 「軌道」.
default.q.n1-18-q22-22.why.2: Correct because 「軌道を修正する（軌道修正する）」is a standard expression meaning to adjust one’s direction, policy, or plan; here, it means changing the business policy toward downsizing.

「思い詰める（おもいつめる）」: to brood, become consumed by negative thoughts, or agonize so deeply that one feels trapped and distressed. It is often used in forms such as 「思い詰めた表情 / 顔 / 様子」 or in advice such as 「そんなに思い詰めないで」(Don’t brood over it so much).

default.q.n1-18-q23-23.why.1: Correct because 「思い詰めた表情」 is a natural and precise expression describing a face weighed down by deep anxiety, distress, and a sense of being trapped.
default.q.n1-18-q23-23.why.2: Incorrect because concentrating intensely to solve a math problem is expressed with 「考え抜いて」 or 「頭をひねって」, not 「思い詰める」, which refers to personal distress or desperation.
default.q.n1-18-q23-23.why.3: Incorrect because putting all one’s heart and effort into making cakes is expressed with 「心を込めて / 一生懸命」, not 「思い詰める」.

Example: 被害が拡大し、もはや住民の避難を遅らせることはできない。(The damage is spreading, and we can no longer delay evacuating the residents.)

default.q.n1-18-q25-25.explanation:
「甚だしい（はなはだしい）」: extremely severe, excessive, or egregious (indicating a degree that is very serious, beyond the normal range, and usually negative or abnormal). Common combinations: 勘違いも甚だしい (a gross misunderstanding), 破損・劣化・被害が甚だしい (severe damage/deterioration/loss), 甚だしい無礼 (extreme rudeness).
Example: 現場の安全管理を怠った会社の責任は甚だしい。(The company bears extremely serious responsibility for neglecting safety management at the site.)
default.q.n1-18-q25-25.why.0: Incorrect because when internationalization progresses rapidly or dramatically, 「急速な / 目覚ましい」 is used; 「はなはだしい」 generally carries a negative or abnormal nuance and is not used to praise development.
default.q.n1-18-q25-25.why.1: Incorrect because an exceptionally high level of popularity, in a positive sense, is expressed as 「すさまじい人気」 or 「絶大な人気」, not 「人気がはなはだしい」.
default.q.n1-18-q25-25.why.2: Incorrect because strenuous or intense exercise is expressed as「激しい運動」, not「はなはだしい運動」.
default.q.n1-18-q25-25.why.3: Correct because 「はなはだしい」 is appropriately used to indicate an exceptionally severe degree of a negative phenomenon, and naturally combines with 「破損や劣化がはなはだしい」 (the damage and deterioration are extremely severe).
default.q.n1-18-q26-26.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 大人は大人で (adults have their own difficulties as adults).

default.q.n1-18-q28-28.verdict: The correct answer is 1. いっさい (not at all, absolutely not).
default.q.n1-18-q28-28.explanation:
• Translation: At my company, bringing any work-related data or documents outside the company is strictly prohibited, regardless of the reason.
• Sino-Japanese vocabulary: 一切 (issai — entirely, absolutely), 業務 (gyōmu — work, business operations), 資料 (shiryō — materials, documents).
• Grammar: The adverb 「いっさい (一切)」 is always used with the negative form 「〜ない」 and means “not at all” or “absolutely not.”

default.q.n1-18-q28-28.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「かならず (必ず)」 means “certainly” or “without fail” and normally accompanies an affirmative statement, command, or judgment. It cannot combine with a negative form to mean an absolute prohibition.
default.q.n1-18-q28-28.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「どうしても」 means “no matter what” or “desperately want to / cannot,” and is not used for an organization-wide prohibition.
default.q.n1-18-q29-29.verdict: The correct answer is 3. にしてみれば (from the perspective of / for the local residents).

default.q.n1-18-q29-29.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「〜といっても」 means “although one says...,” adding a limitation or qualification to the preceding statement.
default.q.n1-18-q29-29.why.2: (c) Correct because the grammar 「〜にしてみれば」means “from the standpoint or perspective of ...,” which fits saying that, for local residents, the seaside scenery is simply an ordinary part of daily life.
default.q.n1-18-q29-29.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「〜はともかくとして」 means “setting ... aside for now” or “putting ... aside,” which does not fit the meaning.
default.q.n1-18-q30-30.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 抜かずに済むものなら (If it were possible not to have it pulled, I would prefer that).
default.q.n1-18-q30-30.explanation:
• Translation: Next week, I am scheduled to have a tooth extracted at the dentist's. If I could avoid having it extracted, I certainly would, but I hear there is no other way.

default.q.n1-18-q30-30.why.0: (a) Incorrect because 「〜と」expresses a natural condition or inevitable result and cannot be combined with a following clause expressing an unrealized wish, 「〜たい」.
default.q.n1-18-q30-30.why.1: (b) Incorrect because 「〜ことで」 indicates a means or cause; it does not form a hypothetical conditional expressing a desired situation.
default.q.n1-18-q30-30.why.2: (c) Incorrect because 「〜のだから」 (“because ...”) gives a reason for an already known fact, which conflicts with the fact that the tooth extraction is actually required next week.
default.q.n1-18-q30-30.why.3: (d) Correct because the pattern 「〜ものなら」, when used with a negative/potential form, means “if it were possible to do something difficult or unlikely,” which perfectly matches the wish to avoid having a tooth pulled despite it being impossible.
default.q.n1-18-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is 2. でいいから (as long as it is at any time that is convenient...).

Yamada: “It’s delicious. Teach me how to make it next time. Anytime you’re free is fine.”

default.q.n1-18-q31-31.why.3: (d) Incorrect because 「〜でもいいけど」 has a hesitant, unfinished nuance (“… would be fine, but…”), making it unnatural in conversation.
default.q.n1-18-q32-32.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 存じ上げています (I know him well; humble form).

Ishikawa: "Oh, Mr. Yamashita works at Company X, right? I hear Mr. Tanaka is going to become the director soon."

Ishikawa: "Yes. He helped me a great deal with my work in the past, so I know him very well."

The passive verb 「言われる」means "be told by that person that...".\n• Example: そんな嘘をついても、すぐにばれるに決まっている。(Even if you tell such a lie, it is certain to be found out immediately.)

default.q.n1-18-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 1. といえるだろうか (can it be said that...? ).

• Meaning: University A revised its curriculum last year, but can we really say that this actually improved the quality of education? I do not think so.
• Sino-Japanese reading note: 改定 (かいてい - revision), 質 (しつ - quality), 向上 (こうじょう - improvement).

- Additional examples:

default.q.n1-18-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 当時.

default.q.n1-19-q54-54.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage states: 「②歴史とは地球を舞台とした途方もなく壮大な演劇なのだ。自分や先祖も舞台の隅で参加している。」 (History is an immensely grand drama staged on Earth. We ourselves and our ancestors are also taking part in a corner of the stage.) This exactly matches the idea that our ancestors and we ourselves both contribute to creating the drama of history.
default.q.n1-19-q54-54.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The passage clearly states that we ourselves are also participating in a corner of the stage (「自分や先祖も舞台の隅で参加している」), not that it is a completed drama left behind by our ancestors (「完成されたドラマ」).
default.q.n1-19-q54-54.why.2: (c) Incorrect because history is a magnificent flow extending across many generations of ancestors up to the present (「先祖や自らがどのような時代の流れの中で生を受け生を営んできたか」), not something limited to the particular era in which one personally lived (「自分が生きてきた時代」).
default.q.n1-19-q54-54.why.3: (d) Incorrect because it mentions only people in the past (「過去の人間」), overlooking that we ourselves in the present also appear and participate in the play (「自分や先祖も舞台の隅で参加している」).
default.q.n1-19-q55-55.verdict: According to the provided answer key, the answer is 3. However, this question belongs to a different reading about researching history and does not match the provided passage about urban space and media.
default.q.n1-19-q55-55.explanation:
Note: The provided passage analyzes the transition from village society, where people knew one another deeply, to urban spaces characterized by anonymity, functional relationships in the marketplace, and a stronger sense of individuality. It also discusses the role of mass media (マスメディア) in supplementing urban communication. However, question 55 and its answer choices belong to a different reading passage about history and the psychology of aging.

* Question translation: Which of the following is consistent with the author's thoughts or feelings?
* Answer choices:
1. It is surprising that someone who had no interest in history when young would naturally become interested in it in middle age.
2. It is only natural that even a little study of history would make people want to know their place in the flow of history.
3. It is surprising that some people reach middle age without wanting to learn their place in history.
4. It is important to build a network of historical knowledge during one's teenage years.
default.q.n1-19-q55-55.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is incorrect because the passage does not mention young people being uninterested in history and then naturally becoming interested in it during middle age.
default.q.n1-19-q55-55.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the passage about urban spaces does not mention studying history or finding one's place in the flow of the times.
default.q.n1-19-q55-55.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is the answer provided in the original question (about studying history in middle age); however, the passage above, which concerns urban spaces and mass media, contains no information about this.
default.q.n1-19-q55-55.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the passage does not discuss people in their teens (十代) needing to build a network of historical knowledge.
default.q.n1-19-q56-56.verdict: The given answer is 2: The characteristic of urban social space is that people are connected through their functions on the premise that they do not know one another. (Note: The passage provided in the test has been mismatched with a reading about music composition.)
default.q.n1-19-q56-56.explanation:
Summary and comparison note:
The passage provided above is actually an essay about the process of composing music and the author's breaking away from traditional knowledge, by Kondo Jo (近藤譲「音楽という謎」). It contains no discussion of “urban social space” (都市の社会空間). Question 56 belongs to a different JLPT reading passage concerning urban sociology.

Question translation:
How did the author describe the characteristics of urban social space?

Answer choices:
1. People do not care about others, and social ties become loose and indistinct.
2. People are connected functionally, on the premise that they do not know one another.
3. People prioritize functional relationships over closeness with others.
4. People favor communication based on anonymity.
default.q.n1-19-q56-56.why.0: (a) Incorrect because it claims that people’s lack of concern for others makes social ties weak or negative. In urban sociology, ties do not disappear; they shift into role-based or functional relationships. In addition, the passage accompanying the question is an article about Kondo Jo’s music and contains no such content.
default.q.n1-19-q56-56.why.1: (b) Correct according to the given answer (2). In standard N1 reading passages on urban society, a characteristic of urban social space is that relationships between strangers are anonymous, yet people are closely connected through their social roles and functions. (Note that the original passage should be reviewed because the excerpt provided above was mistakenly taken from a passage about music.)
default.q.n1-19-q56-56.why.2: (c) Incorrect because it uses a comparative expression of priority (“rather than intimacy”). The essential nature of urban space is functional relationships among strangers, not people rejecting or undervaluing intimacy.
default.q.n1-19-q56-56.why.3: (d) Incorrect because it claims that people “prefer” anonymous communication. Anonymity and functional connections are objective structural characteristics of urban space, not the result of individual psychological preferences.
default.q.n1-19-q57-57.verdict: The provided answer is 2: People began to become more strongly aware of their individual identity (note: the question and answer choices are completely unrelated to the supplied passage about children catching insects).
default.q.n1-19-q57-57.explanation:
- Comparison with the passage: The provided passage is a comparative reading (A and B) about “children collecting insects” (子どもの昆虫採集). Passage A argues that the experience has educational value in scientific learning only when guided by adults, while passage B argues that children’s independent passion for exploration is already the beginning of learning and of forming their own worldview. The passage contains no content about “urban social space” (都市の社会空間). Therefore, question 57 does not correspond to the provided reading material.

- Question translation:
  都市の社会空間の経験によって、人々の自己に対する意識はどう変わったか。
  (How did people’s awareness of themselves change through their experiences of urban social space?)

- Answer choice translations:
  1. 集団のなかの一員という立場を意識するようになった。 (They began to be aware of their position as members of a group.)
  2. 個人であるということをより強く自覚するようになった。 (They began to become more strongly aware of themselves as individuals.)
  3. 自分が果たすべき義務をより明確に意識するようになった。 (They began to become more clearly aware of the duties they should fulfill.)
  4. 自分の才能は社会のなかで生かすべきものだと考えるようになった。 (They began to think that their talents should be put to use in society.)
default.q.n1-19-q57-57.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is unsuitable because the entire passage contains no discussion of urban spatial experiences or awareness of one's position as a member of a group (集団のなかの一員).
default.q.n1-19-q57-57.why.1: (b) Option 2 is the stated answer to the question (becoming more aware of being an individual—個人であること); however, the accompanying passage actually discusses children collecting insects (子どもの昆虫採集), not urban space.
default.q.n1-19-q57-57.why.2: (c) Choice 3 does not fit because the passage contains no information about gaining a clearer awareness of the duties that must be fulfilled (果たすべき義務).
default.q.n1-19-q57-57.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is unsuitable because the passage does not discuss making use of one’s talents in society (自分の才能は社会のなかで生かすべき).
default.q.n1-19-q58-58.verdict: The provided answer is choice 1 (人々の間の情報共有を安定させている); however, the question and the passage provided do not match in content.
default.q.n1-19-q58-58.explanation:
1. Summary of the passage & comment on the question:
The passage provided in the test is an essay by Naruke Makoto, excerpted from 『大人げない大人になれ!』, discussing goal setting (目標設定) in business and in personal life. The author points out that circumstances are always unpredictable and changing, so we cannot and should not force ourselves to stick to fixed goals or compromise points (落とし所). Instead, we should devote ourselves fully to the task at hand and respond flexibly to each small change.
However, question no. 58 asks about "mass media in urban society (都市社会におけるマスメディア)," which belongs to an entirely different reading passage from the July 2015 JLPT N1. In that original passage, the correct answer is choice 4. The excerpt provided here contains no information related to the question.

2. Translation of the question:
都市社会におけるマスメディアについて、筆者はどのようにとらえているか。
(How does the author view mass media in urban society?)

3. Translation of the choices:
1. 人々の間の情報共有を安定させている。 (It stabilizes information sharing among people.)
2. 人々の社会的な関係を強化している。 (It strengthens people's social relationships.)
3. 情報の複雑化を抑制している。 (It suppresses the increasing complexity of information.)
