default.q.n1-27-q5-5.explanation:
Sentence translation: This hypothesis lacks a strong scientific basis.
Kanji: 根拠 = grounds, basis, reliable foundation.
Common expressions: 根拠に乏しい (to lack a basis), 根拠がある／ない (to have/not have grounds), 根拠を示す (to provide grounds).
Example: 根拠のない噂に惑わされないように気をつけてください。(Please be careful not to be swayed by unfounded rumors.)
default.q.n1-27-q5-5.why.0: (a) 「こんしょ」 has the wrong on-reading for 「拠」. 「拠」 is read as 「きょ」 or 「こ」, not 「しょ」.
default.q.n1-27-q5-5.why.1: (b) 「こんじょ」has the wrong reading for「拠」; it is easily confused with 根性 こんじょう (perseverance, grit).
default.q.n1-27-q5-5.why.2: (c) 「こんきょ」is the correct reading of「根拠」(basis, grounds, reliable evidence).
default.q.n1-27-q5-5.why.3: (d) 「こんぎょ」 is incorrect because 「拠」 is pronounced with the unvoiced sound 「きょ」, not the voiced 「ぎょ」.
default.q.n1-27-q6-6.verdict: The correct answer is 4. かんじん.
default.q.n1-27-q6-6.explanation:
Sentence translation: Whatever the task, the beginning is always the most important part.
Sino-Japanese reading: 肝心 (the liver and heart, symbolizing the body's most essential parts; it is also commonly written 肝腎).
Common expressions: 肝心な点 (the crucial point), 肝心要 (かんじんかなめ - the most important thing), 初めが肝心 (the beginning is crucial).
Example: どんなに素晴らしい計画でも、実行しなければ肝心の成果は得られない。(No matter how excellent a plan is, its essential results cannot be achieved unless it is put into practice.)
default.q.n1-27-q6-6.why.0: (a) 「たんしん」 is incorrect for both kanji: 「肝」 is read 「かん」, not 「たん」 as in 単/胆, and 「心」 here has the voiced reading 「じん」.
default.q.n1-27-q6-6.why.1: (b) 「かんしん」 is incorrect because the 「心」 in this word is voiced and read 「じん」. It is easily confused with 関心 (interest) and 感心 (admiration).
default.q.n1-27-q6-6.why.2: (c) 「たんじん」 is an incorrect reading of 「肝」 (肝 is read as 「かん」, not 「たん」).
default.q.n1-27-q6-6.why.3: (d) 「かんじん」 is the correct reading of 「肝心」, meaning especially important, crucial, or essential.
default.q.n1-27-q7-7.explanation:
- Meaning of the sentence: “In the corner of the storage room, I found an old doll covered in dust.”
- 「埃（ほこり）まみれ」: covered in dust, coated with dust.
- Related kanji: 物置: storage room, 隅: corner, 人形: doll.
- Example: 泥まみれになってサッカーの練習をした。(I practiced soccer covered in mud.)
default.q.n1-27-q7-7.why.0: (a) 「〜ぐるみ」 means “the whole of” or “entire,” and is commonly used with nouns referring to groups, such as 「家族ぐるみ」 (“the whole family”) and 「町ぐるみ」 (“the entire town”). It is not used to mean that a surface is covered in dust and dirt.
default.q.n1-27-q7-7.why.1: (b) 「〜がらみ」 means “related to... / around...,” as in 「金がらみ」(related to money) and 「50歳がらみ」(around 50 years old), so it does not fit the context here.
default.q.n1-27-q7-7.why.2: (c) 「〜まみれ」 describes a surface covered or smeared with something dirty or unpleasant, such as ほこり, 泥, 血, or 汗. Therefore, 「ほこりまみれ」(covered in dust / coated with dust) is correct.
default.q.n1-27-q7-7.why.3: (d) 「〜ずくめ」means “entirely filled with” or “nothing but” a particular thing or color, as in 「いいことずくめ」(nothing but good things) and 「黒ずくめ」(dressed entirely in black). It is not used for dirt stuck to the surface of an object.
default.q.n1-27-q8-8.explanation:
Meaning: "Since Kimura and I share common interests, our conversations are always lively."
- 「会話が弾む（はずむ）」: for a conversation to become lively, animated, and enthusiastic.
- Kanji and vocabulary: 共通 (common, shared), 趣味 (hobby, interest), 会話 (conversation), 弾む (to become lively, animated, or excited).
- Example: 久しぶりに会った旧友と話が弾んだ。(I had a lively conversation with an old friend whom I had not seen in a long time.)
default.q.n1-27-q8-8.why.0: (a) 「舞う」（まう） means to dance or float in the wind, as with flowers, leaves, or dust: 「花びらが舞う」. It does not combine with 「会話」.
default.q.n1-27-q8-8.why.1: (b) 「弾む」(はずむ) combines with 「会話」 to form 「会話が弾む」, meaning that a conversation becomes lively and enthusiastic, which fits the context of having a shared interest.
default.q.n1-27-q8-8.why.2: (c) 「転がる」（ころがる - to roll）means to roll around, lie down, or tumble, as in 「ボールが転がる」; it is not used to describe a conversation.
default.q.n1-27-q8-8.why.3: (d) 「跳ねる」（はねる - haneru）means to jump, bounce, or splash (as in 「油が跳ねる」, oil splashes, or 「魚が跳ねる」, a fish jumps); it does not naturally combine with 「会話」.
default.q.n1-27-q9-9.explanation:
Sentence meaning: "A healthcare system suited to the actual conditions of the local area is being sought."
- 「実情（じつじょう）」: actual conditions, real situation.
- Sino-Japanese character meanings: 地域 (local area), 医療 (healthcare), 求める (to seek, demand).
- Example: 現場の実情を把握してから対策を立てる。(We should understand the actual conditions at the site before developing a countermeasure.)
default.q.n1-27-q9-9.why.0: (a) 「実情」（じつじょう） means “actual circumstances” or “real situation.” The expression 「地域の実情に合った」 means “suited to the actual circumstances of the local area” and is completely accurate.
default.q.n1-27-q9-9.why.1: (b) 「実況」（じっきょう）means “the actual situation unfolding at the scene,” and is commonly used in broadcasting or reporting, as in 「実況中継」(live coverage).
default.q.n1-27-q9-9.why.2: (c) 「実権」（じっけん）means “actual power” and is commonly used in「実権を握る」(hold the real power); it does not fit the context of a healthcare system.
default.q.n1-27-q9-9.why.3: (d)「実在」(じつざい) means “to exist in reality” and commonly modifies nouns referring to entities, as in「実在の人物」(a real person). It does not combine with「〜に合った」.
default.q.n1-27-q10-10.explanation:
Meaning: “That athlete is considered a once-in-a-decade talent.”
- 「逸材（いつざい）」: exceptional talent, outstanding talent.
- Common expressions: 「十年に一人の逸材」(a once-in-a-decade talent), 「将来有望な逸材」(a promising talent with a bright future).
- Kanji readings: 選手 (athlete, player), 逸材 (exceptional talent).
default.q.n1-27-q10-10.why.0: (a) 「玄人」（くろうと） means “an expert,” “professional,” or “seasoned practitioner” (the opposite of 「素人」, an amateur). It is not used with a time-based expression for the rarity of talent such as 「十年に一人の〜」.
default.q.n1-27-q10-10.why.1: (b) 「大家」(たいか) means “a master or leading expert,” usually someone with many years of experience in academia or the arts. It does not suit a young talented athlete.
default.q.n1-27-q10-10.why.2: (c) 「巨匠」（きょしょう - MASTER）means “an outstanding master” or “a great artist/director,” usually referring to a highly accomplished director, painter, or musician. It is not used for an athlete.
default.q.n1-27-q10-10.why.3: (d) 「逸材」（いつざい） means “an outstanding talent” or “a rare gifted person.” It is commonly used in the idiom 「十年に一人の逸材」 (“a talent seen only once in ten years”), so it is completely correct.
default.q.n1-27-q11-11.explanation:
- Sentence meaning: "If the application contains errors or omissions, it will not be accepted."
- 「不備（ふび）」: deficiency, omission, incompleteness.
- Common expressions: 「書類に不備がある」(the documents contain omissions or deficiencies), 「設備の不備」(inadequate or incomplete facilities).
- Vocabulary: 書類 (documents), 申請 (application), 受理 (acceptance and processing).
default.q.n1-27-q11-11.why.0: (a) 「不穏」（ふおん） means “uneasy, ominous, threatening,” and commonly describes an atmosphere or movement (such as 「不穏な空気」 or 「不穏な動き」), not a document file.
default.q.n1-27-q11-11.why.1: (b) 「不当」 (ふとう) means “unjust, unreasonable, improper” (as in 「不当な扱い」 unfair treatment and 「不当解雇」 wrongful dismissal); it does not go with 「書類に〜がある」.
default.q.n1-27-q11-11.why.2: (c) 「不備」（ふび）means “a deficiency, omission, incompleteness,” and is commonly used directly with documents or equipment, as in 「書類に不備がある」(the documents contain deficiencies/errors). It is completely appropriate here.
default.q.n1-27-q11-11.why.3: (d) 「不順」（ふじゅん） means “irregular, contrary to the natural order” (such as 「天候不順」, irregular weather, or 「生理不順」, irregular menstruation), and is not used for documents.
default.q.n1-27-q12-12.explanation:
Sentence meaning: "The restoration of the painting created about 300 years ago has been completed, and it is expected to go on public display starting next month."
- 「修復（しゅうふく）」: to restore an artwork or historic site to its original condition.
- Kanji meanings: 絵画 (painting), 公開 (opening something to the public for display).
- Example: 国宝の仏像を修復する作業が進められている。(Work to restore a national treasure Buddha statue is underway.)
default.q.n1-27-q12-12.why.0: (a) 「回復」（かいふく）means “recovery” or “a return to a good condition” in contexts such as health, the economy, or the weather (e.g. 「天気の回復」, 「疲労回復」). It is not used for restoring paintings or works of art.
default.q.n1-27-q12-12.why.1: (b) 「修復」（しゅうふく）means “to repair or restore something to its original state,” such as a work of art, historical monument, or architectural structure (e.g., 「絵画の修復」), so it is completely correct.
default.q.n1-27-q12-12.why.2: (c) 「復旧」(ふっきゅう) means “restoring normal operation” after an accident or natural disaster, and is used for roads, transportation systems, and networks: 「道路の復旧」, 「システムの復旧」.
default.q.n1-27-q12-12.why.3: (d) 「復興」（ふっこう）means “reconstruction, revival after a disaster or war” on a large scale, as in 「被災地の復興」 (“reconstruction of disaster-stricken areas”).
default.q.n1-27-q13-13.explanation:
Meaning: "His strength is that he understands not only economics but also the law."
- 「強み（つよみ）」: strength, advantage, strong point. (Antonym: 「弱み（よわみ）」 — weakness.)
- Sino-Japanese readings: 経済 (economics), 法律 (law), 詳しい (knowledgeable, well-versed).
- Example: 語学力は就職活動において大きな強みになる。(Language ability can be a major strength when looking for a job.)
default.q.n1-27-q13-13.why.0: (a) 「深み」（ふかみ） means “depth” or “profundity,” as in 「味に深みがある」 (“the flavor has depth”) and 「人物に深みがある」 (“the person has depth”). It does not mean a personal advantage or strength.
default.q.n1-27-q13-13.why.1: (b) 「強み」（つよみ - STRENGTH）means “strength, strong point, or competitive advantage.” Here, being not only good at economics but also knowledgeable about law is his strength.
default.q.n1-27-q13-13.why.2: (c) 「高み」（たかみ）means “a high place” or “a pinnacle,” and is commonly used in 「高みを目指す」(aim for greater heights) or 「高みの見物」(watch from above, remaining detached).
default.q.n1-27-q13-13.why.3: (d) 「重み」（おもみ - weight, profound significance, dignity）means “weight,” “profound significance,” or “gravitas,” as in 「言葉の重み」 (the weight of one's words) and 「歴史の重み」 (the weight of history). It does not fit the context.
default.q.n1-27-q14-14.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 今までになく新しい (new in a way never seen before).
default.q.n1-27-q14-14.explanation:
• Sentence meaning: This film was produced using a groundbreaking method.
• Vocabulary: 画期的 (かっきてき — groundbreaking; epoch-making): revolutionary, opening the door to a new era, unprecedented.
• Example: 画期的な新薬の開発により、多くの患者が救われた。(The development of a groundbreaking new drug saved many patients.)
default.q.n1-27-q14-14.why.0: (a) 「広く知られている」 means “widely known” or “familiar to many people”; it does not mean innovative or groundbreaking.
default.q.n1-27-q14-14.why.1: (b) 「最近ではめずらしい」 means “rare in recent times,” so it cannot express the idea of ushering in a new era or age.
default.q.n1-27-q14-14.why.2: (c) 「非常に時間がかかる」 means “takes a very long time,” which is completely different in meaning from the original word.
default.q.n1-27-q14-14.why.3: (d) 「今までになく新しい」 means unprecedentedly new, making 「画期的な」 the most accurate synonym.
default.q.n1-27-q15-15.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 計画して (plan, anticipate).
default.q.n1-27-q15-15.explanation:
• Meaning: That company is planning or scheming to enter the overseas market.
• Vocabulary: 目論む (もくろむ): plan, intend, scheme (often used for a business plan or an attempt to achieve a particular goal).
• Example: 彼は事業のさらなる拡大をもくろんでいる。(He is plotting to expand his business even further.)
default.q.n1-27-q15-15.why.0: (a) 「計画して」 means “to plan” or “intend to carry out,” and is an exact synonym of 「もくろんで」.
default.q.n1-27-q15-15.why.1: (b) 「果たして」means completing or achieving a goal; it does not express planning or plotting something in one's mind.
default.q.n1-27-q15-15.why.2: (c) 「開始して」 means to begin carrying something out, whereas 「もくろむ」 refers only to the stage of plotting or planning.
default.q.n1-27-q15-15.why.3: (d) 「あきらめて」means to give up or abandon something, which is the complete opposite meaning.
default.q.n1-27-q16-16.verdict: The correct answer is 4: ヒント (hint, clue).
default.q.n1-27-q16-16.explanation:
• Meaning: To solve the problem, I would like a little more of a clue or hint.
• Vocabulary: 手がかり (てがかり): a clue, trace, or hint that serves as a basis for solving a problem or investigating a case.
• Example: 警察は防犯カメラの映像を手がかりに犯人を追っている。(The police are tracking the suspect using footage from security cameras as a clue.)
default.q.n1-27-q16-16.why.0: (a) 「イメージ」 means an imagined picture or impression; it does not mean a clue or hint for solving a problem.
default.q.n1-27-q16-16.why.1: (b) 「サポート」means support or assistance; it does not refer to evidence or a clue used to find the answer.
default.q.n1-27-q16-16.why.2: (c) 「チャンス」 means “opportunity” or “chance,” not a clue or suggestive data.
default.q.n1-27-q16-16.why.3: (d) 「ヒント」 means a hint or clue and is completely synonymous with 「手がかり」 in the context of solving a problem.
default.q.n1-27-q17-17.verdict: The correct answer is 1: すぐには (immediately).
default.q.n1-27-q17-17.explanation:
• Sentence meaning: That person's story cannot be believed immediately.
• Vocabulary: にわかに (俄かに): suddenly, immediately. With the negative pattern 「にわかには〜ない」, it becomes an idiomatic expression meaning “cannot ... right away” or “cannot yet ...”.
• Example: その噂の真偽については、にわかには判断できない。(I cannot immediately determine whether that rumor is true.)
default.q.n1-27-q17-17.why.0: (a) 「すぐには」 means "immediately"; with a negative expression, it means "cannot ... right away," precisely corresponding to 「にわかには～ない」.
default.q.n1-27-q17-17.why.1: (b) 「完全には」means “not completely,” expressing partial negation; it does not describe time or immediacy as 「にわかに」 does.
default.q.n1-27-q17-17.why.2: (c) 「すなおには」 means obediently, honestly, or without suspicion; it does not correspond to 「にわかには」.
default.q.n1-27-q17-17.why.3: (d) 「簡単には」means "easily" and emphasizes difficulty; it does not match the meaning of immediacy expressed by「にわかには」.
default.q.n1-27-q18-18.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 便利で役に立っている (convenient and useful).
default.q.n1-27-q18-18.explanation:
• Sentence meaning: This pot is very convenient and useful.
• Vocabulary: 重宝 (ちょうほう): convenient, useful, valuable because it is so handy. In the form 「重宝している」, it often means that the speaker finds something useful and uses it frequently.
• Example: この電子レンジは多機能で、毎日の料理にとても重宝している。(This microwave has many functions and is extremely useful for my everyday cooking.)
default.q.n1-27-q18-18.why.0: (a) 「以前より値上がりしている」means “the price has risen compared with before”; the mistake is confusing 宝, meaning treasure or value, with the actual meaning of the word.
default.q.n1-27-q18-18.why.1: (b) 「形が気に入っている」 means liking the design or shape, not describing usability.
default.q.n1-27-q18-18.why.2: (c) 「評価が高まっている」means that people's evaluation is improving; it does not mean that something is useful in itself.
default.q.n1-27-q18-18.why.3: (d) 「便利で役に立っている」 means convenient and very useful, which is exactly synonymous with 「重宝している」.
default.q.n1-27-q19-19.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 厳しい (strict, harsh).
default.q.n1-27-q19-19.explanation:
• Meaning: Mr. Nakamura is always extremely strict about his work.
• Vocabulary: シビア (from English “severe”): strict, harsh, or demanding, referring to attitudes, working conditions, or circumstances.
• Example: プロの世界は結果に対して非常にシビアだ。(The professional world is extremely demanding when it comes to results.)
default.q.n1-27-q19-19.why.0: (a) 「弱気だ」 means timid, weak, or lacking confidence, contrary to a firm and strict attitude.
default.q.n1-27-q19-19.why.1: (b) 「厳しい」 means strict or harsh and is an exact synonym of the loanword 「シビアだ」 (severe).
default.q.n1-27-q19-19.why.2: (c) 「柔軟だ」 means flexible or adaptable, conveying the opposite of being strict or rigid.
default.q.n1-27-q19-19.why.3: (d) 「注意深い」 means careful, cautious, or attentive to details; it does not express the strict, demanding quality of 「シビア」.
default.q.n1-27-q20-20.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 学校は地域と連携して生徒の安全を守っている。
default.q.n1-27-q20-20.explanation:
「連携（れんけい）」means coordinating and working together among institutions, organizations, groups, or departments to achieve a common goal.
- Common expressions: 「〜と連携する」「連携を図る」「連携を強化する」.
- Example: 警察と消防が連携して救助活動を行った。(The police and fire department worked together to carry out rescue operations.)
default.q.n1-27-q20-20.why.0: Correct. 「連携する」 means to coordinate or link actions among organizations or individuals; 「地域と連携して」 (“in cooperation with the local community”) is completely natural and appropriate in context.
default.q.n1-27-q20-20.why.1: Incorrect. When several employees use the same printer, use 「共有して（使う）」 (“share/use jointly”) or 「共同で」; 「連携」 refers to coordinating activities.
default.q.n1-27-q20-20.why.2: Incorrect. When stock prices move in tandem with or correlate with exchange rates, use 「連動して」 (“in tandem with”), not 「連携」.
default.q.n1-27-q20-20.why.3: Incorrect. When telling someone to carry a map while mountain climbing, use 「携帯してください」 or 「持参してください」, not 「連携」.
default.q.n1-27-q21-21.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 審判の判定に不服を唱えることはできない。
default.q.n1-27-q21-21.explanation:
「不服（ふふく）」means dissatisfaction or unwillingness to accept an official judgment, decision, or order.
- Common phrases: 「不服を唱える」「不服を申し立てる」「不服そうな顔/態度」.
- Example: 裁判の判決に不服がある場合は、控訴することができる。(If you are dissatisfied with a court ruling, you can appeal it.)
default.q.n1-27-q21-21.why.0: Incorrect. To incur the dislike or anger of people around you, use 「反感を買った」('incurred resentment') or 「怒りを買った」('incurred anger'), not 「不服を買う」.
default.q.n1-27-q21-21.why.1: Incorrect. To describe releasing accumulated daily frustration, use 「日ごろの鬱憤（うっぷん）を晴らす」 or 「日ごろのストレスを発散する」. 「不服」 does not naturally combine with 「晴らす」.
default.q.n1-27-q21-21.why.2: Correct. 「不服」refers to dissatisfaction with a judgment or decision;「判定に不服を唱える」(voice opposition to a ruling) is a standard collocation.
default.q.n1-27-q21-21.why.3: Incorrect. For a customer complaints department, use 「苦情（クレーム）を受け付ける」 or 「ご意見」. 「不服」 is not used in this customer-service context.
default.q.n1-27-q22-22.verdict: The correct answer is 4: 自分の店を持つという夢が、とうとうかなった。
default.q.n1-27-q22-22.explanation:
「かなう（叶う）」means for a dream, wish, or hope to come true or be fulfilled.
- Common expressions: 「夢がかなう」「願いがかなう」「希望がかなう」「長年の思いがかなう」.
- Example: 努力を続けた結果、第一志望の大学に合格するという願いがかなった。(After continuing to work hard, my wish to be accepted by my first-choice university came true.)
default.q.n1-27-q22-22.why.0: Incorrect. When hardships are rewarded, use 「苦労が報われ（報われる）」, not 「苦労がかなう」.
default.q.n1-27-q22-22.why.1: Incorrect. For an accurate weather forecast, use 「天気予報が当たり（当たる）」, not 「かなう」.
default.q.n1-27-q22-22.why.2: Incorrect. When a carefully prepared event takes place or ends smoothly, use 「無事終了した」, 「無事開催された」, or 「成功した」; an event does not combine with 「かなう」.
default.q.n1-27-q22-22.why.3: Correct. 「かなう（叶う）」 is used when a dream or wish becomes reality; 「夢がかなう」 (a dream comes true) is the most standard and natural usage.
default.q.n1-27-q23-23.verdict: The correct answer is 1: あの新人選手は目覚ましい成長を見せている。
default.q.n1-27-q23-23.explanation:
「目覚ましい（めざましい）」means remarkable, outstanding, or astonishing—something that makes others open their eyes in admiration. It is commonly used to describe development, progress, or achievements.
- Common expressions: 「目覚ましい成長」「目覚ましい発展」「目覚ましい活躍」「目覚ましい進歩」.
- Example: AI技術の目覚ましい進歩により、人々の生活は大きく変化している。(People’s lives are changing dramatically due to the remarkable progress of AI technology.)
default.q.n1-27-q23-23.why.0: Correct. 「目覚ましい」 describes remarkable development or progress; 「目覚ましい成長を見せる」 is a standard and common collocation.
default.q.n1-27-q23-23.why.1: Incorrect. Terrifyingly loud, startling sounds are expressed with 「驚くほどの」, 「凄まじいほどの」, or 「飛び起きるほどの」, not 「目覚ましい」 modifying a sound.
default.q.n1-27-q23-23.why.2: Incorrect. For bright, eye-catching colors, use 「鮮やかな色」 (vivid colors) or 「目立つ色」 (conspicuous colors); 「目覚ましい」 is not used to describe colors.
default.q.n1-27-q23-23.why.3: Incorrect. When someone wakes up feeling refreshed and alert, 「目覚めがいい」 or 「すっきりしている」 is used. 「目覚ましい」 describes outstanding achievements or progress, not a person’s state of alertness.
default.q.n1-27-q24-24.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 靴のひもがほどけないようにしっかりと結んだ。
default.q.n1-27-q24-24.explanation:
「ほどける（解ける）」means to come undone, come loose, or unfasten (used for knots, shoelaces, and yarn; figuratively, tension or misunderstandings can also be relieved or resolved).
- Common phrases: 「靴のひもがほどける」「結び目がほどける」「緊張がほどける」.
- Example: 彼女の優しい笑顔を見て、張り詰めていた緊張がすっとほどけた。(When I saw her gentle smile, the tension that had been building suddenly melted away.)
default.q.n1-27-q24-24.why.0: Incorrect. When a loose screw causes a chair to wobble, use 「ねじが緩んで（緩む）」; screws do not 「ほどける」.
default.q.n1-27-q24-24.why.1: Correct. 「ほどける」is used when a knot or tied cord comes undone; expressing “tie them tightly so that the shoelaces do not come undone” with「靴のひもがほどけないように」is completely standard.
default.q.n1-27-q24-24.why.2: Incorrect. For a button that has come undone or is not fastened, use 「ボタンが外れている（外れる）」; 「ほどける」 is not used for buttons.
default.q.n1-27-q24-24.why.3: Incorrect. When the ice in a glass melts, use「氷が溶けた（溶ける）」, not「ほどける」.
default.q.n1-27-q25-25.verdict: The correct answer is 3: 部長が海外の支社に赴任するので、みんなで送別会を開いた。
default.q.n1-27-q25-25.explanation:
「赴任（ふにん）」 means going to take up a post or assignment at a new workplace, usually at a branch office in another prefecture or overseas and generally for an extended period.
- Common expressions: 「海外支社に赴任する」, 「単身赴任」 (taking an assignment away from home alone, without one's family), 「赴任地」 (place of assignment).
- Example: 彼は来月から大阪支社へ赴任することになっている。(He is scheduled to take up a post at the Osaka branch starting next month.)
default.q.n1-27-q25-25.why.0: Incorrect. Working at another location for three days is a short-term business trip, so 「出張しなければならない」must be used. 「赴任」refers to relocating permanently to a new workplace for a longer-term assignment.
default.q.n1-27-q25-25.why.1: Incorrect. Having new employees participate in or gain practical experience at a retail sales floor during training is expressed with 「売り場に入ってもらう」 or 「売り場を経験してもらう」, not 「赴任」.
default.q.n1-27-q25-25.why.2: Correct. 「赴任」means moving to take up an assignment at a new work location, especially a distant branch or an overseas post. 「海外の支社に赴任する」is completely natural and correct.
default.q.n1-27-q25-25.why.3: Incorrect. Being appointed to a new position, such as company president, takes 「社長に就任する」 (assume office); 「赴任」 is associated with moving to a new place of work, not merely being promoted or appointed.
default.q.n1-27-q26-26.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (とあって).
default.q.n1-27-q26-26.explanation:
Meaning: Because the famous writer A's lecture was free of charge, a huge crowd of fans came and filled the venue.
Sino-Japanese vocabulary: 作家 (author/writer), 講演会 (lecture), 無料 (free of charge), 詰めかける (to flock to a place in large numbers).
Grammar pattern: N / plain form + とあって means “because the circumstances are particularly...”. Example: 夏休みとあって、プールは子どもたちでいっぱいだ。(Because it is summer vacation, the pool is packed with children.)
default.q.n1-27-q26-26.why.0: (a) 「にして」 can mean 'even,' 'only at,' or 'both A and B'; it is not used to explain the cause of an event leading to the result in the following clause.
default.q.n1-27-q26-26.why.1: (b) 「にあって」 means “precisely in such special circumstances or a situation,” and the following clause generally describes an adaptive behavior, attitude, or action, not merely an objective cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.n1-27-q26-26.why.2: (c) 「として」 means “as” or “in the capacity of,” so it is not appropriate for expressing a cause.
default.q.n1-27-q26-26.why.3: (d) 「とあって」 is an N1/N2 grammar pattern in the form 'N / plain form + とあって', indicating that a special circumstance leads to an inevitable or unusual result in the following clause (because the lecture was free, a large number of fans came).
default.q.n1-27-q27-27.explanation:
Meaning: Whenever I hear stories about people who have moved from the city to live in the countryside, I feel deeply that “the countryside has the power to heal people’s hearts.”
Kanji readings and meanings: 都会 (city), 田舎 (countryside), 移り住む (move to live somewhere), 癒す (heal), 感じる (feel).
Grammar pattern: V-る + につけ: “whenever one does something, one always feels or thinks something.” It is often used with 見るにつけ, 聞くにつけ, and 思うにつけ. Example: この写真を見るにつけ、故郷の家族を思い出す。(Whenever I look at this photo, I remember my family back home.)
default.q.n1-27-q27-27.why.0: (a) 「につけ」 combines with the perception verb '聞く' to form '聞くにつけ,' meaning 'whenever I hear...,' which fits perfectly with the following phrase 'つくづく感じる' ('feel deeply').
default.q.n1-27-q27-27.why.1: (b) 「なり」 means “as soon as...,” with the following clause describing an immediate, intentional action by a third person. It is not used for an ongoing emotion or psychological realization.
default.q.n1-27-q27-27.why.2: (c) 「とは」expresses surprise or exclamation at something unexpected or hard to believe, so it does not fit this sentence structure.
default.q.n1-27-q27-27.why.3: (d) 「にしてみると」 means “from someone’s standpoint” or “judging from someone’s perspective.” It follows a noun referring to a person and cannot directly follow the verb 「聞く」.
default.q.n1-27-q28-28.explanation:
Meaning: This pot is convenient because it can be used for anything from stir-fried dishes to fried dishes.
Sino-Japanese readings: 鍋 (なべ - pot), 炒め物 (いためもの - stir-fried dish), 揚げ物 (あげもの - fried dish), 便利 (べんり - convenient).
Grammar pattern: N1に、N2にと: “for N1, for N2, and so on” (everything can be used for...). It lists representative examples to emphasize variety or overall versatility. Example: 彼は仕事に、勉強にと毎日忙しい日々を送っている。(He spends every day busy with work, studying, and so on.)
default.q.n1-27-q28-28.why.0: (a) 「は」 is a particle that marks the topic; it does not form the corresponding grammar pattern for listing items.
default.q.n1-27-q28-28.why.1: (b) 「と」 forms the representative listing pattern 「～に、～にと」 (“everything from ... to ...”); here, 「いため物に、揚げ物にと何にでも使えて」 means “it can be conveniently used for anything, from stir-fries to fried dishes.”
default.q.n1-27-q28-28.why.2: (c) 「や」 connects ordinary nouns in patterns such as AやB; it does not follow the particle に in this sentence pattern.
default.q.n1-27-q28-28.why.3: (d) 「か」 indicates a choice or doubt and does not form this type of listing structure.
default.q.n1-27-q29-29.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (させられた).
default.q.n1-27-q29-29.explanation:
Meaning: The printer malfunctioned, so I called the manufacturer to ask about it. After making me answer question after question for quite some time, the person in charge eventually told me that they could not help me.
Sino-Japanese vocabulary: 調子 (condition), 製造会社 (manufacturing company), 問い合わせる (to inquire), 担当者 (person in charge), 質問 (question), 対応 (handling/support).
Grammar pattern: V-た + あげく: “after doing something for a long time... ultimately resulting in a bad or regrettable outcome.” Example: 色々悩んだあげく、結局会社を辞めることにした。(After agonizing over it for a long time, I ultimately decided to quit my job.)
default.q.n1-27-q29-29.why.0: (a) 「させた」is the active causative past form, meaning to make someone do something, whereas the subject here is the speaker (“I”), who was made to answer by the person in charge.
default.q.n1-27-q29-29.why.1: (b) 「させられる」 is the causative-passive form in the plain non-past form, so it does not fit the 「V-た + あげく」 structure used to recount a sequence of past events.
default.q.n1-27-q29-29.why.2: (c) 「させる」is the active causative form in its basic form, so it is wrong both in the direction of the action and in the verb tense.
default.q.n1-27-q29-29.why.3: (d) 「させられた」is the past passive-causative form (答えさせられた: was forced to answer), and it combines correctly with あげく to form 「答えさせられたあげく」(after being forced to answer question after question, one was ultimately rejected).
default.q.n1-27-q30-30.verdict: The provided answer is 4 (のではないか); however, the grammatically correct N1 expression for this context of unexpectedly discovering something is 2 (ではないか).
default.q.n1-27-q30-30.explanation:
Meaning: That day, I hurriedly boarded a train that had just pulled into the platform. However, the train began moving in the opposite direction. I deeply regretted not checking the train's destination carefully.
Kanji readings: 反対方向 (はんたいほうこう: opposite direction), 行き先 (いきさき: destination), 確かめる (たしかめる: check, confirm), 後悔 (こうかい: regret).
N1 grammar: V-た + ではないか expresses surprise or alarm when the speaker suddenly discovers an unexpected fact right in front of them. Example: ドアを開けると、誰もいないはずの部屋に電気がついているではないか。(When I opened the door, the lights were on in a room that was supposed to be empty!)
default.q.n1-27-q30-30.why.0: (a) 「ではない」 is a simple negative form and cannot stand alone at the end of a clause to express surprise or astonishment.
default.q.n1-27-q30-30.why.1: (b) 「ではないか」 following a past-tense verb (〜たではないか) is a standard N1 grammar structure expressing surprise or the discovery of an unexpected fact (“So the train has started running in the opposite direction!”).
default.q.n1-27-q30-30.why.2: (c) 「のではない」 is a plain negative assertion meaning “it is not that...” and is completely wrong for the meaning required by the context.
default.q.n1-27-q30-30.why.3: (d) 「のではないか」, the provided answer, expresses a conjecture or gentle doubt (“might it not be...?”). However, in this narrative context, where the speaker is confronting an ironic event that has already occurred, option [2] is more accurate.
default.q.n1-27-q31-31.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (お出しする以上).
default.q.n1-27-q31-31.explanation:
Meaning: A: “What does the restaurant place the greatest emphasis on?” B: “Hygiene management. Once we serve a meal to our customers, we pay more attention to hygiene and safety management than anything else.”
Kanji vocabulary: 衛生管理 (hygiene management), 食事 (meal), 注意 (attention).
Grammar pattern: plain-form V + 以上(は): “Once ... , then naturally/one must ...” The humble form お + V-stem + する: お出しする (the restaurant’s humble way of saying “serve a dish”). Example: 一度約束した以上、絶対に守らなければならない。(Once you have made a promise, you absolutely must keep it.)
default.q.n1-27-q31-31.why.0: (a) 「お出しになる以上」 uses honorific language incorrectly. 「お出しになる」 is respectful language for an action performed by a guest, whereas bringing out food for service is an action performed by restaurant staff and should use humble language.
default.q.n1-27-q31-31.why.1: (b) 「お出しになるうえ」 incorrectly uses honorific language for the speaker’s own action, and 「〜うえ」 does not express the strong sense of commitment or unavoidable responsibility conveyed by 「〜以上」.
default.q.n1-27-q31-31.why.2: (c) 「お出しする以上」 correctly uses the humble form 「お出しする」 for the restaurant’s action together with 「〜以上」, expressing the responsibility that “once we serve food to customers, we naturally must pay close attention to hygiene.”
default.q.n1-27-q31-31.why.3: (d) 「お出しするうえ」 is correct humble language, but 「〜うえ(で)」 means “during the process of” or “when doing something.” It does not convey the clear sense of responsibility and determination expressed by 「〜以上」.
default.q.n1-27-q32-32.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (でしかないことに).
default.q.n1-27-q32-32.explanation:
Sentence meaning: Until I went abroad to study, I assumed that the world I could see was everything. In reality, I had not realized that it was only an extremely small part of the world.
Vocabulary: 留学 (study abroad), 世界 (world), 一部分 (one part), 気付く (to realize).
Grammar pattern: N + でしかない: "is merely... / is nothing more than...". Example: 彼の言っていることは単なる言い訳でしかない。(What he is saying is nothing more than an excuse.)
default.q.n1-27-q32-32.why.0: (a) 「でないことにしか」has an incorrect grammatical combination and word order, resulting in a semantically illogical double negative.
default.q.n1-27-q32-32.why.1: (b) 「でしかないことに」 uses the pattern “N + でしかない” (“is nothing more than...”) combined with “〜ことに気付いていなかった,” forming a complete phrase meaning: “did not realize that it was only a small part.”
default.q.n1-27-q32-32.why.2: (c) 「にないことでしか」 is incorrect in both word order and Japanese grammar.
default.q.n1-27-q32-32.why.3: (d) 「にしかないことで」means “something found only in...,” so it is unsuitable for expressing “only a small part.”
default.q.n1-27-q33-33.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (ばかばかしく思えるくらい).
default.q.n1-27-q33-33.explanation:
Meaning of the dialogue: A: 'Hey, have you tried the calculation function I showed you the other day?' B: 'Yes. It calculates things so easily that it seems ridiculous how much time the task used to take.' A: 'See? Just leave computer-related matters to me!'
Sino-Japanese vocabulary: 計算機能 (calculation function), 簡単.
Grammar structure: V/Adj + くらい: 'to the extent that... / so ... that...'. The spontaneous-form verb 思える means 'naturally feel/seem'. Example: 涙が出るくらい感動した。(I was so moved that I cried.)
default.q.n1-27-q33-33.why.0: (a) 「ばかばかしい思いをするもので」: 「思いをする」 means to undergo or suffer a negative experience caused by external circumstances. Combined with 「もので」 (“because”), it is unsuitable for modifying the degree of 「簡単に計算できた」.
default.q.n1-27-q33-33.why.1: (b) 「ばかばかしく思えるもので」has the ending “〜もので,” which indicates a reason or justification and does not fit this sentence’s context.
default.q.n1-27-q33-33.why.2: (c) 「ばかばかしい思いをするくらい」 uses 「思いをする」 unnaturally; the spontaneous form 「思える」 (“naturally feel”) is more appropriate when describing the speaker’s subjective perception.
default.q.n1-27-q33-33.why.3: (d) 「ばかばかしく思えるくらい」 uses 思える (the spontaneous form: to feel) together with the degree expression 〜くらい (to the extent that...), creating the complete meaning: “the calculation is so easy that the effort made in the past seems ridiculous.”
default.q.n1-27-q34-34.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (待っていただくわけにはいきませんか).
default.q.n1-27-q34-34.explanation:
Meaning: Yamanaka: “Hello, may I ask if this is Mr. Kimura? I’m Yamanaka from AB Publishing. Would it be all right if I came to pick up the manuscript now?” — Kimura: “I’m sorry, but I still haven’t finished it. Could you wait another three days?”
Sino-Japanese readings: 出版 (publication), 原稿 (manuscript).
Grammar pattern: V-ていただくわけにはいきませんか is a tactful, polite way to ask someone to do something for you (“Would it be possible for you to...?”). Example: もう少しお時間をいただくわけにはいきませんか。(Could you give me a little more time?)
default.q.n1-27-q34-34.why.0: (a) 「待っておいでになります」is the respectful form meaning “the teacher is waiting.” It is incorrect because the person who should be waiting here is editor Yamanaka, the other party, not the author.
default.q.n1-27-q34-34.why.1: (b) 「お待ち申し上げております」is humble language meaning "I am waiting for you." The direction is incorrect because the author is asking the other person to wait.
default.q.n1-27-q34-34.why.2: (c) 「待たせていただくことにしましょうか」 sounds arrogant and presumptuous, as if deciding unilaterally, "Shall we agree that I will make you wait?" It is impolite in conversation.
default.q.n1-27-q34-34.why.3: (d) 「待っていただくわけにはいきませんか」is an extremely humble and polite way to make a request or negotiate in business honorific language: “Would it be possible for you to kindly wait another three days?”
default.q.n1-27-q35-35.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (つもりだったかっていうと).
default.q.n1-27-q35-35.explanation:
Meaning in the context of the reading dialogue: “Actually, if you ask whether I had planned from the beginning to become an astronaut, that wasn’t the case. After graduating from university, I was actually planning to become a doctor.”
On-readings: 宇宙飛行士 (astronaut), 医者 (doctor).
Grammar pattern: 〜かというと / 〜かっていうと: “if you ask whether… / speaking of whether…” Used when the speaker raises a hypothetical question and then explains or corrects the assumption in the following clause. Example: 嫌いになったのかというと、そうではなく、忙しくて会えないだけだ。 (If you ask whether I came to hate them, that’s not it—I’m simply too busy to meet them.)
default.q.n1-27-q35-35.why.0: (a) 「つもりだったかっていうと」 uses the past tense 「つもりだった」 (“had intended to...”) together with the colloquial pattern 「〜かっていうと」 (= 「〜かというと」, “if one asks whether...”). It fits the following explanation of a past intention: “Because when I graduated, I had intended to become a doctor.”
default.q.n1-27-q35-35.why.1: (b) 「つもりなのかっていわれたら」 uses the present-tense form 「つもりなのか」 and 「いわれたら」 (“if one is asked by someone else”), so it does not fit a narration of a past intention.
default.q.n1-27-q35-35.why.2: (c) 「つもりじゃなかったのかっていわれたら」 is a negative question in the passive form, meaning “if one is asked, ‘Wasn't that your intention?’” Its logic does not fit the statement.
default.q.n1-27-q35-35.why.3: (d) 「つもりがなかったかっていうと」 is a negative question meaning 'if you ask whether I did not intend to...,'. This contradicts the correction 「そうじゃないんです」 (that is not the case) in the following clause.
default.q.n1-27-q36-36.verdict: The correct order is: 2 → 4 → 1 → 3. The ★ position is choice 1 (ない).
default.q.n1-27-q36-36.explanation:
・ Complete sentence: 大学入試では、試験当日初めてその大学に行き、迷ってしまったということのないように事前に見学しておくとよい。
・ Meaning: For a university entrance exam, it is a good idea to visit the university beforehand so that you do not go there for the first time on the day of the exam and get lost.
default.q.n1-27-q36-36.why.0: (a) 1. ない: It occupies the third position (the ★ gap) and modifies the following noun or particle to form the grammar pattern 「〜ことのないように」 (“so that ... does not happen”).
default.q.n1-27-q36-36.why.1: (b) 2. という: In position 1, it follows the clause 「迷ってしまった」 to connect the content of the event (“the matter of getting lost…”).
default.q.n1-27-q36-36.why.2: (c) 3. ように: It occupies the fourth position, following the adjective 「ない」to form the purpose pattern 「〜ないように」(so as not to), connecting to the advice in 「事前に見学しておくとよい」.
default.q.n1-27-q36-36.why.3: (d) 4. ことの: It occupies the second position after 「という」. The particle 「の」 functions as the subject in place of 「が」 in the relative clause modifying 「ない」 (ことのない = ことがない).
default.q.n1-27-q37-37.verdict: The correct order is: 4 → 2 → 1 → 3. The choice in the ★ position is 1 (となる).
default.q.n1-27-q37-37.explanation:
・Complete sentence: 趣味を持つのは良いことだと思いますが、家庭を犠牲にしてまでとなると、それはちょっと問題です。
・Meaning: I think having a hobby is a good thing, but if it goes so far that you have to sacrifice your family, that is somewhat problematic.
default.q.n1-27-q37-37.why.0: (a) 1. となる: It appears in position 3 (the ★ gap). Combined with 「まで」, it forms 「までとなる」 (reach the point of becoming...), which serves as the premise for the conditional particle 「と」.
default.q.n1-27-q37-37.why.1: (b) 2. まで: occupies position 2 and follows「にして」to form the grammar pattern「〜てまで」(to the extreme extent of doing something).
default.q.n1-27-q37-37.why.2: (c) 3. と: It occupies the fourth position and combines with 「となる」 to form the conditional structure 「〜となると」 (“if it comes to that...”), linking to the following evaluative clause 「それはちょっと問題です」.
default.q.n1-27-q37-37.why.3: (d) 4. にして: It occupies the first position and follows the noun phrase 「家庭を犠牲」, forming 「家庭を犠牲にして」(at the cost of one's family).
default.q.n1-27-q38-38.verdict: Correct order: 3 → 2 → 4 → 1. The position marked ★ is choice 4 (自分の責任).
default.q.n1-27-q38-38.explanation:
・ Complete sentence: 管理職になったら、たとえ自分には責任がなくても自分の責任だとして部下の失敗も引き受けるというくらいの覚悟がなくてはならない。
・ Translation: Once you become a manager, you must be prepared to take responsibility for your subordinates’ failures as well, treating them as your own responsibility even when you are not personally at fault.
default.q.n1-27-q38-38.why.0: (a) 1. だとして: In the fourth position, it follows the noun 「自分の責任」 to form 「〜だとして」 (regarding it as / assuming it to be...), modifying the action 「部下の失敗も引き受ける」.
default.q.n1-27-q38-38.why.1: (b) 2. がなくても occupies the second position and follows「責任」to form the concessive clause「〜がなくても」(even without...). It corresponds to the adverb「たとえ」at the beginning of the sentence.
default.q.n1-27-q38-38.why.2: (c) 3. 自分には責任: It goes in the first position, immediately after the adverb 「たとえ」, opening the concessive clause 「自分には責任がなくても」(even if I am not responsible).
default.q.n1-27-q38-38.why.3: (d) 4. 自分の責任: It occupies position 3 (★) and is a noun phrase functioning as a complement before 「だとして」, expressing taking responsibility oneself.
default.q.n1-27-q39-39.verdict: Correct order: 3 → 4 → 2 → 1. The position marked ★ is choice 2 (我が社だが).
default.q.n1-27-q39-39.explanation:
・ Complete sentence: 今でこそ一流企業と言われる我が社だが、もともとは小さな町工場だった。
・ Meaning: Although our company is now considered a leading company, it was originally just a small local factory.
default.q.n1-27-q39-39.why.0: (a) 1. もともとは: it occupies the fourth position, following the contrastive conjunction 「我が社だが」, and begins the explanation of the company’s past and origins: 「小さな町工場だった」.
default.q.n1-27-q39-39.why.1: (b) 2. 我が社だが occupies the third position (★). It is the subject modified by「一流企業と言われる」and includes the conjunction「だが」to transition contrastively to the following clause.
default.q.n1-27-q39-39.why.2: (c) 3. 今でこそ: goes in position 1 at the beginning of the sentence and forms the grammar pattern「今でこそ〜（が）」(nowadays / now, although...), contrasting the present with the past.
default.q.n1-27-q39-39.why.3: (d) 4. 一流企業と言われる: It occupies position 2 and is an attributive clause modifying the noun「我が社」that follows「今でこそ」.
default.q.n1-27-q40-40.verdict: The correct order is: 4 → 1 → 3 → 2. The star (★) marks answer choice 3 (思いきや).
default.q.n1-27-q40-40.explanation:
・ Complete sentence: 新番組でこれまでにない役柄を演じる俳優の上田秋さん。役作りに悩んでいるのかと思いきやそうでもないという。
・ Meaning: Actor Aki Ueda plays a role unlike any he has played before in the new program. One might assume that he is struggling to develop the character, but apparently that is not the case.
default.q.n1-27-q40-40.why.0: (a) 1. と: occupies position 2 and follows the interrogative particle「のか」to form the quoted thought「〜のかと」before the verb「思いきや」.
default.q.n1-27-q40-40.why.1: (b) 2. そうでもない: It occupies position 4, follows the expectation-reversing phrase 「〜と思いきや」to indicate a contrary reality, and comes before 「という」as the content being conveyed.
default.q.n1-27-q40-40.why.2: (c) 3. 思いきや: It occupies position 3 (blank ★) and is the core component of the grammar pattern 「〜かと思いきや」 (one might think that..., but in fact...).
default.q.n1-27-q40-40.why.3: (d) 4. のか belongs in the 1st position, directly following the verb「悩んでいる」to form an embedded question or speculation in「〜のかと思いきや」.
default.q.n1-27-q41-41.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (入るのはいい).
default.q.n1-27-q41-41.explanation:
- Meaning: The pattern 「〜のはいい（が／けれど／として）」 acknowledges or accepts the matter or action in the preceding clause (“it is fine to ...”), then presents a condition, caution, or more important issue in the following clause.
- Connection: V (dictionary form or plain form) + のはいい（が／けれど）
- Additional examples:
  + 「旅行に行くのはいいが、予算オーバーにならないように気をつけてね。」(Going on a trip is fine, but be careful not to exceed the budget.)
  + 「冗談を言うのはいいとしても、TPO（時・場所・場合）はわきまえるべきだ。」(Joking is fine, but you should still understand the appropriate time, place, and circumstances.)
default.q.n1-27-q41-41.why.0: (a) 「入るのにいい」expresses an evaluation meaning “good/convenient for entering”; it is not used to accept an action as a premise with a condition in the following clause.
default.q.n1-27-q41-41.why.1: (b) 「入るのがいいのか」has the nuance of wondering or hesitating, “Would it be better to go in?” It does not fit the following clause, which expresses advice or a request.
default.q.n1-27-q41-41.why.2: (c) 「入るのはいい」means “entering/participating is acceptable (but...)” and fits perfectly into a structure that acknowledges one point before stating a condition or qualification in the following clause.
default.q.n1-27-q41-41.why.3: (d) 「入るのでいいのか」expresses the question “Is it okay to choose this one?” and does not form a complete sentence in a context expressing conditional approval.
default.q.n1-27-q42-42.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (やめてほしいのだ).
default.q.n1-27-q42-42.explanation:
- Meaning: The pattern「〜てほしいのだ」combines the structure expressing a desire for someone to perform or stop an action,「〜てほしい」, with the explanatory/emphatic ending「〜のだ（んだ）」. It is used when the speaker wants to express their core desire to the other person earnestly, firmly, or with clarification.
- Formation: V-て + ほしいのだ / ほしくないのだ
- Additional examples:
  + 「私たちはただ、平和に安心して暮らさせてほしいのだ。」(We simply want to be allowed to live peacefully and without fear.)
  + 「これ以上無駄な争いを続けるのはやめてほしいのだ。」(I genuinely want you to stop continuing this pointless conflict.)
default.q.n1-27-q42-42.why.0: (a) 「やめようと思う」expresses the speaker’s own intention (“I intend to quit/stop”), so it does not fit a context involving a request or desire for someone else to stop negative behavior.
default.q.n1-27-q42-42.why.1: (b) 「やめてほしいのだ」combines「〜てほしい」(want someone to do or stop something) with「のだ」(emphasizing the reason or feeling), clearly and decisively expressing the wish for someone else to stop.
default.q.n1-27-q42-42.why.2: (c) 「やめるのだろうか」 expresses doubt or concern about another person’s action (“I wonder if they will stop”), and does not convey the speaker’s wish or request.
default.q.n1-27-q42-42.why.3: (d) 「やめられるものではない」 means "cannot possibly give up or stop," denying the possibility of quitting. This is the complete opposite of wanting someone else to stop an action.
default.q.n1-27-q43-43.verdict: The correct answer is 4 (たしかに / bことは間違いない).
default.q.n1-27-q43-43.explanation:
- Meaning: The pattern 「たしかに〜ことは間違いない」uses the adverb「たしかに」(indeed, certainly) together with「〜に間違いない / 〜ことは間違いない」(there is no doubt that..., it is certainly...) to strongly and confidently affirm a fact, cause, or conclusion.
- Connection: たしかに + [plain form (V/A-い/A-な/N+である)] + ことは間違いない
- Additional examples:
  + 「彼のこれまでの実績を見れば、たしかに今回の昇進が妥当であることは間違いない。」(Judging from his achievements so far, there is no doubt that this promotion is well deserved.)
  + 「犯行現場に残された指紋から、たしかに彼がその場にいたことは間違いない。」(Based on the fingerprints left at the crime scene, there is no doubt that he was there.)
default.q.n1-27-q43-43.why.0: (a) 「やはり ... ところだった」combines “as expected” with the structure “almost...,” so it does not form a logical adverb–predicate pair for making a definite statement.
default.q.n1-27-q43-43.why.1: (b) 「いったい ... のか」 is a rhetorical question or challenge (“what on earth...?”), so it does not fit a context asserting an obvious fact.
default.q.n1-27-q43-43.why.2: (c) 「といっても ... わけでもない」 is used for partial negation (“although one says that, it is not necessarily...”), so it is unsuitable for emphasizing a positive affirmation.
default.q.n1-27-q43-43.why.3: (d) 「たしかに ... ことは間違いない」 combines the adverb of acknowledgment 「たしかに」 (“indeed,” “certainly”) with the absolute-affirmation pattern 「〜に間違いない / 〜ことは間違いない」 (“there is no doubt that...”); the combination is completely appropriate.
default.q.n1-27-q44-44.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (見させてしまう).
default.q.n1-27-q44-44.explanation:
- Meaning: The pattern「V-（さ）せてしまう」combines the causative form (make or let someone do something) with「〜てしまう」(expressing an action that occurs unexpectedly, spontaneously, or irresistibly). In media, art, and literature, this pattern often describes a work or event so powerful that it unconsciously draws others into performing action V.
- Connection pattern: V (causative form) + てしまう (Group 1: V-あせてしまう / Group 2: V-させてしまう / Group 3: させてしまう・こさせてしまう)
- Additional examples:
  + 「彼の迫真の演技は、観客に涙を流させてしまうほど感動的だった。」(His realistic performance was so moving that it made the audience shed tears involuntarily.)
  + 「この小説の展開の速さは、読者に夜を徹して一気に読ませてしまう。」(The fast pace of this novel draws readers into reading it straight through the night.)
default.q.n1-27-q44-44.why.0: (a) 「見させてしまう」 uses the causative form (使役形) together with 「〜てしまう」 to express creating an attraction that causes the viewer to become absorbed in watching, unconsciously or naturally.
default.q.n1-27-q44-44.why.1: (b) 「身を乗り出させる」means “make someone lean forward.” Although it expresses causation, it does not fully convey guiding someone to watch the entire content, as 「見させてしまう」does.
default.q.n1-27-q44-44.why.2: (c) 「見られてしまう」 is the passive form (受身形), meaning “end up being seen by someone else.” The action is directed toward the subject and does not express the subject’s active ability to attract or influence.
default.q.n1-27-q44-44.why.3: (d) 「身を乗り出される」is the passive form “to have one’s body lean forward,” which is structurally unusual and semantically inappropriate.
default.q.n1-27-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (ぼく / bみんな).
default.q.n1-27-q45-45.explanation:
- Meaning: In essays and argumentative writing, especially in a narrative style, moving from one's own subjective experience 「ぼく（私）」 to the empathy of the larger group 「みんな（人々）」 is a classic structure used to demonstrate the universality of an observation or phenomenon.
- Expression pattern: [ぼく] はもちろんのこと、[みんな] も〜 / [ぼく] だけでなく、[みんな] が〜
- Another example:
  + 「あの素晴らしい演奏には、ぼくだけでなく会場にいたみんなが心を奪われた。」(That wonderful performance captivated not only me but everyone in the audience.)
  + 「新しいサービスについて、ぼくが感じた疑問は、利用したみんなにとっても共通のものだった。」(The question I had about the new service was also shared by everyone who used it.)
default.q.n1-27-q45-45.why.0: (a) 「ぼく / みんな」 creates a natural relationship from the narrator’s perspective: it begins with a personal feeling (“I”) and expands to the community’s shared reaction (“everyone”), making a reasonable generalization within the passage.
default.q.n1-27-q45-45.why.1: (b) Placing 「広告主 / みんな」 with the advertiser as the subject of the first clause fails to create the same sense of shared direct experience as the narrator’s personal viewpoint.
default.q.n1-27-q45-45.why.2: (c) 「広告主 / ぼくも」combines "advertiser" with "I, too," creating an awkward mismatch between the subject receiving something and the person experiencing it.
default.q.n1-27-q45-45.why.3: (d) 「ぼく / 広告主も」is illogical because the advertiser creates the product, rather than being someone who receives and enjoys the advertisement together with the narrator.
default.q.n1-28-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 1 (失敗を経験しながら課題を見つけ出すカ).
default.q.n1-28-q46-46.explanation:
This passage by Yotaro Hatamura, excerpted from 失敗学のすすめ (Learning from Failure), identifies two essential factors for cultivating and developing creativity in the modern era:
1. The necessity of facing failure: Since creativity means the ability to create something new, it cannot be cultivated by avoiding failure (「創造力とは新しいものをつくりだす力を意味している以上、失敗を避けて培えるものではありません」 -> 失敗を経験しながら).
2. The nature of creativity: The most important first step is not solving a problem assigned by someone else, but setting a new topic or problem oneself (「創造力を身につける上でまず第一に必要なのは、決められた課題に解を出すことではなく、自分で課題を設定する能力です」 -> 課題を見つけ出す力).
Taken together, these points make choice 1 the best answer: "Experiencing failure while finding topics or tasks for oneself."
default.q.n1-28-q46-46.why.0: (a) Correct. The author states that because creativity means creating something new, failure is unavoidable (失敗を経験しながら), and that the essential point is to set a subject oneself rather than solve a predetermined problem (自分で課題を設定する → 課題を見つけ出す). This choice accurately reflects both of the author’s central ideas.
default.q.n1-28-q46-46.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The expression "課題をこなしていく" (completing or dealing with assigned tasks) contradicts the idea that the goal is not "決められた課題に解を出すことではない" (solving predetermined problems). In addition, repeatedly accumulating failures (失敗を重ねる) is not constructive or an active search for new problems.
default.q.n1-28-q46-46.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The phrase 「課題を遂行する力」 means the ability to carry out a predetermined task or assignment, whereas the intended meaning is the ability to set one’s own topic or task (自分で課題を設定する能力).
default.q.n1-28-q46-46.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The phrase「課題を解く力」(the ability to solve assigned problems) is precisely「決められた課題に解を出す」, which the author states is not the central ability required (～ことではなく).
default.q.n1-28-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (アサクラ株式会社の国際課が12月に山中ビルに移転すること).
default.q.n1-28-q47-47.explanation:
This is a reading-comprehension question based on a business notice (ビジネス文書) sent to customers and business partners:
- In the notice, Asakura Company states that, due to business expansion, the entire head office (本社) will move to the Yamanaka Building beginning in January next year (来年1月より本社を移転).
- However, to facilitate urgent business transactions in the meantime, the International Affairs Section (国際課) alone will move ahead of the full relocation and begin operating at the new office in the Yamanaka Building on December 3 (これに先立ち、国際課のみ12月3日より新事務所にて業務を開始いたします).
The notice's immediate and central purpose for business partners is to inform them that the International Affairs Section will relocate in December, so they will have the correct contact information. Therefore, choice 2 is correct.

default.q.n1-28-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 3 (見る雲の形は世代によって違うが、一人一人は雲の形はいつも同じだと思っているため).
default.q.n1-28-q48-48.explanation:
The passage by author Fujisawa Kouji explains the cause of differences or mismatches (すれ違い) in how generations perceive things through the metaphor of “the shape of clouds”:
1. Scientific standards and the values of society are constantly moving and changing very gradually over time, much like the shape of clouds drifting across the sky (見る雲の形は世代によって違う).
2. However, because the changes are so gradual, most people, as they grow up, take the image of the clouds from their youth as the “only standard model” and assume that clouds have always had the same shape (一人一人は雲の形はいつも同じだと思っている).
The actual differences between eras, combined with each person’s assumption that standards never change, lead to mismatches (すれ違い) between generations. Therefore, answer choice 3 is the most accurate.
default.q.n1-28-q48-48.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage emphasizes that the shape of people’s values has actually changed across generations, not that it “does not change in any generation” (どの世代でも変わらない).
default.q.n1-28-q48-48.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The claim that “people of every generation see the image of the cloud in the same way” (どの世代でも同じ) completely contradicts the author’s analysis.
default.q.n1-28-q48-48.why.2: (c) Correct. The author points out that the shape of the cloud (the standards of value) changes over time and across generations, but each person mistakenly believes that the shape of the cloud they once saw is unchanging, leading to differences in perception between generations.
default.q.n1-28-q48-48.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The issue discussed in the passage is awareness of objective standards, not “each person’s preference for the shape of clouds” (一人一人の好きな雲の形).
default.q.n1-28-q49-49.verdict: The correct answer is 2 (示されたデータが偏ったものではないか見抜く力).
default.q.n1-28-q49-49.explanation:
The excerpt from Tamura Shu's work データの罠 discusses data-processing and data-evaluation skills (data literacy) in the media industry:
- Data and statistics always have two sides: a bright side (what is visible and advantageous) and a dark side (what is hidden and limiting). Emphasizing only one side can provoke confrontation and mislead public opinion.
- Therefore, people involved in media and journalism (報道に携わる人間) must not accept figures passively or uncritically. They need strong critical analytical skills to determine whether the data provided is biased, selectively edited, or distorted (示されたデータが偏ったものではないか見抜く力).
Therefore, choice 2 most accurately expresses the quality that media professionals need according to the author.
default.q.n1-28-q49-49.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The author emphasizes the need to recognize and understand the dark or hidden aspects of data (影の部分) for a comprehensive view, not to “remove the dark aspects” (影の部分を取り除く).
default.q.n1-28-q49-49.why.1: (b) Correct. People working in communications need critical analytical skills to determine whether data is biased, one-sided, or manipulated.
default.q.n1-28-q49-49.why.2: (c) Incorrect. Simply “communicating the data unchanged in an easy-to-understand way” is not enough, because if the original data are biased, transmitting them unchanged will inadvertently spread misinformation to the public.
default.q.n1-28-q49-49.why.3: (d) Incorrect. “Selecting data that suits the purpose of the report” is precisely the dangerous, one-sided steering behavior that the author warns against and criticizes.

The passage presents Honda Katsuichi's two conditions for risk-taking: 「命の危険性」 (the danger of losing one's life—counterfeit money) and 「行為の主体性」 (agency in one's actions—counterfeit goods). The author emphasizes that in modern times, when maps no longer contain unexplored geographical spaces, risk-taking is like an artist painting on a blank canvas. What matters most is agency: finding a new subject or direction oneself and pursuing it in one's own unique way.

- 2. What matters is taking on a challenge in a place where pioneers have achieved remarkable feats, with renewed determination.

default.q.n1-28-q50-50.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is the correct answer according to the original passage: When the world no longer contains unexplored regions («地図の空白がなくなった現代»), what matters is for an adventurer, like an artist, to discover a new subject or route and challenge it using a unique method.
default.q.n1-28-q50-50.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect according to the logic of the passage because, in the modern era, “geographical blank spaces” where no one has ever set foot no longer exist («地図の空白がなくなった現代»). Normally, this mechanism remains dormant (“asleep”), but in an emergency the government activates it and assumes direct responsibility for management and operations.

What does the phrase “②体制を制度にして” mean?

### Main point of the reading:
The passage discusses why traditional Japanese architecture often has a short lifespan. The author asserts that the reason is not that wood itself lacks durability—wooden architecture can last for hundreds or even thousands of years if properly maintained.
