default.q.n1-3-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 1: 顧客を限定して、その要望に応えた商品を作るべきだ (The target customers should be narrowed down, and products should be created to meet their needs precisely).
default.q.n1-3-q47-47.explanation: In the passage about business strategy, the author argues that in an era when consumer needs are becoming increasingly segmented and diverse, a business with limited resources cannot satisfy everyone (「万人受け」— appealing to the general public). If it tries to meet every need in a scattered manner, it will quickly disperse its resources and fail to create superior value for anyone. Therefore, the optimal strategy is to clearly define the target-customer boundary—"whom to sell to and whom not to sell to"—and concentrate all business resources on serving that customer group exceptionally well. Therefore, answer choice 1 is the most accurate.
default.q.n1-3-q47-47.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is correct because it accurately expresses the author’s position: clearly identifying and narrowing the target customer segment in order to focus resources and serve it as effectively as possible.
default.q.n1-3-q47-47.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is incorrect because the author discusses how to allocate and optimize the limited business resources currently available, not a proposal to expand or increase those resources.
default.q.n1-3-q47-47.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because this is precisely the view the author rejects. The author argues that trying to satisfy every diverse demand of the masses is impossible and wastes resources.
default.q.n1-3-q47-47.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the author emphasizes “focusing on a specific customer group,” not “focusing exclusively on developing a single product line.”
default.q.n1-3-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 2: 世間の評価や期待を気にしながら生きる必要はない (There is no need to live constantly worrying about society's evaluations or expectations).
default.q.n1-3-q48-48.explanation: The passage analyzes people's psychology in social life: Many people constantly feel pressured and anxious because they care too much about the opinions, judgments, and expectations of those around them. The author points out that, in reality, other people are busy with their own concerns and are not watching or expecting nearly as much from us as we imagine. Therefore, it is completely unnecessary to force ourselves to live according to society's expectations and judgments. Thus, choice 2 accurately reflects the author's message.
default.q.n1-3-q48-48.why.0: (a) Choice 1 is inappropriate because the passage is not mainly discussing how difficult or easy it is to avoid being disliked; it is about freeing oneself psychologically from other people’s gaze.
default.q.n1-3-q48-48.why.1: (b) Choice 2 is correct because it accurately summarizes the author's view: Do not place pressure on yourself because of society's judgments or expectations; let go of that psychological burden.
default.q.n1-3-q48-48.why.2: (c) Choice 3 is incorrect because it contradicts reality and is not something the author advocates; concealing shortcomings only increases anxiety.
default.q.n1-3-q48-48.why.3: (d) Choice 4 is incorrect because the author does not negatively advise people to deliberately expose their flaws and be disliked in order to make life easier. Rather, the author advises them not to fear other people’s opinions excessively.
default.q.n1-4-q45-45.verdict: The correct answer is 1: The more someone seeks information, the more anxious they feel when there is information they do not know.
default.q.n1-4-q45-45.explanation: The final sentence states: 「今、流行っているものの情報に熱心であればあるほど、世間で流行っていることを知らないと自分が遅れるんじゃないか、という焦りみたいなものが人間を突き動かすのが情報化社会の特徴です。」 (A characteristic of the information society is that the more enthusiastically people pursue information about current trends, the more they are driven by anxiety that they may fall behind if they do not know what is popular in society.) The author emphasizes the connection between relentlessly pursuing information and the anxiety caused by fearing that one may miss something. Therefore, choice 1 expresses the content most accurately.
default.q.n1-4-q45-45.why.0: (a) Correct. The passage points out that the more enthusiastically people pursue trending information (熱心であればあるほど), the more they are driven by impatience and anxiety about falling behind if they do not know the latest information (焦りみたいなものが人間を突き動かす). This corresponds exactly to the idea that the more information people seek, the more anxious they become about information they do not know.
default.q.n1-4-q45-45.why.1: (b) Incorrect. The article points out the concern that trends may drive people’s behavior, but it does not say that people who enthusiastically gather information “know only what is currently popular” (世間で流行っていることしか知らない).
default.q.n1-4-q45-45.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The passage says that too much information leaves people confused about what to choose (何を選んだらいいかわからない); it does not claim that failing to choose will cause them to “fall behind society” (世間から遅れてしまう). The fear of falling behind is a subjective feeling of anxiety (焦り), not an inevitable objective consequence.
default.q.n1-4-q45-45.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The author does not make the absolute claim or offer the advice that “simply caring about trend information means one cannot survive in an information society” (情報化社会で生きられない).
default.q.n1-4-q46-46.verdict: The correct answer is 3: Being able to critically and objectively assess one’s own opinions.
default.q.n1-4-q46-46.explanation: The passage analyzes the nature of the act of "writing": When thoughts or abstract ideas (「思ったこと」や「考えたこと」) are transformed into concrete written language (文字という具体的な存在), the writer can directly see and "observe objectively" (客観的に観察する) their own thinking. Through this self-observation, a critical mindset (「批判」のこころ) inevitably emerges, enabling the writer to recognize the immaturity and superficiality of their initial thoughts and reconsider them. Therefore, choice 3 most accurately reflects the author's intention.
default.q.n1-4-q46-46.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The article emphasizes examining and reevaluating preexisting thoughts in order to recognize their immaturity, not “noticing a new way of thinking” (新しい考え方に気づく).
default.q.n1-4-q46-46.why.1: (b) Incorrect. Putting one’s thoughts into words is a means of observing one’s own thinking. The passage does not discuss “communicating one’s opinions concretely to others” (具体的に伝えられる).
default.q.n1-4-q46-46.why.2: (c) Correct. When thoughts are written down, they become external objects that the writer can observe objectively (客観的に観察する), inevitably arousing a critical, self-critical attitude (「批判」のこころを呼び起こす) toward their own opinions.
default.q.n1-4-q46-46.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The article discusses observing thoughts and ideas (「思ったこと」や「考えたこと」), not “observing changes in one's own mood and emotions” (こころの変化を観察する).
default.q.n1-4-q47-47.verdict: The correct answer is 2: Advertising that fails to understand consumers' psychology cannot be considered good advertising.
default.q.n1-4-q47-47.explanation: The passage discusses the relationship between “consumer psychology,” which the author identifies as the essence (本質), and “the way of communicating” (伝え方) in advertising. The author criticizes advertisers for becoming absorbed in superficial novelty of presentation while neglecting to explore customers’ psychology more deeply. The author emphasizes: 「本質なきところに良い伝え方など存在するはずがない」(Where there is no essence, there can be no good way of communicating). Therefore, an advertisement that fails to grasp the essence—consumer psychology—cannot be considered a good advertisement.
default.q.n1-4-q47-47.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The author only states that products are becoming harder to sell, causing advertisers to place greater emphasis on expression; the author does not claim that advertising has become more difficult because it is harder than before to understand consumers' psychology.
default.q.n1-4-q47-47.why.1: (b) Correct. The author regards consumer psychology as the essence (本質) and states that there can be no good way of communicating without understanding that essence (本質なきところに良い伝え方など存在するはずがない). In other words, without understanding consumer psychology, it is impossible to create good advertising.
default.q.n1-4-q47-47.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The author emphasizes the fundamental importance of consumer psychology, but never says that “once consumer psychology is understood, there is no need to focus on presentation” (表現にこだわる必要はない).
default.q.n1-4-q47-47.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The author criticizes the absence of consumers’ psychological essence, rather than arguing that “understanding consumers’ psychology alone is insufficient for effective advertising.”
default.q.n1-4-q48-48.verdict: The correct answer is 2: By recognizing differences in thought between oneself and others, one’s own thinking can be explored more deeply.
default.q.n1-4-q48-48.explanation: The author defines dialogue (対話) as the process of subtly recognizing the differences between oneself and the other person. Beginning with the concern or feeling that “we still do not fully understand each other,” listening to the carefully considered differing views of the other person gives us an opportunity to reexamine and verify our own ideas (自分の考えを再点検する), thereby deepening and developing our thinking (自身の思考を深めていく). Therefore, choice 2 expresses the author’s core idea perfectly.
default.q.n1-4-q48-48.why.0: (a) Incorrect. The passage says that dialogue enables people to perceive differences subtly (繊細に分かる); it does not claim that “the greater the differences, the livelier or more passionate the dialogue” (熱い対話ができる).
default.q.n1-4-q48-48.why.1: (b) Correct. By recognizing differences in how others think and listening to different perspectives, we can reconsider our own views and deepen our thinking (自分の考えを再点検し、自身の思考を深める).
default.q.n1-4-q48-48.why.2: (c) Incorrect. The uneasiness or pain caused by failing to understand each other is only the starting point of dialogue; the goal is not to “overcome the pain and achieve empathy with others” (他人と共感できる).
default.q.n1-4-q48-48.why.3: (d) Incorrect. The article emphasizes listening in order to refine and deepen one’s own thinking, and does not mention “developing expressive ability so that others can understand you more easily” (他人に理解してもらいやすくなる).
default.q.n1-4-q57-57.verdict: The correct answer is 3: Robopie differs in that it incorporates a large number of movement programs and activation rules, making its movements unpredictable.
default.q.n1-4-q57-57.explanation:
Main point: The author made the robot Robopie different from ordinary robots, which respond to sensors in fixed ways, by loading it with more than 300 movement programs and more than 700 rules for randomly and variously triggering them. This made the robot’s movements complex and unpredictable, even to its creator.

Question: What is the difference between Robopie and other robots?
Answer choices:
1. Because its movement patterns are limited, its movements can be predicted to some extent.
2. Because it makes its own judgments about some of the information it receives before moving, its movements cannot be predicted.
3. Because it contains a large number of programs about how to move, its movements cannot be predicted.
4. Because it is programmed with varied and complex movements, it can move naturally like a human.
default.q.n1-4-q57-57.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the passage does not say that the movement patterns are limited in order to make them predictable. On the contrary, the robot is programmed with so many movements that its behavior cannot be predicted.
default.q.n1-4-q57-57.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the robot does not independently judge the information provided; its inability to predict results from the combination of hundreds of installed programs and operating rules.
default.q.n1-4-q57-57.why.2: (c) Correct because the author clearly states that more than 300 movement programs and more than 700 rules for detecting and activating movements were programmed («300以上の動作プログラムをし、動作パターンが次々にどういう順番で発現するかというルールを700以上プログラムした»). As a result, even the robot's creator could not predict its next movement.
default.q.n1-4-q57-57.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the purpose of programming is not to make the robot move naturally like a human («人間のように自然な動きができる»), but to create complex and unpredictable behavior.
default.q.n1-4-q58-58.verdict: The correct answer is 3: The author feels that although Robopie is actually just a program being activated, it moves as if it has a will of its own.
default.q.n1-4-q58-58.explanation:
Main point: When Robopie recognized a voice during the meeting and then began walking in a particular direction, it was actually just a random program that had been activated. However, the behavior seemed so realistic that the author felt as if the robot had a will of its own.

Question translation: When Robopie "began walking in a particular direction," what did the author think?
Answer choices:
1. There was an error in the program, and Robopie had developed a will of its own and begun moving.
2. It was not the program operating; Robopie had thought for itself and begun moving.
3. The program was operating, and Robopie moved as if it had a will of its own.
4. The program malfunctioned, and Robopie moved contrary to the creator's intentions.
default.q.n1-4-q58-58.why.0: (a) Incorrect because there is no programming error («プログラムに間違いがあり») that would cause the robot to develop genuine will.
default.q.n1-4-q58-58.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the program itself is still operating («プログラムが作動した»); this does not mean that the robot thought independently outside its programming.
default.q.n1-4-q58-58.why.2: (c) Correct because Robopie’s walking is actually caused by an activated internal program, but the way it appears makes observers feel as if it were acting according to its own will («意思があるかのように»).
default.q.n1-4-q58-58.why.3: (d) Incorrect because the passage does not mention the program malfunctioning («誤作動») against the inventor’s intentions.
default.q.n1-4-q59-59.verdict: The correct answer is 4: The author argues that the “mind” is something people imagine when observing complex movements or behaviors whose entire mechanism exceeds their ability to understand.
default.q.n1-4-q59-59.explanation:
Main point: The author concludes that the “mind/heart” (心) is not a concrete entity inside a machine or living organism, but something imagined and attributed to an object by an observer who sees behavior or movements so complex that their mechanisms cannot be fully understood.

Translation of the question: What does the author think about the “mind/heart” (心)?
Translation of the answer choices:
1. If we observe something believing that it has a mind, we can understand the intentions behind its complex movements.
2. Since no such entity exists, imagining whether something has a mind is meaningless.
3. Because the mechanisms are too complex, even human beings cannot imagine them in one another.
4. It is something people imagine when they see complex movements whose mechanisms they cannot fully understand.
default.q.n1-4-q59-59.why.0: (a) Incorrect because the author does not say that believing in a mind would help one understand the intentions behind complex movements.
default.q.n1-4-q59-59.why.1: (b) Incorrect because the author presents imagining other people’s minds as a natural psychological mechanism humans use when facing complexity, and does not claim that such imagination is meaningless («意味がない»).
default.q.n1-4-q59-59.why.2: (c) Incorrect because the passage does not mention that even human beings cannot imagine or understand one another's minds («人間同士であっても想像できない»).
default.q.n1-4-q59-59.why.3: (d) Correct, because the author concludes that the “mind” (心) is essentially something an observer imagines when faced with behavior so complex that it cannot be fully understood («理解しきれない複雑な動きを見たときに、人間が想像するものだ»).
default.q.n1-4-q60-60.verdict: The correct answer is choice 3: A argues that taking notes is necessary to make use of the content, whereas B argues that focusing too much on note-taking is meaningless.
default.q.n1-4-q60-60.explanation:
Main points:
- Text A: The author habitually takes notes (a 「メモ魔」). Whether listening to a lecture or having an ordinary conversation, the author makes every effort to record as much as possible in order to absorb the information and make use of that knowledge in future opportunities.
- Text B: The author warns that focusing too intently on writing down every word distracts one from thinking about and understanding the content, making note-taking meaningless if the essence of the discussion is not grasped.

Translation of the question and answer choices:
Question: What did A and B say about taking notes (memoing)?
1. Both A and B believe that being aware of what needs to be recorded is more important than the amount of notes taken.
2. Both A and B believe that as much information as possible should be recorded accurately.
3. A believes that taking notes is necessary in order to make use of the content, whereas B believes that focusing too much on note-taking is meaningless.
4. A believes that one should record both the issues and one's impressions, whereas B believes that notes cannot be taken accurately without understanding the content.
default.q.n1-4-q60-60.why.0: (a) This choice does not fit because Author A describes himself as someone who takes extensive notes (「メモ魔」) and always tries desperately to write everything down while listening (「必死にメモを取りながら話を聞きます」) in order to absorb as much as possible, rather than advocating focusing only on content over quantity.
default.q.n1-4-q60-60.why.1: (b) This choice does not fit because only Author A wants to take copious notes in order to absorb as much information as possible (「最大限吸収して帰ろう」). Author B objects to merely taking numerous, accurate notes without listening in order to understand.
default.q.n1-4-q60-60.why.2: (c) This choice matches the passage precisely: Author A says that taking notes may allow information to be applied and used later (「そこで何を感じたり、新しく知り得たものは、別の機会に自分の役に立つかもしれないからです」), whereas Author B argues that taking notes has no meaning if one focuses too much on writing them and fails to absorb or understand the content (「メモを取ることに集中し過ぎては意味がない」).
default.q.n1-4-q60-60.why.3: (d) This choice does not fit because Passage A never mentions recording both the issue and one's impressions (「問題点や感想なども一緒に記入」). In addition, Author B emphasizes that taking notes without understanding the material is ineffective, not that accurate note-taking is impossible.
default.q.n1-4-q61-61.verdict: The correct answer is choice 1: What A and B have in common is their recognition of the importance of listening with the desire to receive or learn something useful.
default.q.n1-4-q61-61.explanation:
Main point:
Although authors A and B have opposing views on note-taking (A supports actively taking notes to preserve and reuse knowledge, while B warns that excessive note-taking can distract people from listening), they share one fundamental point: the purpose of listening is to adopt an active attitude and try to take away and distill something useful for oneself.

Translation of the question and choices:
Question: What do A and B have in common in their views on how to listen to someone speak?
1. It is important to listen with the intention of gaining something from it.
2. There is no need to try to understand everything on the spot.
3. Taking notes while listening makes it easier to remember.
4. It is important to show interest and concern so that the speaker feels at ease.
default.q.n1-4-q61-61.why.0: (a) This choice matches the content of both passages exactly. Author A shows an attitude of wanting to absorb as much useful information as possible while listening (「せっかくその場にいるのだから、最大限吸収して帰ろう」「自分の役に立つ」). Author B likewise believes that the real purpose of listening is to think actively and take in the value of a talk, rather than merely acting as a passive recording machine.
default.q.n1-4-q61-61.why.1: (b) This choice does not fit because Author A wants to absorb as much as possible on the spot (「最大限吸収して帰ろう」), and Author B also expects listeners to concentrate on understanding the content while listening. Neither says that one need not try to understand everything on the spot.
default.q.n1-4-q61-61.why.2: (c) This choice does not match because only author A has the habit of listening while taking notes (「必死にメモを取りながら話を聞きます」). Author B instead warns that being too busy writing notes can hinder thinking and understanding.
default.q.n1-4-q61-61.why.3: (d) This choice does not match the content because both texts focus solely on how listeners can absorb information as effectively as possible for themselves. They do not mention creating a sense of reassurance for the speaker (「話し手に安心感を与える」).
default.q.n1-5-q7-7.verdict: The correct answer is 1. 保護 (protection of privacy).
default.q.n1-5-q7-7.explanation:
- Meaning: When reporting on victims, a pseudonym is used to protect their privacy.
- Kanji-based terms & vocabulary: 仮名 (かめい: pseudonym, alias), 被害者 (ひがいしゃ: victim), プライバシー (privacy), 保護 (ほご: protection).
- Additional example: 個人情報を適切に保護することが重要だ。(It is important to protect personal information appropriately.)
default.q.n1-5-q7-7.why.0: (a) 保護 (ほご - protection): Correct. Combined with プライバシー, it forms the natural phrase 「プライバシーを保護する」, meaning to protect privacy and secure personal information.
default.q.n1-5-q7-7.why.1: (b) 防御 (ぼうぎょ): Incorrect. It means defense against physical, military, or sports attacks and does not collocate with プライバシー.
default.q.n1-5-q7-7.why.2: (c) 警備 (けいび) is incorrect. It means guarding or providing security for a building or event, as in 警備員, and is not used for private information.
default.q.n1-5-q7-7.why.3: (d) 支援 (しえん): Incorrect. It means material, financial, or emotional support (such as 支援金 or 被災者支援), which does not fit the context.
default.q.n1-5-q8-8.verdict: The correct answer is 3. 忠実に (reproducing something faithfully and accurately according to the original).
default.q.n1-5-q8-8.explanation:
Sentence meaning: This model faithfully reproduces a real building at a scale of 1/20.
- Vocabulary: 模型 (model), 忠実 (faithful, true to the original), 再現 (reproduction, recreation).
- Common expression: 原作を忠実に再現する (to faithfully recreate the original work).
default.q.n1-5-q8-8.why.0: (a) 従順に (じゅうじゅんに): Incorrect. It means obediently or submissively, and is generally used for people's or pets' personalities.
default.q.n1-5-q8-8.why.1: (b) 厳正に (げんせいに): incorrect. It means strict, impartial, and fair, and is used for examinations, judgments, or disciplinary actions, as in 厳正な審査/処分.
default.q.n1-5-q8-8.why.2: (c) 忠実に (ちゅうじつに): Correct. Combined with 再現する, 「忠実に再現する」 means to reproduce or recreate something faithfully and accurately according to the original.
default.q.n1-5-q8-8.why.3: (d) 均等に (きんとうに): Incorrect. It means “equally” or “evenly” in terms of quantity or proportion (均等に分ける), and does not modify 再現する in this context.
default.q.n1-5-q9-9.verdict: The correct answer is 2. すくって (scoop up water with both hands).
default.q.n1-5-q9-9.explanation:
Meaning: The river water was crystal clear and clean, so I scooped up water with both hands to wash my face.
- Vocabulary: 澄む (to be clear, transparent), 掬う (to scoop, ladle, or pick up liquid or small objects with one's hands, a spoon, or a ladle).
- Another example: スプーンでスープをすくって飲む。(Use a spoon to scoop up and drink the soup.)
default.q.n1-5-q9-9.why.0: (a) めくって (めくる): Incorrect. It means to turn over or flip through something, such as a book page, calendar page, or blanket.
default.q.n1-5-q9-9.why.1: (b) すくって (すくう - 掬う): Correct. It means to scoop water or another liquid with cupped hands or a ladle. 両手で水をすくう means “to scoop up water with both hands.”
default.q.n1-5-q9-9.why.2: (c) はさんで (はさむ - 挟む): Incorrect. It means to place or夹 something between two objects (pinching a finger, inserting a bookmark into a book, etc.).
default.q.n1-5-q9-9.why.3: (d) つまんで (つまむ - 摘む): Incorrect. It means to pinch, pick up, or grasp something with one's fingertips or chopsticks (e.g., pinching one's nose: 鼻をつまむ, or picking up food).
default.q.n1-5-q10-10.verdict: The correct answer is 4. 念願 (long-cherished wish, long-held desire).
default.q.n1-5-q10-10.explanation:
Meaning: After working as hard as I could, I finally obtained the home I had long dreamed of owning.
- Vocabulary: 一生懸命 (いっしょうけんめい - with all one’s might, diligently), 念願 (ねんがん - a long-cherished wish), マイホーム (one’s own home).
- Common expressions: 念願のマイホーム (the home one has long dreamed of), 念願がかなう (a long-cherished wish comes true).
default.q.n1-5-q10-10.why.0: (a) 志望 (しぼう): Incorrect. It means the desire to pass an entrance examination or apply to a school or company, as in 志望校 and 志望動機. It is not used as a modifier for マイホーム.
default.q.n1-5-q10-10.why.1: (b) 本意: Incorrect. It means one's true intention or genuine desire (often used in the negative forms 不本意 and 本意ではない, meaning "against one's wishes").
default.q.n1-5-q10-10.why.2: (c) 欲求 (よっきゅう): Incorrect. It means an instinctive or psychological need or desire, as in 欲求不満 and 基本的欲求.
default.q.n1-5-q10-10.why.3: (d) 念願 (ねんがん): Correct. The fixed expression 「念願の～」 refers to a long-held wish or aspiration that has finally been achieved (念願のマイホーム, 念願の優勝).
default.q.n1-5-q11-11.verdict: The correct answer is 3. ピント (focus, camera focus).
default.q.n1-5-q11-11.explanation:
Meaning: To take a good photograph, it is important to focus the camera properly first.
- Katakana vocabulary: ピント (focus, lens sharpness, from the Dutch word “brandpunt”), ピントを合わせる (focus; figuratively, focus on the central point of an issue).
- Figurative example: 彼の意見はピントが外れている。(His opinion misses the point / is off topic.)
default.q.n1-5-q11-11.why.0: (a) ポーズ: Incorrect. It means a pose or posture, commonly used in ポーズをとる (“to pose for a photo”), and does not combine with 合わせる in the context of a camera.
default.q.n1-5-q11-11.why.1: (b) カーソル (cursor): Incorrect. A mouse pointer displayed on a computer screen.
default.q.n1-5-q11-11.why.2: (c) ピント (Pinto / focus): Correct. Combined with 合わせる, it forms 「ピントを合わせる」, meaning to focus or adjust a camera’s focus.
default.q.n1-5-q11-11.why.3: (d) テンポ (tempo): Incorrect. It means the pace of music or the speed and rhythm of how a story or event develops (テンポが速い/良い).
default.q.n1-5-q12-12.verdict: The correct answer is 2. 食い込んだ (breaking into, making it into a high ranking).
default.q.n1-5-q12-12.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: Although it was their first time competing in the national tournament, the team somehow fought through the tough matches and broke into the top ranks.
- Vocabulary: 初出場 (はつしゅつじょう: first appearance), 勝ち抜く (かちぬく: win through the rounds), 食い込む (くいこむ: break into a ranking; extend into; cut into).
- Common expressions: 上位に食い込む (break into the top ranks), ベスト8に食い込む (make it into the top eight), 予定が次の時間に食い込む (the schedule run into the next time slot).
default.q.n1-5-q12-12.why.0: (a) 乗り込んだ (のりこむ): Incorrect. It means boarding a vehicle or entering an opponent’s territory (敵地に乗り込む), and it does not collocate with 上位.
default.q.n1-5-q12-12.why.1: (b) 食い込んだ: Correct. Combined with 上位, 「上位に食い込む」 means making an effort to break into and secure a high position in the rankings.
default.q.n1-5-q12-12.why.2: (c) 駆け込んだ: Incorrect. It means to run hurriedly or rush into somewhere (駆け込み乗車: rushing onto a train at the last moment; 病院に駆け込む: rushing to a hospital).
default.q.n1-5-q12-12.why.3: (d) 追い込んだ (おいこむ): Incorrect. This transitive verb means to corner or drive someone into a difficult situation (窮地に追い込む, 相手を追い込む).
default.q.n1-5-q13-13.verdict: The correct answer is 1. てっきり (I was convinced that..., I mistakenly thought that...).
default.q.n1-5-q13-13.explanation:
Meaning of the sentence: Because the person gave me directions, I assumed they were a local, but it turned out that they were also a tourist.
- Adverb and grammar: てっきり～と思う/思っていた (to assume that..., to be firmly convinced that..., expressing an initial mistaken belief that is contradicted by the truth), 道案内 (みちあんない — giving directions).
- Another example: てっきり彼が犯人だと思っていたが、無実だった。(I was convinced that he was the culprit, but he turned out to be innocent.)
default.q.n1-5-q13-13.why.0: (a) てっきり: Correct. This adverb commonly occurs with 「てっきり～と思ったら / と思っていた」 to express a firm initial assumption that turns out to be completely wrong.
default.q.n1-5-q13-13.why.1: (b) きっぱり: Incorrect. It means decisively or bluntly, as in きっぱり断る (to refuse decisively).
default.q.n1-5-q13-13.why.2: (c) しっかり: Incorrect. It means firmly, reliably, or seriously, as in しっかり勉強する and しっかり持つ (to hold firmly).
default.q.n1-5-q13-13.why.3: (d) はっきり: Incorrect. It means clearly, distinctly, or unambiguously (as in はっきり言う—say clearly, はっきり見える—be clearly visible).
